papers.title: Retrospective Comparison of Radiation Oncology Patient Message Responses Generated by Epic and Institutionally Managed LLMs
papers.summary: We retrospectively compared Epic-generated draft replies with institutionally managed hybrid GPT-4.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro responses to 51 selected single-turn radiation oncology messages. Six clinicians, blinded to response source, rated overall quality on a five-point scale and perceived editing effort on a four-point scale. Mixed-effects models accounted for repeated ratings by message and clinician. Adjusted overall-quality means were 2.95 for Epic, 4.27 for hybrid GPT-4.1, and 4.39 for hybrid Gemini 2.5 Pro. Corresponding editing-effort means were 2.38, 1.46, and 1.41, with lower scores indicating less perceived effort. Both hybrid models received more favorable ratings than Epic for both outcomes (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001), without a statistically significant difference between the hybrid models. These findings support prospective evaluation of clinician-supervised draft generation, though editing time and patient outcomes were not measured, and clinical safety was not established.

papers.title: $\Lambda$-Gravity from Entropy
papers.summary: The Gravity from Entropy (GfE) theory treats the metric of spacetime as quantum operators and proposes the GfE action for gravity. The GfE Lagrangian is given by the Geometric Quantum Relative Entropy (GQRE) between the true metric and the metric induced by the matter fields and curvature. The theory leads to modified gravity equations and predicts the emergence of a dynamical cosmological constant $\Lambda_{\mathcal{G}}$. In the low energy, small curvature limit the GfE gravity equations reduce to Einstein equations with vanishing cosmological constant, i.e. in the weak field linear approximation $\Lambda_{\mathcal{G}}$ vanishes. In this work, we propose a generalisation of the GfE theory, called $\Lambda$-Gravity from Entropy ($\Lambda$GfE). Following a thermodynamic approach, we introduce a Lagrange multiplier $\Lambda$ to define the local volume of the theory. By enforcing local Weyl stationarity of the $\Lambda$GfE action modulo the volume constraint of the theory, we derive the equation for $\Lambda$. The $\Lambda$GfE equations of motion include two dark energy contributions: the emergent and dynamical contribution given by $\Lambda_{\mathcal{G}}$ plus a constant contribution given by $\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ can be identified with the cosmological constant in the low energy small curvature limit. While this theory cannot predict the exact value of $\Lambda$, here it is shown that the vacuum contributions to the dressed stress-energy tensor cancel from the trace-free equations of motion of the $\Lambda$GfE theory. Within the GfE framework, the $\Lambda$GfE also offers a novel interpretation of the dark energy terms, with potentially testable consequences for cosmological observations.

papers.title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
papers.summary: Theoretical modelling of diamond growth should ideally provide estimates of the growth rate depending on experimental conditions. To that end, a description of all possible reactions related to the competing adsorption, desorption and migration mechanisms is required. Here, we provide precise calculations of the reaction rate coefficient of methyl-related reactions on hydrogen-terminated (100) diamond surface, as $\mathrm{CH_3}$ is known to be the main growth precursor in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of diamond. To achieve this goal, we successfully combined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and variational transition state theory (VTST), allowing to extend our analysis to barrierless reaction. Our rigorous treatment of the quasi-free rotation of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ adsorbates on the surface allows us to overcome numerical errors for the finite difference calculations of the vibrational spectra for evaluating the partition functions of the system. Our results suggest that the mechanism that deplete the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ concentration the most is the absorption on a surface radical site. We also evidence the anisotropy of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ migration along the dimer of the (100)-(2x1):H surface. In a more general perspective, the calculated reaction rates coefficient for methyl reactions and migration presented in this work, together with the data for hydrogen reaction and other main gas surface reactions, bridge the gap between the atomic-scale description and the large-scale modelling of diamond growth.

papers.title: High-speed laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina
papers.summary: We demonstrate real-time laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina using a Phantom S980 streaming camera at $3840\times2160$ pixels, 8-bit depth, and 1000 frames per second, with a $988\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ exposure. We report four recordings of the peripapillary retina around the optic disc in the right eye of one healthy 25-year-old emmetropic man, acquired without pharmacological pupil dilation, using 852-nm diffuse Maxwellian illumination at an entering optical power of 5.0 mW. Each recording contained 4096 frames (4.10 s), and all 16384 frames in the reported recordings were retained. Open-source Holoflow software on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 computes $K=\sigma/\mu$ over $5\times5$ spatial pixels and nonoverlapping blocks of 16 frames, producing 62.5 contrast maps/s with 60-frame/s rendering and no additional averaging. The nominal raw-input throughput is 8.29 Gpixel/s. Main retinal arterial and venous branches and smaller peripapillary vessels were visualized. Variations during the cardiac cycle were visible in the principal retinal arteries and veins, as illustrated in the Supplementary Videos. Regional inverse-contrast traces show an arterial dicrotic notch and spontaneous venous pulsation. This single-volunteer demonstration establishes an operating point for high-throughput retinal speckle-contrast visualization. Physiological observations are descriptive; contrast is an instrument-dependent observable rather than a calibrated blood-flow velocity.

papers.title: Competitive exploration in structured environments
papers.summary: Organisms must constantly weigh exploiting the resources they know against exploring for better ones. When foragers compete, the best behavior for each forager also depends on what its competitors do. How does competition change the strategic balance between exploration and exploitation? Here we address this question in a minimal model: two $\epsilon$-greedy temporal-difference learners on a one-dimensional lattice, who start at a small reward at one end and are unaware of a larger reward at the other. For a lone forager, the optimal exploration rate increases monotonically with the value of the distant reward, and with its distance up to a critical distance. When two foragers share the lattice and split rewards, the choice of exploration rate becomes a game whose Nash equilibria have both foragers exploring, both staying, or one exploring while the other stays (anti-coordination). Under local best-response dynamics, pairs of foragers often converge on both exploring or both staying, even when anti-coordination would be socially optimal. This social dilemma arises for a wide range of parameters, and it persists even in a simplified model without explicit spatial structure. A minimal, naturalistic signal, in which one forager informs the other that it has found the distant reward, can remove many of the dilemmas in which both foragers explore, and can produce a Nash equilibrium whose collective payoff exceeds that of every outcome available without signaling.

papers.title: Beam performance and data-constrained optical modeling of a UV-transmitting acrylic Cherenkov counter for hadron identification
papers.summary: A threshold Cherenkov counter based on ultraviolet-transmitting (UVT) acrylic has been developed for hadron identification in the S-2S spectrometer at J-PARC. Three 730 mm $\times$ 100 mm $\times$ 50 mm radiators were beam tested: polished UVT acrylic without WLS, UVT acrylic roughened on the four long surfaces without WLS, and polished UVT acrylic containing 10 ppm by mass bis-MSB as a wavelength shifter (WLS). The polished/WLS prototype gave the largest two-ended photoelectron yield among the tested configurations. At a 1-photoelectron software-SUM threshold, its measured detection efficiency remained above 99% throughout the scanned longitudinal range, with no significant degradation up to an average extracted-particle rate of approximately $2.5\times10^{5}~{\rm s^{-1}}$ during beam delivery. Beam observables constrained a Geant4 optical model with one common detector response scale and no PMT-specific response tuning. The model reproduces the observed response hierarchy and main longitudinal trends. In the central |y| < 200 mm region, simulated and measured MPV estimators for the calibration configurations typically agree within about 15%, while larger deviations occur toward the radiator ends, especially for rough/no-WLS. With the calibrated parameters fixed, the model was used to compare unmeasured detector configurations and quantify the momentum dependence of $K^{+}$/p discrimination. In the central, normal incidence geometry, a 90% $K^{+}$-survival working point is predicted to keep proton survival below 3% up to about 1.8 GeV/c. The measurements and constrained extrapolations support the polished UVT/WLS configuration for S-2S and quantify its expected particle-identification reach beyond the simple threshold regime.

papers.title: From AI-assisted to AI-native Industrial Control: Architecture, Agent Design, and Challenges
papers.summary: The integration of AI and industrial control is rapidly transforming industrial automation. However, current approaches remain predominantly AI-assisted, where AI functions are incorporated as auxiliary components without fundamentally altering the underlying architecture of industrial control systems. Consequently, the potential of AI to enable higher levels of autonomy, adaptability, and continuous evolution remains underutilized. This paper proposes an AI-native industrial control paradigm, which reconceptualizes industrial control systems by positioning AI as the intrinsic core rather than an external enhancement. The proposed paradigm is built upon an AI-native infrastructure and a collection of collaborative agentic AIs, each encapsulating a set of advanced skills. Among them, the industrial control agent plays a central role in orchestrating the system lifecycle. Through this paradigm, industrial control shifts from a closed, capability-oriented, human-driven, and passive engineering process to an open, task-oriented, intent-driven, and autonomous solution delivery mechanism. The paper further analyzes the key challenges of the AI-native paradigm from both AI and industrial control perspectives, including issues related to AI model reliability, formal verification, real-time assurance, and heterogeneous resource orchestration. Overall, this work outlines a forward-looking vision for industrial control in the AI era and identifies critical research directions toward autonomous, evolvable, and adaptive control systems in complex and dynamic industrial environments.

papers.title: Just-in-time volumetric imaging: Learning 2D-3D thoracic motion models during image-guided interventions
papers.summary: Despite two decades of innovation, cutting-edge bronchoscopic techniques still fail to yield clear diagnostic decisions in 30% of cases and miss malignancies in 20% of cases. Intraprocedural 3D imaging drastically improves both tool positioning and diagnostic yield. However, each 3D spin represents a static snapshot of an anatomy that is continuously evolving as the patient is ventilated throughout the procedure. Here, we propose just-in-time volumetric imaging, in which a patient-specific 2D--3D motion model is trained on pre-intervention scans before it is needed and then supplies volumetric images from single fluoroscopic projections during sampling. Given the inspiration-hold CBCT already acquired for navigation and an additional motion-inclusive CBCT, our optimization regime named VoxelMap-DualScan (VM-DS), solves a low-rank motion model by alternating least squares and then amortizes it into a projection encoder trained on synthesized projections with known motion, all within a 10-minute window. On eight held-out cases from the public DIR-Lab 4DCT dataset, VM-DS achieved a mean landmark target registration error of 2.8 mm, a structural similarity index of 0.95 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 37.6 dB. Accuracy was maintained when reducing the number of projections used for training from 227 to 57. Inference takes 1.5 ms per projection, making the framework suitable for real-time use during image-guided interventions. Code will be made available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap/tree/VM-DS

papers.title: Physical Adjoint Learning in Wave Systems with Asymmetric Couplings
papers.summary: Developing self-optimizing physical systems that learn directly from their response to external stimuli offers a promising route toward adaptive and intelligent machines. A key ingredient is the ability to evaluate optimization gradients within the physical hardware, bypassing the need for accurate numerical models. In wave systems, \textit{in-situ} adjoint methods provide this capability by exploiting reciprocity to physically realize the adjoint dynamics. However, this approach generally breaks down in nonreciprocal systems, where the adjoint field cannot be directly accessed through the original device. Here, we develop an \textit{in-situ} adjoint optimization framework that extends physical gradient computation to wave systems with asymmetric couplings through computationally low-cost similarity transformations between the forward and transposed operators. We utilize available degrees of freedom like tailored injected excitations, targeted measurements, and tunable parameters, to enable adjoint field reconstruction through forward experiments on the same physical platform. We demonstrate the versatility of the protocol through broadband transmission and isolation, coherent perfect absorption, programmable wavefront shaping, and spatially selective sensing. Our results provide a route to self-optimization in complex nonreciprocal wave systems through efficient physical gradient-based learning. The number of experiments required by the protocol does not increase with the number of optimization parameters, and the method remains applicable even when parts of the system are completely inaccessible.

papers.title: Electro-optic comb-driven massive data transmission on monolithically integrated lithium niobate photonic circuits
papers.summary: Driven by large AI models, the demand for datacenter interconnects is outstripping traditional scaling laws. This necessitates a transition toward dense multiplexing techniques, such as wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), for datacenter environments, transferring long-haul spectral efficiency to short-reach, high-bandwidth applications. Integrated optical frequency combs offer compact, low-cost light sources for future datacenter WDM interconnects. However, existing Kerr comb and mode-locked laser implementations suffer from drawbacks in power efficiency, spectral flatness and phase noise. Their fixed, device-specific channel spacings often conflict with standard WDM grids, and co-integration with high-speed modulators remains challenging. Here, we overcome these limitations by demonstrating high-capacity data transmission using flat-top electro-optic combs on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a platform featuring flat spectra, tunable wavelengths and comb spacing, alongside native compatibility with (de-)multiplexers and high-speed modulators. Using 46 wavelength channels from two lasers and a 50-GHz on-chip electro-optic comb, we realize 16.56 Tb/s coherent transmission over a 98.84-km deployed fiber link between two universities and two datacenters in Hong Kong, verifying its suitability for inter-datacenter connections. To highlight grid reconfigurability, we reconfigure the comb to 100-GHz spacing via an on-chip demultiplexer and demonstrate 10-channel, 80-GBaud coherent transmission at 6.4 Tb/s. We further report a proof-of-concept monolithic WDM transmitter integrating the comb and high-speed modulator, achieving 19-channel, 45-GBaud IM/DD transmission at 1.71 Tb/s. Our work validates TFLN electro-optic combs as flexible, compact and scalable WDM engines for both coherent and IM/DD datacenter links to satisfy rapidly rising bandwidth requirements.

papers.title: Laser wakefield acceleration and x-ray emission in plasma produced by the electrical explosion of an aluminum wire
papers.summary: Underdense plasmas used in relativistic laser-plasma interactions are conventionally produced from gaseous targets, whereas low-density metallic plasmas remain comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate the interaction of a femtosecond petawatt laser with expanded aluminum plasma using particle-in-cell simulations based on an experimentally motivated exploding-wire density profile. Three-dimensional simulations show that the laser propagates through the low-density metallic plasma, drives a pronounced wake-like structure, accelerates electrons to near-GeV energies, and produces directional broadband x-ray emission. Charge-state-resolved diagnostics further show that electrons associated with higher aluminum ionization stages are disproportionately represented in the energetic population. Complementary two-dimensional simulations indicate that the net electron energy gain is dominated by longitudinal electric-field work and show that relativistic electron generation persists under variations of the assumed initial ionization and density conditions, although the yield remains quantitatively sensitive to the plasma state. These results demonstrate the feasibility of electrically exploded aluminum plasma as a target platform for laser wakefield acceleration and associated x-ray generation.

papers.title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
papers.summary: Fluorescence from fluorophore-polymer overlayers reflects an interplay between molecular photo-physics and thickness dependent optical propagation. Combining spectrally resolved single mole-cule measurements, transition dipole moment orientation analysis and ensemble fluorescence, we show that structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores can exhibit similar red shifted emission profiles under thick polymer overlayers even without additional reflecting surface. This similarity indicates a common optical transfer function imposed by the overlayer rather than a pure-ly fluorophore specific molecular response. Although local molecular interactions, excited state dy-namics and vibronic coupling govern intrinsic emission, the overlayer modifies detected spectra through refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection ge-ometry. Vibronic energy spacing distributions remain largely preserved as thickness changes, whereas spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically. Thus, polymer thickness pri-marily reshapes detected spectrum through optical propagation and outcoupling while retaining vi-brational modes. Time dependent density functional theory identifies candidate Franck-Condon and Herzberg-Teller active dye modes contributing to spectral fluctuations and dipole reorientation.

papers.title: Toward Integrated Microwave Diagnostics for Future Fusion Devices: Design of a Compact Waveguide Diplexer
papers.summary: Microwave diagnostics are essential for plasma control and physics studies in magnetic confinement fusion, providing measurements of electron density, electron temperature, and energetic-particle behavior. However, diagnostic access in future burning-plasma reactors will be severely constrained by breeding blankets, neutron shielding, and compact reactor geometries, requiring reduced blanket opening areas while maintaining diagnostic capability. This work presents a compact waveguide diplexer for front-end integration of multiple microwave diagnostics. The proposed diplexer combines a waveguide T-junction with two iris-coupled sixth-order Chebyshev bandpass filters, enabling microwave reflectometry and electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostics to share a common transmission line while operating in separate frequency bands. As an initial study, the diplexer is designed for the 65-70 GHz reflectometry and 85-90 GHz ECE systems on the J-TEXT tokamak. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate insertion losses below 1 dB and channel isolation exceeding 40 dB across both operating bands. The proposed methodology provides a compact and scalable approach to microwave diagnostic integration and establishes a practical basis for multi-diagnostic front-end systems in future fusion devices.

papers.title: Data-efficient linear hyperspectral imaging through risk-guided co-design
papers.summary: Computational hyperspectral imaging reconstructs spatial-spectral information from limited optical measurements. Linear reconstructors are efficient and interpretable, but often underperform deep nonlinear models, which typically require substantial training data and computational resources. Here we present a theory-guided encoding-reconstruction co-design framework that achieves, to our knowledge, state-of-the-art linear reconstruction performance. We establish a theory for the exact five-term decomposition of reconstruction risk and introduce a method for diagnosing the statistical-coverage lower bound within a fixed principal component analysis envelope, which together inform the optimized design of hyperspectral imaging systems. The framework applies across coded-aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI), diffractive optical element imaging and spectral filter array imaging, achieving 34.76 dB mean PSNR in single-shot CASSI, outperforming a deep baseline by 9.43 dB with only five source scenes, and matching empirical cross-domain risk within 0.2%. Our results establish a data-efficient and theoretically grounded route to high-performance linear hyperspectral reconstruction, while providing a quantitative basis for identifying whether reconstruction is limited by optical encoding, reconstruction design or statistical coverage.

papers.title: State-specific perturbation theory for configuration interaction singles: Theoretical analysis, benchmarks, and improvement with size-intensive level shifts
papers.summary: We recently proposed a state-specific second-order perturbation theory based on the configuration interaction singles (CIS) state, termed CIS(2). Here, we clarify its theoretical connections, assess the accuracy of its excitation energies in greater detail, and develop size-intensive level shifts to improve both accuracy and convergence of its amplitude equations. We first derive the MP2 structure of its working equations and show that our previously introduced Hybrid partition recovers CIS(D) when the ground-state Fock operator is used and the residual Fock action on the CIS reference is neglected. For this partition, an expanded benchmark shows that using the CIS-state Fock operator improves Rydberg and especially charge-transfer accuracy relative to CIS(D), while slightly worsening valence accuracy. We analyze how the hole and particle densities contribute to these changes in excitation energy, which differ among the classes. We then introduce size-intensive level shifts that preserve the ground-state correlation contribution of noninteracting fragments while leaving the ground-state MP2 energy unchanged. With appropriately calibrated parameters, these shifts improve overall accuracy and substantially accelerate convergence without increasing the formal scaling of the amplitude solve. Different optimal parameters for valence and Rydberg states reveal the limitations of a common parameter. The analysis further shows that shifting the contracted-triples block contributes markedly to the excitation-energy correction in addition to accelerating convergence.

papers.title: Non-Maxwellianity in Temperature Relaxation between Plasma Species
papers.summary: Temperature relaxation between plasma species is usually described by Landau--Spitzer (LS) theory, which assumes Maxwellian distributions throughout. We show analytically that, for two Maxwellian species in homogeneous isotropic plasmas, the interspecies collisions driving relaxation generate a universal three-lobe initial distortion and that these distortions initially reduce energy exchange over a broad parameter range. Full Fokker--Planck simulations reveal substantial relaxation delays when interspecies deformation competes with self-thermalization. For post-shock deuterium--tritium plasmas relevant to inertial confinement fusion, with $T_{\mathrm{T}}/T_{\mathrm{D}}=1.5$, the relaxation time exceeds the LS prediction by 47%. The accompanying distortions lower the apparent DD/DT temperature ratio and produce positive DD and negative DT Gamow-shift residuals relative to Maxwellian predictions. These results also motivate examining non-Maxwellianity in fuel heating by fusion $\alpha$ particles.

papers.summary: We propose and numerically study an x-ray source in which a single laser pulse first accelerates electrons while passing through a relativistically transparent thin overdense foil and then, after reflection from a plasma mirror, collides head-on with them. papers.title: Explosive instability, quiet plasma: phase-space cascades, coherent vortices, and transport suppression in a dipole pair plasma
papers.summary: Turbulence in a magnetised dipole pair plasma can transfer electrostatic energy into coherent flows while carrying entropy to small scales. This occurs via a dual cascade in a four-dimensional phase space, whereby advection by the fluctuating electric field nonlinearly phase-mixes the transit-averaged particle motion. Below a critical pressure gradient, zonal bands suppress the kinetic mode, leaving a transport floor. When the fluid mode is unstable, an explosive burst collapses into a zonal condensate on which two vortices "breathe" by reversible energy exchange, without causing net transport.

papers.title: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators
papers.summary: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.

papers.title: Drift wave turbulence and transport analysis of hot ion L-mode plasma with fishbone instability on the HL-3 tokamak
papers.summary: We establish the cross-scale coupling by which a fishbone mode governs both toroidal rotation and drift-wave turbulence in the HL-3 hot ion mode ($T_i \approx 3T_e$, $T_i(0)\approx9.8$\,keV). Combining multi-diagnostic measurements, OMFIT modeling, and TGLF simulations, we show that under 2.5\,MW co-injected NBI a steep fast-ion pressure gradient excites an $m=1,n=1$ fishbone mode. The mode redistributes resonant fast ions outward and decouples the NBI torque, and the sawtooth crash it triggers collapses the rotation from above $100$ to $60$\,krad/s. The same fast ions drive the fishbone and stabilize ion scale ITG/TEM turbulence. Their redistribution lowers the instability threshold and erodes the internal transport barrier. The effective ITG threshold combines a dominant temperature-ratio term, a fast-ion dilution factor, and an $E\times B$ shear term. TGLF scans show the high $T_i/T_e$ ratio suppresses all transport fluxes, synergistically with the fast-ion population. A single macroscopic MHD mode governs both momentum balance and microturbulence stability.

papers.title: On Gill's problem with anomalous diffusion
papers.summary: The classical formulation of Gill's theorem establishing the linear stability of the buoyant flow in a vertical porous channel subject to transverse diffusion and bounded by impermeable walls is here reconsidered from the perspective of anomalous mass diffusion. Anomalous diffusion is a physical effect implying a more general formulation of the governing equations of mass transfer either in a fluid or in a fluid-saturated porous medium. Anomalous diffusion is mathematically modelled via a diffusion equation with a time-dependent mass diffusivity. In this study, the stationary and parallel buoyant flow in a vertical porous layer saturated by a fluid is investigated. The implications of the anomalous diffusion model for the proof that such a flow is always linearly stable are analysed.

papers.title: WRF-JAX v1.1.28: a differentiable regional weather model with fully coupled physics, numerically consistent with WRF and matching 128-process CPU performance on a single GPU
papers.summary: Porting a regional weather model in its entirety to a graphics processing unit (GPU) requires complete implementation of the dynamical core and all physical processes, and improved computational efficiency. This paper introduces WRF-JAX v1.1.28, a JAX reimplementation of the WRF 4.5 dynamical core and the complete CONUS physics suite. We conducted 27 ten-day integrations across nine regions and three initialization months, with a horizontal grid spacing of 3 km and $700\times700$ grid points, and established two numerical-difference baselines. The full-field RMSEs of wind, temperature, and moisture in WRF-JAX and the WRF internal numerical-difference baseline showed similar long-term evolution: the medians of the case-wise RMSE ratios were 1.05-1.07 at 24 h and 1.02-1.04 at 240 h. The mean sustained integration time on a single NVIDIA A800 was 175.0 s per model hour, corresponding to speedups of 1.17 and 1.05 relative to 128-process single-precision WRF runs compiled with gfortran and ifort, respectively. The experiments further backpropagated through 100 steps with full physics coupling, obtaining all three-dimensional gradient components of the initial UVTQ fields in a single calculation. The full-field Gaussian random-direction evaluation used 500 directions and three perturbation amplitudes per variable; the median relative differences in directional derivatives for zonal wind, meridional wind, dry potential temperature, and water vapour were 2.58-5.22%, 2.94-6.49%, 7.86-10.06%, and 3.51-3.91%, respectively. WRF-JAX combines fully coupled forecasting with differentiation across time steps, providing computable approximate gradients for regional weather simulation and end-to-end optimization, with accuracy comparable to that of the original WRF model and a forward integration speed equivalent to that of the original WRF model running on at least 128 cores.

papers.title: Analysis of C-point and V-point Inhomogeneous Vector Beams Stability under Anisotropic Turbulence in Ground-to-Air Transmission
papers.summary: In the present work, we explore the impact of anisotropic turbulence on the propagation characteristics of polarization singular LG and circular Airy vector beams along vertical, oblique, and horizontal transmission configurations. The influence of altitude-dependent turbulence anisotropy on beam evolution is assessed through changes in intensity distribution and degradation of spatial structure. Polarization characteristics of the propagated fields exhibiting C-point and V-point polarization singularities are quantified using the Stokes parameter framework, from which the degree of polarization is derived based on ensemble-averaged electric field correlations. To further interpret polarization dynamics, the corresponding Stokes vectors are mapped onto the higher order Poincar\'e sphere, providing a geometric visualization of turbulence-driven depolarization and polarization state dispersion. Numerical simulations have shown that the anisotropy of turbulence significantly enhances the polarization instability. Horizontal and slant-path propagations suffer stronger depolarization and polarization-state diffusion than vertical propagation. These results demonstrate the importance of vectorial polarization analysis in describing the propagation of a structured beam in real atmospheric environments. Overall, C-point polarization singularities of circular Airy vector beams are found to be the most resistant to turbulence-induced intensity fluctuation and polarization degradation in anisotropic atmospheric conditions.

papers.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
papers.summary: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

papers.title: Theoretical progress on regularized lattice Boltzmann collision models on weakly incompressible and compressible thermal flows
papers.summary: Numerical stability has long constrained the application of lattice Boltzmann methods to high-Reynolds-number and high-Mach-number flows. Improving the stability and accuracy of collision models has therefore remained a major challenge for nearly three decades. Regularized collision models constitute an important class of lattice Boltzmann collision models and have recently undergone substantial theoretical development. They are now widely used for high-Reynolds-number turbulence, high-Mach-number compressible flow and aeroacoustics. This article systematically reviews their development and establishes a unified theoretical framework that clarifies the relationships among the principal formulations. The analysis identifies the underlying principle of the regularized multiple-relaxation collision model: higher-order kinetic moments that cannot be represented by the discrete lattice are rapidly relaxed in a coordinate-independent, self-similar moment space, thereby preventing spurious modes from contaminating the hydrodynamic equations.

papers.title: Transient Supercriticality in Hawkes Processes: Detection, Identifiability, and Apparent Criticality
papers.summary: Self-exciting (Hawkes) models of epidemics, earthquakes, financial markets, and social cascades are usually calibrated with a branching ratio $n$ below one. This is a condition for stationarity, not for existence: a process with $n>1$ grows exponentially but remains finite on any finite horizon. Imposing stationarity is also misleading, because transient supercritical episodes then masquerade as near-criticality. Reconstructing the latent genealogy of events, we show that a single finite record can reveal an excursion into the regime $n(t)>1$, and back, and date its onset and end. Detectability is governed by the excess $n-1$ times the square root of the number of exposed parents. Even when the memory time of the triggering is unknown, the data determine the growth rate of activity during the episode nearly as precisely as when it is known, and hence whether $n$ crossed unity, whereas the value of $n$ requires independent knowledge of the memory time. Letting the data choose between endogenous amplification and external forcing prevents confusing the two. In the 2015 Korean MERS outbreak, our reconstruction shows that transmission by hospital cohorts had collapsed by 28 May, before the incidence peak and two weeks before the instantaneous reproduction number fell below one; in real time, it establishes the collapse a few days earlier than this standard indicator. Our framework separates stationarity, non-explosion, and transient supercritical amplification, and provides a practical route for detecting short-lived endogenous instabilities in self-exciting systems.

papers.title: Multiplex relational event models of self-reported and perceived gossip
papers.summary: Gossiping is a complex social phenomenon that unfolds through multiple types of relations. Among other things, individuals may initiate gossiping about others as a result of believing themselves to be the target of gossip. These two processes, i.e., gossiping and gossip perception, form a dynamic multiplex network, where self-reported and perceived gossip ties coexist and can influence each other over time. We develop a multiplex relational event model to study the joint evolution of these two processes. The proposed model includes endogeneous covariates that capture the influence of events occurring within one layer, as well as events occurring on the other layer, on the rate of self-reported and perceived gossiping. We analyze survey data collected annually from 44 secondary schools in Hungary. We show how a multiplex relational event model, including linear, smooth and random effects, is able to describe the social mechanisms operating within and between self-reported and perceived gossiping and to capture how these two layers influence each other over time.

papers.title: Gold nanorods targeting tumor vasculature: Monte Carlo evaluation of the radioenhancement effects
papers.summary: Gold nanoparticles targeted to tumor vasculature can raise the dose to endothelial cells, and the enhancement depends on their position relative to the vessel wall. Despite growing interest in endothelial radiosensitization, intravascular and immediate perivascular dose enhancement has not been resolved at the level of individual endothelial cells for different nanoparticle locations. Earlier vascular dosimetry scored thin wall layers, analytic endothelial slabs, or tissue-region averages. This study quantifies the dose enhancement ratio (DER) of gold nanorods (AuNRs) in individual endothelial cells and in the perivascular region for three AuNR locations. Track-structure Monte Carlo simulations in TOPAS modeled a 10 um long, 16 um diameter microvessel segmented into six endothelial cells. AuNRs were placed homogeneously in the lumen, on the inner vessel wall (vascular-targeted), or on the outer vessel wall (extravasated) at concentrations of 5 to 50 mg Au/g water within the vessel volume under 50 and 100 kVp X-rays. All DERs were corrected for the lack of charged-particle equilibrium (CPE) inherent to microscale simulations. Inner wall-attached AuNRs produced the highest microvessel-averaged DERs, reaching approximately 3.8 at 50 mg Au/g water and approximately 1.96 at 18 mg Au/g water under 50 kVp. The DER increased linearly with AuNR concentration and was higher at 50 kVp than at 100 kVp. Including AuNRs outside the simulated segment (infinite vessel approximation) increased endothelial DERs by 5 to 10 percent. In the perivascular region, the DER was highest within the first 10 um, where outer wall-attached AuNRs gave the highest values. The results establish a physical dose enhancement basis for endothelial and perivascular cells and can guide the design of vascular-targeted radiosensitization.

papers.title: At last, an explicit singular value decomposition for electrical impedance tomography
papers.summary: We derive a diagonalization of the normal operator of the linearized electrical impedance tomography (EIT) problem on the disk in the case of a radially symmetric Schr\"odinger potential with Dirichlet-to-Neumann data. The normal operator in this case is not compact and the spectrum continuous.

papers.title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
papers.summary: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.

papers.title: Towards Exact Multidimensional Fluxes: A Structure-Preserving Data-Informed Framework for Riemann Solvers
papers.summary: Finite-volume and discontinuous Galerkin methods update cells using the space-time flux integral over their faces, which typically depends on the solutions to local Riemann problems. In the multidimensional Riemann problem setting, this integral is difficult to evaluate exactly because of complex wave interactions. In this work, we show that the exact space-time flux integral is a polynomial in the time step and face dimensions. This motivates a learning-based approach, as only the mapping from the initial states to the polynomial coefficients needs to be learned. We propose a structure-preserving, data-informed Riemann solver framework that uses a neural network trained on high-resolution simulation data to learn this mapping. Key structural properties, including consistency and symmetry, are enforced by construction. Provided that the high-resolution simulations converge to the exact flux integrals and the network accurately predicts the coefficients, this framework yields near-exact flux integrals for use in numerical simulations. We demonstrate the framework using classical implosion and explosion problems for the two-dimensional Euler equations. In an unsplit MUSCL-Hancock scheme, the learned Riemann solver remains stable at a CFL number of 0.9, whereas the same scheme using the exact one-dimensional Riemann solver fails. Compared with the latter scheme at CFL=0.45, the learned scheme is slightly more accurate and requires approximately 30% less computational time.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Symbolic Regression for Mean-Velocity and Mixing-Length Scaling in Zero-Pressure-Gradient Turbulent Boundary Layers
papers.summary: Developing interpretable full-profile relations for mean velocity and effective mixing length remains challenging because the near-wall, overlap, and outer regions exhibit distinct scaling behaviors. In this paper, physics-constrained symbolic regression is used to construct analytical relations for incompressible zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers. Classical logarithmic and Prandtl mixing-length scalings provide the starting points, while the regression identifies near-wall transition functions under asymptotic constraints and Reynolds-number-dependent outer corrections. The resulting expressions retain the prescribed leading-order near-wall exponents, reproduce the principal overlap-region behavior, and describe finite-Reynolds-number variations. The mean-velocity relation agrees well with 35 profiles from direct numerical simulations, large-eddy simulations, and experiments spanning friction Reynolds numbers from 252 to 72,526, while the mixing-length relation captures the principal trends in the simulation-derived data. These results illustrate how physical scaling knowledge can guide symbolic regression toward compact, interpretable analytical descriptions of canonical wall turbulence.

papers.title: Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed beyond electrically small antennas
papers.summary: The reception of electromagnetic signals becomes increasingly challenging at longer wavelengths, as conventional antenna feeds must scale with the operating wavelength, making it difficult to reconcile compactness with high sensitivity. Rydberg atoms enable direct field-to-optical conversion within deeply subwavelength sensing volumes, yet an effective receiving feed that couples incident fields into the atomic interaction volume remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce a Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed (RAFEF) that integrates electromagnetic field capture and enhancement with Rydberg-atomic transduction. We establish a physical model to quantify its receiving capability, Phi, that jointly accounts for sensitivity enhancement, receiving bandwidth and normalized three-dimensional volume, and experimentally obtain Phi_dB = 70.81 dB. Compared with a conventional loop-antenna feed, the RAFEF provides a higher received SNR and overall receiving capability, while its tunable narrowband response enables frequency selectivity directly at the receiving-feed stage. We further demonstrate selective recovery of a target channel from simultaneously incident signals and reception of a 93.5 MHz FM broadcast after approximately 10 km of over-the-air propagation. These results establish the RAFEF as an atomic receiving-feed architecture that exploits localized electric-field transduction to extend Rydberg-atomic reception beyond conventional electrically small antenna feeds.

papers.title: The Intermediate Silicon Tracker Detector for sPHENIX
papers.summary: A new barrel-type silicon detector has been constructed in the central rapidity region of the sPHENIX experiment as part of its charged-particle tracking system. The detector, referred to as the intermediate silicon tracker (INTT), provides single-event timing capability and contributes to charged-particle tracking in combination with the silicon-pixel vertex detector and the time-projection chamber. The INTT consists of two cylindrical barrels with full azimuthal coverage. The inner and outer barrels comprise 24 and 32 silicon strip ladders, respectively. Each ladder consists of four silicon strip sensors, covering the pseudorapidity range $|\eta| < 1.07$ for collision vertices within $\pm~10$ cm along the beam axis, at radial distances between 72 and 103 mm. The INTT has been fully integrated into the sPHENIX data acquisition system, with detector signals processed by eight FELIX servers. Continuous data taking is enabled by a streaming readout mode, in which detector data are accumulated without hardware triggers, while a conventional trigger-based mode is also supported. The detector achieves stable operation, small inactive area, and high efficiency, providing precise timing, tracking, and vertexing performance during the collection of beam-beam collision data.

papers.title: From Stochastic Transport Models to High-Dimensional Bayesian Inference
papers.summary: The Stochastic Transport in Upper Ocean Dynamics project introduced a new paradigm for representing uncertainty in geophysical fluid dynamics through stochastic transport models calibrated from data. This paper provides a synthesis of the principal theoretical and data assimilation developments achieved as part of the project. The central theme of the paper is the transformation of stochastic transport models from a modelling paradigm into a mathematically rigorous framework equipped with analytical, variational, calibration and Bayesian data assimilation methodologies suitable for geophysical fluid dynamics. We describe the development of the theory of stochastic transport equations, including well-posedness, regularity and approximation results, together with their geometric foundations based on stochastic variational principles, rough paths and fractional transport models. We further review methodologies for calibrating stochastic transport structures from observational and high-resolution simulation data, ranging from reduced-order stochastic models to modern generative approaches. Finally, we discuss Bayesian inference and high-dimensional data assimilation techniques developed for stochastic transport models, including particle filter methodologies and machine learning uncertainty quantification. Taken together, these developments establish a coherent framework linking stochastic transport modelling, rigorous analysis, calibration and Bayesian inference, thereby providing a foundation for uncertainty quantification and forecasting in geophysical fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Bistability of ice-shelf cavity circulation and melt under coastal polynya forcing
papers.summary: Antarctic ice shelves play a key role in controlling the mass loss of the Antarctic Ice Sheet. Increasing evidence from regional studies suggests the possibility of abrupt transitions from low to high basal melt regimes under future climate forcing. The computational cost and complexity of these realistic simulations yet limit their ability to systematically investigate the steady-state response of ice shelves to incremental forcing, the reversibility of abrupt transitions and the underlying positive feedback loops. Here, we report a detailed analysis of abrupt regime changes in an ice-shelf cavity with idealized geometry, subject to prescribed temperature and salinity stratifications in the far field and near-ice-front surface salt fluxes representing the impact of sea-ice production in coastal polynyas. We show that a cold regime emerges when the buoyancy loss in the polynya is sufficient to trigger deep convection, while a warm regime develops otherwise. The steady response of the system exhibits hysteresis, characteristic of irreversible transitions, and scaling laws are proposed for both melt rates and transition thresholds. We demonstrate that bistability emerges when a gyre recirculates the meltwater within the ice-shelf front area. The bistable forcing range increases with far-field ocean temperature but decreases with background stratification. We also show that increasing horizontal viscosity limits bistability, which may explain the range of behaviors reported in previous studies.

papers.title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for M{\o}ller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
papers.summary: We reformulate the overlap of wave-function derivatives that defines the atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors (VG-APTs) used to compute vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) rotatory strengths. In place of our earlier determinant-level derivatives, the new approach expresses these tensors as contractions involving molecular-orbital derivative integrals, perturbed and unperturbed one- and two-electron density matrices, and dot products of the perturbed correlated wave-function amplitudes. Following the elegant treatment of the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction by Gauss and co-workers, the formulation holds for any real, normalized CI-like wave function. The two-electron density contribution vanishes exactly, because one perturbation is real (nuclear) and the other imaginary (magnetic field or momentum); this removes multiple terms from our earlier AAT and VG-APT expressions for second-order M\o{}ller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and configuration interaction singles and doubles (CISD). We also present a simplified form of the origin-independent length-gauge [LG(OI)] rotatory strength that avoids the singular-value decomposition of the outer product of the length-gauge APT and VG-APT vectors for each mode, and that clarifies how the LG(OI) and velocity-gauge rotatory strengths are related. Applying the density-based AATs and VG-APTs to ($P$)-hydrogen peroxide, (\textit{S})-methyloxirane, and (\textit{S})-3-chloro-1-butyne, we find that discrepancies among the gauges arise chiefly from basis-set incompleteness in the VG-APT. The charge-sum rule serves as a useful measure of that incompleteness, independent of the correlation method.

papers.title: Performance and optimization of multi-fin oscillatory propulsion
papers.summary: Multi-fin bioinspired propulsion systems have seen a rise in interest recently due to natural occurrence in animal systems and emerging technology. These systems make use of fin-fin interaction to improve swimming performance where the downstream fins use the wake of the upstream fin to their benefit. While 2-fin systems are relatively well understood, it is unclear how performance is impacted as the number of fins grow. Using an immersed boundary method solver, we model the multi-fin systems to analyze performance across several key parameters: spacing between fins, phase offset, freestream velocity, and number of fins per system. We characterize performance via system thrust and propulsive efficiency. We show that a dimensionless phase parameter incorporating inter-fin spacing, oscillation frequency, and freestream velocity approximately collapses the thrust response across different operating conditions, providing a useful predictor of favorable wake-interaction timing. As more fins are added ($>2$), they can further enhance the group thrust and efficiency without modifying the performance of the fins upstream. Through optimization, we found this enhancement to peak with a 3-4 fin system, after which performance diminishes with additional fins due to the growing wake complexity. Optimal conditions led to boosts in thrust or efficiency of 30% and 20%, respectively. From this study, we show that there are performance gains realized in larger fin systems (though with diminishing returns) and optimizing system performance of multi-fin systems can be done sequentially to save computational resources.

papers.title: HarP: a simulation tool for high-order harmonic generation and propagation in gases
papers.summary: Accurately simulating high-order harmonic generation (HHG) for attosecond science requires connecting the microscopic single-atom quantum dynamics and the macroscopic propagation of intense driving laser fields. HarP is an open-source Python code designed to address this multiscale problem. It solves the wave equations for both the driving laser field and the generated harmonics, using precomputed dipole tables for the nonlinear polarization density. This tabulation enables the direct integration of accurate microscopic models while avoiding costly calculations during the propagation. The methodology builds upon the approach of [L'Huillier et al. (1992) PRA 46, 2778] and has already facilitated multiple studies on phase matching, propagation effects and HHG optimization. This paper presents the underlying physical model, its numerical implementation, and comparison against alternative simulation frameworks.

papers.title: Formation of international environmental agreements and payoff allocation
papers.summary: Dealing with climate change requires that all countries engage in costly efforts to reduce their emissions. Reaching this objective has so far been elusive because it is in the best interest of each country to let the others do the effort and benefit itself from a better environment. The presence of negative externalities and strategic behavior have made game theory a natural paradigm to design an international environmental agreement (IEA) that codifies what countries should do. Considering that countries are sovereign and no supranational entity can impose an agreement, a stream of literature adopted a noncooperative mode of play to the formation of an environmental coalition. On the other hand, as joint optimization of all countries' payoff leads to the best outcome, cooperative games approach has also been proposed to share the cost of climate change. Both approaches have their pros and cons.

papers.title: Parameter-Decoupling-Informed Learning for Superresolution: Laboratory Validation and Galaxy Imaging
papers.summary: We present a parameter-decoupling-informed learning model for estimating subwavelength separations of point sources, without requiring prior knowledge of source properties, control over the sources, or continued access to their light signals. The method builds on our parameter-decoupled quantum superresolution estimation theory, which circumvents the need to estimate nuisance parameters such as partial coherence, brightness imbalance, and relative phase. Our convolutional neural network further accommodates practical imperfections, including background noise, photon loss, and centroid and orientation misalignment. We validate the method using synthetic and experimentally generated images, achieving separation-estimation fidelity above $82\%$ for separations as small as approximately $0.075\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is the Gaussian intensity-PSF standard deviation. This corresponds to an illustrative separation of $\sim13.5$ nm when $\sigma=180$ nm, suggesting potential relevance to length scales addressed by advanced active-source microscopy. Applied to archival Hubble images of NGC~4486B, the model yields nuclear separations of 9.3-13.2~pc, consistent with the previously reported value of 12~pc. Comparisons using the same training and testing images demonstrate substantially higher fidelity than conventional direct data-driven learning in the tested cases. The method's robustness to varying source properties and imaging imperfections supports retrospective astrophysical image analysis and motivates applications in live-cell microscopy and quantum metrology where source control or renewed optical measurements are impractical.

papers.title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low-recycling scrape-off layer: A one dimensional gyrokinetic study
papers.summary: A liquid lithium boundary offers a route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless such that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length ($\lambda_n$) estimates presented here can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but need more complete kinetic treatment. We present gyrokinetic simulations, with one configuration-space dimension and two velocity-space dimensions, of low and higher-recycling LTX-$\beta$ SOL conditions using Gkeyll, an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line, self-consistently evolving kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses constrained by experimental midplane measurements. The hotter low-recycling case develops a larger parallel potential variation, and a density response not captured by an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure of the field equations, demonstrating the importance of kinetic electrons and the ambipolar potential in reducing electron end losses. Collisionality scans show that, as ion neoclassical collisionality falls below unity, the ion distribution develops pronounced non-Maxwellian features. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, particularly for low recycling, because ions become mirror-trapped and electron losses are throttled by the ambipolar potential. These results indicate that low-recycling lithium boundaries in LTX-$\beta$ access a regime where mirror trapping and electrostatic confinement fundamentally alter parallel residence times relative to conventional fluid expectations, an effect expected to be more pronounced in larger devices.

papers.title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
papers.summary: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.

papers.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
papers.summary: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

papers.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
papers.summary: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.

papers.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
papers.summary: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

papers.title: Optical Speckle Patterns as Nonlinear Feature Maps for Photonic Machine Learning
papers.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has increased the demand for energy-efficient hardware, and optical computing has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional electronic processors owing to its high parallelism and potentially lower power consumption. In this work, we investigate an optical computing architecture based on an integrated photonic circular multipass cell, focusing on its suitability for machine learning and pattern recognition tasks. The properties of the system are evaluated through measures of nonlinearity and cosine similarity, which characterize the system's information-processing capacity and the dimensionality of the generated feature representations. Numerical results demonstrate that the reservoir mirror reflectance, the size of the encoded figure, and the refractive-index contrast between the reservoir and the encoded figure modify the nonlinearity of the system, as verified via pairwise similarity estimates. These results indicate that the features generated by the circular multipass cell can be tailored by adjusting the system parameters, providing a means to control the reservoir transformation of the input data. The resulting representations were applied to classification tasks involving texture images and thyroid collagen images, achieving classification accuracies ranging from 69% to 93%. These findings suggest that photonic computing systems could provide a basis for more energy-efficient machine-learning hardware.

papers.title: Automatic indexing of wide-band quasi-Laue neutron diffraction patterns of large unit cells
papers.summary: With a continuous spectrum of incident neutron wavelengths, quasi-Laue diffraction records many Bragg reflections from a stationary crystal, each satisfying the diffraction condition at a particular wavelength. Because the wavelength of each reflection is not measured, the crystal orientation must be determined from the scattering directions alone. At the new IMAGINE-X instrument, instant-readout detectors and many short exposures per experiment require this indexing to run automatically, yet for a protein crystal at the full 2-10 Angstrom band a single peak can have approximately $10^4$ candidate reflections, and a random orientation indexes a large fraction of the observed peaks. We describe an algorithm that indexes such patterns for a known unit cell and wavelength band. Differential evolution searches uniformly sampled rotations, matching observed directions to band-limited shells of candidate directions, and each solution is tested against the indexing expected for a random orientation. In a benchmark search, a k-d tree and a persistent pool of 32 worker processes reduce the wall time 270-fold relative to a serial scan of all candidates. The algorithm is first validated on the time-of-flight diffractometer MANDI, where the measured wavelengths give a reference solution by standard indexing. With the wavelengths discarded, every indexed reflection from 93 rare-earth garnet patterns agrees up to harmonic order. The algorithm then reliably indexes the natural mineral mesolite, measured on the original image plate at IMAGINE before the upgrade, and the protein T4 lysozyme, measured on the new IMAGINE-X instrument over the full band.

papers.title: Transverse detuned loading for modulation bandwidth enhancement in VCSELs
papers.summary: Directly modulated vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) are central to short-reach optical interconnects, where modulation bandwidth and power efficiency are critical factors for increasing data transfer capacity. Conventional oxide VCSELs still require power-hungry signal processing to achieve high-speed data transmission above 100 Gb/s. Here we report an experimental implementation of detuned loading in a VCSEL to enhance the modulation bandwidth. The detuned loading is achieved by carrier-induced index variations that reshape an engineered transverse mode so its overlap with spatially selective optical losses decreases with increased carrier density. This produces a negative differential loss reminiscent of that in detuned-loaded DBR lasers lasing on the long-wavelength reflectivity flank. The resulting 850 nm single-mode VCSEL exhibits an enhanced carrier-photon relaxation frequency of 44 GHz, yielding a 3dB electrical modulation bandwidth exceeding 50 GHz. The enhancement persists from 25 {\deg}C to 75 {\deg}C showing the robustness of the mechanism introduced. The same device supports 106.25 Gb/s NRZ transmission without digital signal processing, transmitter pre-emphasis or receiver equalization. These results establish transverse detuned loading as a robust alternative approach for extending the modulation bandwidth of vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers.

papers.title: A low-volume cold-atom microwave clock with an additively manufactured cavity
papers.summary: We present the performance of a compact microwave interrogated atomic clock based on laser cooled $^{87}$$\rm{Rb}$ atoms. The clock utilizes a micro-fabricated grating magneto-optical trap (gMOT) to cool and trap atoms, and an additively manufactured microwave cavity for microwave interrogation. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $370$ at a 1 Hz bandwidth and mid-term instability of $6.7\times10^{-14}$ at an averaging time of $\tau=3 \times 10^{4}$ s. In addition, a low cost mu-metal foil has been implemented on the vacuum chamber to reduce the quadratic Zeeman shift which was previously limiting stability beyond $\tau = 10$ s.

papers.title: Chirpons: elementary local phase oscillations associated with complex zeros
papers.summary: For a complex wave, the local phase variation provides the instantaneous frequency in time, the local wavenumber in space, and the local momentum in quantum mechanics. Here we study this quantity from the complex-zero structure of the analytic continuation of the wave. A single nonreal zero produces a localized Lorentzian phase variation on the real axis, whose position, width, sign, amplitude, and integrated phase are fixed by the zero itself. We call this elementary zero-associated oscillation a chirpon. The representation is exact for finite products and finite Fourier sums, and extends to entire and band-limited functions through canonical factorization. We illustrate the construction with superoscillatory sequences and discrete Fourier sums, showing how local anomalous oscillations can be reconstructed from periodic families of complex zeros. We further show how linear systems transform chirpons through the displacement of their associated complex zeros, and illustrate this dynamics for quadratic dispersive propagation and a resonant harmonic oscillator. This establishes a direct relation between local phase structure and the amplitude and phase response of the transfer function, suggesting a zero-based form of spectroscopy in which system parameters can be inferred from the motion, width, and orientation of chirpons. More broadly, the chirpon description provides a unified framework for instantaneous frequency, local wavenumber, superoscillation, backflow, and other local phase phenomena, while offering a new route for probing linear systems through the dynamics of their complex zeros.

papers.title: Lanthanide Crystal Field Theory in the J-Mixing Regime: $f^n$ Configurations
papers.summary: The low-energy sector of the lanthanide $f^n$ shell is to first approximation governed by the interplay of three interactions: Coulomb repulsion, spin-same-orbit coupling and the ligand crystal field potential. To rationalize the energy landscape in different chemical environments, it is desirable to extract the phenomenological crystal field parameters from experimental data; however, in practice, high-dimensional fitting procedures complicate their routine determination. Here, we present a computational extraction procedure based on real tensorial sets and the $U(7)$ canonical chain that, unlike existing operator equivalent methods, takes all $J$ multiplets of the lowest-energy $LS$ term into account, ensuring meaningful results even in the presence of considerable $J$-mixing. Two series of lanthanide compounds, [Ln(III)(C$_8$H$_8$)$_2$]$^-$} and doped Ln(III):Y$_2$O$_3$} (Ln $\in$ {Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu}) serve as examples for high- ($D_{8h}$) and low-symmetry ($C_2$) scenarios. Consequences for the generalisation toward actinides are briefly discussed.

papers.title: Relativistic Space-Charge-Limited Current in Electrostatic Limit for a Finite-Width Diode with Arbitrary Injection Energy
papers.summary: We develop a weakly relativistic and electrostatic formulation of space-charge-limited current (SCLC) with arbitrary injection energy, covering the accelerating-diode and drift-space regimes. The one-dimensional (1D) relativistic SCLC model is obtained from a stationary-current condition, which is validated against the numerical solutions. Based on this relativistic 1D SCLC model, we investigate two different approaches to account for the effects of finite emission area for a two-dimensional (2D) planar diode of a finite width of $W$, which is larger than the gap spacing $D$. The field-balance (FB) approach evaluates the opposing space-charge fields at the potential minimum, whereas the density-weighted (DW) approach uses the mean absolute distance of electrons from that minimum. The two approaches yield different corrections at finite injection energy, even in the non-relativistic limit, with FB model predicting a larger leading-order enhancement. DW model reproduces our previously published classical coefficient and the classical drift-space limit, whereas the FB model gives a different result. Note both approaches are identical for zero injection velocity. Comparisons with 2D electrostatic particle-in-cell (ES-PIC) simulations, it is found that FB and DW model show better agreement for higher injection energy (= gap voltage) at smaller and larger $W/D$ emission area respectively.
