papers.title: Multiphase Gas Structure in JWST Little Red Dots
papers.summary: JWST has uncovered a population of compact high-redshift galaxies, 'little red dots' (LRDs), exhibiting broad Balmer emission lines that often show narrow absorption features and strong Balmer breaks - spectral signatures attributed to dense gas surrounding rapidly growing black holes, but whose small-scale structure remains unknown. A striking feature of LRD spectra is that the H$\beta$ absorption is systematically deeper than H$\alpha$, yet in any homogeneous gas this ordering is physically impossible. Here we model the H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ line profiles using radiative transfer simulations for 11 LRDs with JWST sensitive high resolution spectroscopy, and independently constrain the $n=2$ hydrogen column density, $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$, from the Balmer-break continuum. We find that the $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$ from H$\alpha$ in a homogeneous medium cannot reproduce the observed H$\beta$ absorption in several objects, and that this $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$ typically falls two orders of magnitude below the lower bound set by the Balmer break. Both tensions are simultaneously resolved by a multiphase medium of dense clumps within diffuse hot ionized gas. This multiphase gas structure is a necessary ingredient for any viable LRD model, regardless of the nature of the central engine.

papers.title: Partial Fragmentation of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS)
papers.summary: We present time-series observations of the long period comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) obtained in 2025-2026, bracketing the comet's fragmentation in early November 2025. We show that a simple radiation pressure model can explain many of the comet's properties: the rapid fading after fragmentation, the increasing mean particle size in the projected photometry aperture, and the time dependence of the surface brightness profile. Small dust particles ($\lesssim 100 \mu$m) dominate the coma, with average dust velocity $\sim$ a few $\times$ 1 meter s$^{-1}$. The nucleus radius is estimated at $\sim$0.5 km and the dust properties are consistent with, but do not prove, an origin in nucleus rotational breakup, followed by being swept down the tail by radiation pressure.

papers.title: O VI Emission in Starbursting BCGs: An HST-COS Extension of "Reigniting the FUSE"
papers.summary: In this extension of our "Reigniting the FUSE" series, we have obtained new far-ultraviolet spectroscopy of 3 starbursting brightest cluster galaxies with the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) aboard HST. With these new data, in combination with archival COS data of 2 additional systems, we measure star formation rates (SFRs) from the young stellar continuum and cooling rates through $10^{5.5}$ K gas with the O VI $1032,1038\,\mathring{\rm A}$ doublet ($\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI}$). We use these measurements to increase the size of the "Reigniting the FUSE" sample, which itself contains high resolution far UV spectroscopy for 29 nearby massive elliptical galaxies from FUSE, and extend it 1 dex upwards in SFR and cooling rate. Our derived SFRs agree well with photometric GALEX$+$WISE SFRs from the literature. The new data also reinforce the previously observed trend in cooling efficiency ($\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI}/\dot{M}_{\rm max}$; where $\dot{M}_{\rm max}$ is the X-ray luminosity-based cooling rate) versus mass, with groups cooling more efficiently than clusters by a factor of $\sim$4-5. When we isolate a sample of the most star-forming central galaxies, we find that the star formation rates, X-ray spectroscopic cooling rates, and UV spectroscopic cooling rates are all consistent with one another, on average, while retaining substantial system-to-system scatter, reflecting time-depenent multiphase condensation and cold gas reservoir evolution. The remainder of the sample, in contrast, overwhelmingly shows ratios of ${\rm SFR}/\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI} \sim {\rm SFR}/\dot{M}_{\rm X,spec} \sim 10\%$.

papers.title: Reproducibility, Methodological Robustness, and Synthetic-Domain Selection Properties of AFINO for TESS Stellar-Flare QPP Analysis
papers.summary: Quasi-periodic pulsation (QPP) searches in stellar flares depend on methodological choices that can affect both classification and the interpretation of recovered periods. A defensible assessment therefore requires explicit separation of reproducibility, robustness, and known-truth performance. We characterize the reproducibility, methodological robustness, numerical behavior, and synthetic-ground-truth selection properties of a frozen public AFINO implementation in the TESS context while keeping observational reference evidence separate from known synthetic truth. The frozen baseline reproduced five published TESS detections in the initial reproduction cohort. A ten-event observational pilot and a catalogue-scale robustness experiment then tested prospectively specified temporal-window and processing perturbations. At catalogue scale, 51 of 61 published-QPP references did not reproduce their frozen reference state under the F3A baseline, so robustness claims were conditioned on baseline-concordant references rather than interpreted as accuracy. In a separately developed synthetic programme, the untouched AFINO 0.5 rule was evaluated once on an independent HELDOUT set: 152 of 1800 synthetic positives were selected and no false selections were observed among 1800 synthetic nulls, with finite Wilson uncertainty. The resulting 156-stratum selection surface and period-recovery summaries remain conditional on the frozen synthetic domain and, for period recovery, on selection; they therefore provide a bounded characterization of methodological robustness and synthetic-domain selection behavior without establishing observational validation or a population-level correction.

papers.title: ODIN: Comparison of Source Extractor and Tractor Source Detection for Lyman Alpha Emitting Galaxy Selection at z=3.1
papers.summary: Lyman Alpha Emitting galaxies (LAEs) are young, actively star-forming galaxies identified by their strong Lyman-alpha emission at a rest-frame wavelength of 121.6 nm, making them valuable tracers of galaxy evolution and the large-scale structure of the Universe. The One-hundred-deg^2 DECam Imaging in narrow-bands (ODIN) survey collects LAE samples during Cosmic Noon. Because LAE selection is based on photometric measurements derived from source-detection algorithms, the choice of detection method can directly affect the resulting LAE samples. We therefore compare two prominent source detection methods, Source Extractor (SE) and Tractor (Tr), to determine which is better suited for LAE selection in ODIN. We investigate differences between SE and Tr in the ODIN-COSMOS field, focusing on the z=3.1 LAE sample. We find that a significant fraction of Tr LAEs have low continuum flux measurements, increasing the inferred narrow-band excess and resulting in an LAE sample nearly twice as large as SE. However, LAEs detected by Tr but not SE exhibit equivalent width estimates indicative of potential contamination. We introduce an additional LAE selection criterion based on the expected Lyman-break behavior of LAEs at z~3 to reduce low-redshift contamination without requiring a significant detection of the break itself. Our results demonstrate that differences in source detection can significantly affect narrow-band LAE selection and motivate the use of SE photometry for ODIN LAE catalogs.

papers.title: Radio view of the Peanut cluster: merger-induced stripping and a radio halo shortly after pericentric passage
papers.summary: The Peanut galaxy cluster (SRGe CL0238.3+2005) offers a rare opportunity to investigate thermal and nonthermal processes only $\sim0.1$\,Gyr after pericentric passage. We present a multi-frequency radio study of this system at $z=0.42$ using new MeerKAT and uGMRT observations, complemented by Chandra and MUSTANG-2 data. We identify two morphologically and spectrally distinct radio components: a double-lobed source in the northern subcluster and extended diffuse emission across the cluster center. The double-lobed source has a strongly curved, ultra-steep spectrum and is offset by $\sim22$\,kpc from the nearest brightest cluster galaxy. Its spectral curvature and positional offset are consistent with remnant AGN plasma that may have been displaced during the merger or reshaped by a shock. The diffuse emission extends over $\sim1$~Mpc and is classified as an ultra-steep spectrum ($\alpha=-1.77\pm0.11$ between 400\,MHz and 1.28\,GHz) radio halo. Its volume-averaged radio emissivity, $(1.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-3}$ Hz$^{-1}$ at 1.4\,GHz, is an order of magnitude higher than the characteristic value for other halos. The radial profile of the halo is well described by a single exponential fit and its radio emission correlates tightly with the X-ray, with a best-fit slope of $1.11\pm0.05$. Chandra and MUSTANG-2 observations reveal candidate surface brightness discontinuities, with the most prominent inner feature coinciding with a region of flatter spectral index, potentially tracing localized particle (re)-acceleration. The coexistence of an extended ultra-steep spectrum radio halo, high radio emissivity, remnant AGN plasma, and candidate X-ray/SZ discontinuities makes the Peanut cluster an important test case for understanding the evolution of diffuse radio emission and its connection to the dynamical state of the intracluster medium in early-stage mergers.

papers.title: Machine Learning Applications in the Solar Interior and Atmosphere
papers.summary: The solar interior and atmosphere constitute a strongly coupled, multiscale dynamical system defined by continuous temporal evolution. Predicting the state of this system requires modeling physical interactions that span disparate spatial and temporal scales, constrained by heterogeneous and sparse data. This chapter formalizes the Sun within the mathematical framework of dynamical systems theory, defining a global state vector ($\vec{S}$) governed by thermodynamical, kinetic, and magnetic properties. Because solar observations represent projected, multi-modal, and partially observable measurements ($\vec{O}[\vec{S}]$) of this hidden state, pure physics-based deduction is fundamentally constrained. We present a unifying thesis: the primary role of machine learning in heliophysics is to act as a structured family of mathematical operators---specifically Inference ($\mathcal{I}$), Emulation ($\mathcal{E}$), Propagation ($\mathcal{P}$), and Control ($\mathcal{C}$)---that reconstruct, simulate, and couple this global state vector across disparate physical layers. By framing the vast, multi-disciplinary literature within this unified state-space taxonomy, we demonstrate how data-driven techniques bridge observational gaps to resolve hidden multiscale couplings and dramatically accelerate the simulation of non-linear processes, establishing a rigorous pathway to predict the global evolution of the Sun.

papers.title: Binary Progenitors of Electron-capture Supernovae
papers.summary: Electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) arise from a narrow progenitor parameter space between oxygen-neon white dwarf formation and iron-core collapse supernovae, governed by the competition between core growth and envelope removal. Binary interactions modify this balance through mass transfer and mergers. Using the binary population synthesis framework POSYDON, we model ECSN progenitors across metallicities from $Z/Z_\odot=2$ to $10^{-4}$, focusing on the initial parameter space, pre-supernova stripping, envelope-based classification, surviving companions, post-supernova orbits, and cosmic event rates. The lower edge of the binary ECSN initial primary mass lies near $7\,M_\odot$, owing to efficient convective overshooting in the POSYDON grids, whereas the upper edge increases with metallicity because stronger line-driven winds require larger initial masses to build carbon-oxygen cores within the ECSN range. Stable mass transfer and mergers occupy distinct regions in initial mass ratio and orbital period space. ECSNe in bound binaries are divided into hydrogen-rich Type II ($\sim30\%$), IIb ($\sim10\%$), and Ib ($\sim60\%$) outcomes according to residual hydrogen and helium envelopes. Across all channels, approximately one-third of ECSNe have a bound companion at explosion; the remaining two-thirds do not. Among these bound systems, approximately $90\%$ of the companions are main-sequence stars at explosion. These companions exhibit a bimodal spin distribution, including a rapidly rotating component associated with prior mass transfer. Evolved-star and compact-object companions each account for only a few percent. Combining the formation efficiencies with cosmic star formation and metallicity evolution models yields an intrinsic ECSN rate peaking at $z\sim2-3$ and declining at higher redshifts. Over cosmic history, ECSNe contribute approximately $1\%-4\%$ of all core-collapse supernovae.

papers.title: Gaia DR3 Compact Binary Candidates Constrained by Radial Velocity Measurements
papers.summary: Astrometry enables the most direct determination of the orbital elements and component masses of compact binaries. The potential of the current Gaia data for this purpose has not yet been fully explored. In this work, we combine Gaia astrometric and radial velocity (RV) measurements to perform joint orbital fitting for 1,835 Gaia astrometric binaries with available RV data. Among the 518 systems with at least three effective RV epochs, we identify 171 compact binary candidates, including four with inferred dark companion masses exceeding 2.1 $M_{\odot}$ and 22 between 1.4 and 2.1 $M_{\odot}$. These candidates provide valuable targets for future follow-up observations and Gaia DR4 analyses. We also flag 1,317 additional potential compact binary candidates with effective RV epochs less than three, including 84 with inferred companion masses above 2.1 $M_{\odot}$ and 173 between 1.4 and 2.1 $M_{\odot}$. More importantly, our results point to a large, currently hidden population of black hole and neutron star binaries that can be further explored with the forthcoming Gaia DR4 data and complementary follow-up observations.

papers.title: Data-driven acquisition offset correction for telescope networks using machine learning and sensitivity analysis
papers.summary: Reliable target acquisition is essential for maximizing observing efficiency, particularly for robotic telescope networks that operate across many sites, instruments, and environmental conditions. Although these facilities generate large volumes of operational and observational data, acquisition procedures often continue to rely on static pointing models and manual adjustments by observatory staff. These approaches can be effective, but they may not fully capture changing behavior associated with telescope configuration, observing conditions, instrument state, or other time-dependent effects. We present a data-driven machine-learning pipeline for automatically predicting and correcting telescope acquisition offsets, demonstrated using archival operational logs from the Las Cumbres Observatory network. Our approach applies both traditional machine-learning methods and deep-learning regression models to learn relationships between measured acquisition offsets and a range of observing, telescope, and instrumentation conditions. By using historical performance data, the pipeline is designed to complement existing pointing models and reduce the need for repeated manual correction. We also present an open-source, Dockerized software service that makes the trained models accessible through a browser-based graphical interface. The service is intended to support straightforward, real-time use by observatory staff while remaining portable across computing environments. Together, the prediction pipeline and deployment framework provide a practical path toward more adaptive, automated, and data-informed telescope acquisition.

papers.title: The anomalously large transiting planet around Boyajian's star: evidence for a circumplanetary ring
papers.summary: A recent study reported a transiting giant-planet candidate with a mass of $9.4^{+4.9}_{-4.1}\,M_{\rm J}$ and a radius of $1.7\pm0.1\,R_{\rm J}$ on a wide orbit around Boyajian's star (KIC 8462852, also called Tabby's star), which is well known for its irregular, deep flux dips. The reported radius is puzzling, because cool giant planets of $\sim$10\,$M_{\rm Jup}$ are expected to have radii close to Jupiter's, so the companion appears $\sim$60--70\% larger than standard models allow. Here we explore the solution that the planet is actually ringed. We develop a fast and accurate code to compute the transit light curve due to a ringed planet, and apply it to the TESS light curve. The ring model is marginally favoured by the data by $\Delta \chi^2>10$ and a difference in Bayesian information criterion (BIC) of $<2$. The preferred configuration is a Jupiter-sized ($1.1\,R_{\rm J}$) planet surrounded by an opaque, highly flattened ring extending to $3.1$--$4.4$ planetary radii with a nearly polar obliquity. While the ring geometry is uncertain, simple estimates suggest that a debris annulus extending out to the planet's Roche limit is needed to explain the large transit depth. The ring thus removes the radius anomaly altogether and is qualitatively consistent with the dusty, comet-shepherding environment inferred from the star's historic dimmings.

papers.title: EP251129a: A Fast X-ray Transient with Two X-Ray Plateaus and Its Off-axis Afterglow
papers.summary: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) detected by the Einstein Probe are extending the parameter space of relativistic stellar explosions toward softer and longer-lived transients. Here we report EP251129a/GRB 251129A at z=0.505, which exhibits two X-ray plateaus: an early plateau lasting $\sim 10^{4}\,\rm s$ followed by a rapid decay with spectral softening, and a second plateau extending to 60 days, placing it at the extreme long-duration end of Gamma Ray Burst (GRB) plateaus. The early optical emission evolves independently of the X-ray, indicating a different origin; whereas the unusual radio afterglow shows a rapid rise of $F_\nu\propto t^{1.9-2.5}$ and a delayed peak at $\sim36-40$ days, providing strong evidence for an off-axis geometry. We find that the early X-ray behavior resembles those of ultra-long GRBs (ULGRBs) and can be naturally explained by the internal dissipation from a newborn millisecond magnetar undergoing gravitational-wave-dominated spin-down before collapsing into a black hole. The early optical, radio and late X-ray emission are well described by an off-axis two-component jet afterglow with additional energy injection, possibly powered by fallback accretion onto black hole. EP251129a therefore connects the emerging EFXT population with ULGRB-like central-engine activity and off-axis afterglow, offering a rare opportunity to probe both the evolution of central engine and jet structure in a single event.

papers.title: A frequency-resolved measurement of the scattering law in FRB 20210415C
papers.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) show diverse temporal morphologies, shaped both by their intrinsic emission and by propagation effects such as residual dispersion and multipath scattering. Because several of these effects can broaden a burst asymmetrically, an asymmetric profile does not by itself establish multipath scattering. We measure the frequency dependence of the temporal tail in FRB 20210415C, a bright burst from the repeating source FRB 20210219C. The burst is detected across approximately 400-800 MHz. Frequency-resolved fits yield an empirical exponential-tail timescale, $\tau_{\rm emp}$, that follows $\tau_{\rm emp}\propto\nu^{\alpha}$. Two complementary treatments of the underlying pulse width give $\alpha=-3.95\pm0.07$ and $-4.14\pm0.08$. Both results are consistent with the commonly adopted $\nu^{-4}$ scattering law. The inferred scattering time is approximately 8.0 ms at 583 MHz, exceeding Galactic foreground estimates by a factor of at least $4\times10^{2}$. This favours a dominant contribution beyond the Milky Way, although the data do not localise the scattering screen. FRB 20210415C therefore provides a direct measurement of a scattering law commonly imposed in catalogue analyses.

papers.title: Power spectrum of longitudinal-velocity residuals in the Galactic disk from Gaia DR3 red-giant-branch stars
papers.summary: Non-axisymmetric structures in the Galaxy produce coherent stellar motions in the Galactic disk. These motions are usually interpreted by assuming parameterized gravitational potentials or specific perturbation models, thereby entangling direct kinematic information with model-dependent assumptions. Using Gaia DR3 astrometry, we analyze the Galactic longitudinal-velocity residuals of nearly four million red-giant-branch stars over $-4 < X_h < 4\, \mathrm{kpc}$ and $-6 < Y_h < 6\, \mathrm{kpc}$ in the heliocentric region. We construct an empirical axisymmetric baseline without introducing any dynamical model, and compute the power spectrum of the residual velocity field. The spectrum exhibits a broad peak at spatial frequency of $f \simeq 0.12 - 0.22\, \mathrm{kpc}^{-1}$, corresponding to a scale of around $5-8\, \mathrm{kpc}$. The residual amplitude is sensitive to the adopted distance scale: inverse-parallax distances $d_\varpi$ yield a peak of around $16\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$, while the Bailer-Jones geometric distances $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$ yield around $12\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$. Minimizing the low-frequency power favors a solar radial motion of $U_\odot=10.8\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $d_\varpi$ and $U_\odot=10.4\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$. Collectively, the resulting spectrum establishes Gaia astrometry as a direct probe of disk-wide non-axisymmetric kinematics and provides quantitative targets for future dynamical modeling and interpretation.

papers.title: How Quickly Did the Giants Form? Constraining the Formation Timescales of Massive Quiescent Galaxies at Cosmic Noon Using Chemical Evolution Modelling
papers.summary: Massive quiescent galaxies (MQGs; $M_\star \sim 10^{11} \, \mathrm{M_\odot}$) at cosmic noon ($z \sim 2$) host $\alpha$-enhanced stellar populations ($\mathrm{[Mg/Fe]} \sim 0.4 - 0.5$) at near-solar [Fe/H], implying rapid formation histories that spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting alone constrains poorly. To determine the physical conditions and formation timescales that generate these abundances, we employ a one-zone chemical evolution model with nucleosynthetic yields calibrated against resolved stars in the Sculptor dwarf spheroidal. Comparing our model to a compilation of observed abundances, we find MQGs are consistent with rapid formation timescales of $\Delta t_\mathrm{SF} \sim 0.1 - 0.4 \, \mathrm{Gyr}$. The progenitors must sustain high star-formation efficiencies (approximately the molecular gas depletion time; $\tau_\star \sim 0.05 \, \mathrm{Gyr}$) and retain most of their metal-enriched ejecta ($\eta \sim 0$), consistent with high-redshift dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs). However, our model favours moderately active progenitors with typical star-formation rates (SFRs) of $200-400 \, \mathrm{M_\odot \, yr^{-1}}$, matching recently identified `NIRCam-dark' galaxies more closely than the broader DSFG population. Sustained starbursts ($\mathrm{SFR} \gtrsim 1000 \, \mathrm{M_\odot \, yr}^{-1}$) are disfavoured, since they would form most stellar mass before significant SN Ia enrichment and underproduce the observed [Fe/H]. The same framework also reproduces the central abundances of local early-type galaxies over longer timescales ($\Delta t_\mathrm{SF} \sim 0.6 - 1 \, \mathrm{Gyr}$). Chemical abundances can therefore provide powerful constraints on the formation histories of MQGs, and incorporating them into SED-fitting routines will ensure inferred histories remain consistent with the observed chemistry.

papers.title: UV-driven organic precursor formation and dust evolution outside the snow line
papers.summary: In the outer regions of protoplanetary disks, dust grains are often mantled with a layer of ice containing simple molecules. The irradiation of the disk by far-ultraviolet (FUV) photons breaks such molecules, producing photoproducts (radicals, ions, and intermediary molecules) in the ice layer that can act as precursors to complex organics. As grains drift towards the warmer, inner region of the disk, their consequent sublimation of ices causes organic synthesis on their surfaces, potentially enhancing grain sticking and dust growth. In addition to interstellar medium radiation, FUV emission from the central star and nearby massive stars can contribute to photoproduct formation. We perform a vertical dust size evolution simulation including grain growth and fragmentation, and calculate photoproduct formation under irradiation from these three sources, treating the central star's FUV continuum and Lyman-$\alpha$ emission separately. We find that enhanced UV irradiation, particularly from stellar Lyman-$\alpha$ emission, significantly increases the total abundance of photoproducts formed. This results from both the strong stellar Lyman-$\alpha$ flux and resonant scattering by the overlying hydrogen layer, which redistributes photons and directs a fraction toward the dust layer. Turbulent mixing and fragmentation cycles further redistribute grains vertically, allowing photoproducts to form throughout the disk. We find that stellar Lyman-$\alpha$ irradiation can produce sufficient photoproducts to produce an organic mantle with an {organic-to-rock ratio of $\approx 10\%$}, which could enhance grain sticking. Our results suggest that FUV-driven organic synthesis may facilitate dust growth and contribute to overcoming barriers to planetesimal formation.

papers.title: Multiplicity of Massive stars in the Milky Way (M3W). II. The brightest single O stars: variability and systemic velocities
papers.summary: (ABRIDGED) M3W studies the dynamical properties of massive stars in the solar vicinity, such as their systemic velocities, which are affected by variability effects: pulsations, line infilling by wind and disks, and incomplete knowledge about the central wavelengths. We want to increase the accuracy of the O-stars systemic velocities. We establish how different wavelength regions are affected by variability, determine the thresholds for the detection of spectroscopic binarity, and obtain accurate central wavelengths including the effects of contamination, forbidden lines, and wind infilling. We analyse 41 apparently single bright O stars. We used multi-epoch HR LiLiMaRlin spectroscopy cleaned with UNWIND and stellar models computed with FASTWIND. The epoch spectra were cross-correlated to study their variability. The RVs were computed from (a) cross-correlation of H and He lines with FASTWIND models, (b) profile fitting of metallic lines, and (c) cross-correlation of the full spectrum with a template star. A comparison between the RV dispersions for different wavelength regions reveals different groups of stars in terms of variability: (a) non-SG slow rotators, (b) fast rotators, (c) SGs, and (d) Oe stars. This is a manifestation of the different role of pulsations, winds, and disks in RV variability. We determine RV dispersion thresholds for the detection of new SBs. We also use a FASTWIND grid to establish the effects of (a) the presence of He II lines close to Balmer lines, (b) the existence of forbidden components in two He I lines, and (c) wind infilling in the determination of accurate RVs. With all of that, we determined RVs for our 41 stars, checked their accuracy, and discovered significant differences with literature values. Our analysis has further revealed four SB1 systems unknown in the summer of 2025, one new SB2, two new Oe stars, and three new Onfp stars.

papers.title: GOWC: an open tool for observing-conditions prediction and observation planning, tested against site monitors and an exposure-time calculator
papers.summary: GOWC (Global Observing-conditions Weather Catalogue) is an open web application that takes the user from a target to an exposure plan across 2,642 catalogued observatory sites. It computes seeing, airmass, extinction, precipitable water vapour, sky brightness and signal-to-noise from live Open-Meteo meteorology, including pressure-level profiles, and tests most of these outputs against an independent reference. The photometric SNR calculator, run with GOWC's own catalogue entries, reproduces the ING SIGNAL exposure-time calculator to a median 1.9 per cent over a 16-point magnitude-airmass grid on two instruments. Precipitable water vapour tracks the Paranal LHATPRO radiometer closely ($\rho=+0.95$, 606 nights) with a +43 per cent wet bias. Seeing is computed from the Tatarski $C_n^2$ chain integrated over the pressure levels above the site and calibrated to the ESO MASS free-atmosphere median at Paranal; matching it requires an effective Tatarski coefficient of 5.7, nearly twice the upper end of the published range, which quantifies how much turbulence four coarse pressure levels fail to resolve. Against ~20 months of ESO DIMM data the seeing forecast has a weak but significant night-to-night ranking skill ($\rho=+0.24$, 575 nights, at Paranal; +0.16 at La Silla). Surface wind alone does as well or better (+0.27, +0.41) and persistence does better (+0.42, +0.47), but the free-atmosphere term tracks MASS ($\rho=+0.35$) and carries information that surface wind does not (partial $\rho=+0.28$, +0.40). At held-out sites the absolute seeing scale is no better than a constant. GOWC therefore treats forecast seeing as indicative, shows measured values wherever a public site monitor exists, and states which outputs are measured, calibrated or unvalidated.

papers.title: Linking Detectable Tidal Features to Stellar Halo Growth: An Integrated Analysis of the Outskirts of Massive Early-type Galaxies
papers.summary: Motivated by the finding that massive galaxies with tidal features (GwT) are preferentially found in low-density environments, one wonders whether this trend arises from enhanced debris survivability or from more active mass-assembly histories. If driven by the latter, structural signatures, such as more developed stellar halos, should also form through cumulative accretion. To address this, we analyze azimuthally averaged surface-brightness profiles of 436 massive early-type galaxies from the DESI Legacy Imaging Survey, comparing the median-stacked profiles of galaxies with tidal features to those without. We find that, after resampling by stellar mass and environmental density, a subtle but systematic structural divergence emerges in the galaxy outskirts ($r>5\times r_{50}$). Specifically, the GwT population in the lower-density & higher-mass regime exhibits a relative intensity excess. This suggests that more developed stellar halos have formed, likely due to longer and/or more significant accretion events. In contrast, those in the higher-density & lower-mass regime show a relative deficiency in intensity, which is reasonable to interpret as a result of structural disruption from environmental effects rather than a lack of cumulative accretion. Our findings suggest that visible tidal features$-$particularly in massive systems within quiet environments$-$do not merely reflect recent stochastic accretion events but also hint at the long-term assembly history of galaxies. This work is a depth-limited study that offers a glimpse into an integrated analysis of tidal debris and stellar halos, thereby introducing a novel pathway to unravel the complex assembly histories of galaxies.

papers.title: An extended red wing of the 5797 {\AA} diffuse interstellar band in the Red Rectangle nebula
papers.summary: Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are interstellar molecular absorption features that are ubiquitous in the interstellar medium (ISM). So far, there was only one known sight line where DIBs show an extend tail towards the red (ETR), namely Herschel 36. Such sight lines are essential to illuminate the DIB problem, namely the identification of their carriers, because they show more DIB variation than standard ISM sight lines. To report a new detection of the 5797 {\AA} DIB in the Red Rectangle nebula with an ETR, which adds a new observational constraint for the DIB carrier. We analysed archival GIRAFFE/FLAMES integral field spectroscopy to extract all spectral features between 5776 and 5810 {\AA} at different spatial positions. We used time series spectra to identify stellar and circumstellar features, and data from different instruments to exclude instrumental effects. We report the firm detection of the 5797 {\AA} DIB that is localised in the Red Rectangle nebula, or in the ISM in the sight line towards it. Curiously, while the 5797 {\AA} DIB shows an ETR in the Red Rectangle, the 5780 {\AA} DIB does not. Further, we report an exceptionally high equivalent ratio of EW(5797)/EW(5780) = 1.79 higher than any other literature value.

papers.title: Calibration requirements for Epoch of Reionization 21-cm signal observations - V. Bias and variance in the cylindrical power spectrum from uGMRT Band 3 observations of the ELAIS-N1 field
papers.summary: Detection of the redshifted 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen requires precise control of systematic effects arising from instrumental calibration. In this work, we investigate the impact of both time- and frequency-dependent residual gain and bandpass errors on the estimation of the multifrequency angular power spectrum (MAPS) using radio interferometric observations. We discuss our previously developed analytical framework for estimating bias and excess variance in 21-cm signal MAPS in the presence of these residual errors and apply it to uGMRT Band-3 observations. The statistical properties of the residual gains are derived from the data themselves, including their temporal and spectral correlations. We introduce a robust technique for additionally flagging poor-quality data. Our results show that the excess variance induced by residual gain and bandpass errors dominates over the bias across the range of angular multipoles considered. The amplitude of this variance is comparable to the expected power spectrum upper limit at redshift $z \sim 2.2$, indicating that residual calibration errors can significantly affect the detectability of the 21-cm signal. We further transform the estimated MAPS into ($k_{\perp}, k_{ll}$) space and find the expected foreground wedge structure. Importantly, we observe a significant power leakage into the nominal EoR window, which we attribute to residual calibration systematics. This highlights that even after standard foreground mitigation, time- and frequency-correlated gain errors can introduce mode-mixing and contaminate the EoR window. Our results emphasise the necessity of improved calibration accuracy and robust characterisation of residual gain statistics for current and upcoming interferometric experiments such as the uGMRT and SKA, to enable reliable detection of the cosmological 21-cm signal.

papers.title: Radial dependence of galaxy and halo properties in cosmic voids: SDSS DR7 and the ELUCID constrained simulation
papers.summary: Cosmic voids provide a setting for examining the interplay between mass and environment in shaping galaxy and halo properties. Using the SDSS DR7 volume-limited galaxy sample and the ELUCID constrained simulation of the local large-scale structure, we investigate the radial profiles of galaxy and subhalo properties across different mass ranges, identifying voids independently in the observed galaxy and simulated subhalo distributions. Both stellar mass and subhalo mass increase from void interiors toward the void boundary, indicating that lower-mass galaxies and subhaloes preferentially reside in void interiors. The satellite fraction of subhaloes also increases systematically toward the void boundary. Galaxy colour and specific star formation rate exhibit radial variations that are weaker than their dependence on stellar mass, while the spiral fraction shows little radial dependence at fixed stellar mass. For dark-matter haloes, the apparent radial increase in size within a broad high-mass bin largely disappears when narrower mass ranges are considered. Halo concentration and spin show radial variations at fixed mass, with higher concentrations and lower spins toward void interiors, although the concentration trend is less pronounced in the extended low-mass sample. The formation redshift of low-mass subhaloes also increases toward the void boundary, whereas this dependence weakens and eventually disappears at higher masses. Overall, the radial trends in galaxy properties are generally weaker than their mass dependence, while several subhalo properties retain measurable radial variations at fixed mass.

papers.title: Comparison of Hybrid and Standard Reconstruction Methods on IXPE Astrophysical Data
papers.summary: The hybrid reconstruction algorithm developed by Cibrario et al. 2023 combined a convolutional neural network (CNN) with standard moment analysis to improve track reconstruction in IXPE Gas Pixel Detectors. Although validated on laboratory data (Cibrario et al. 2025), the method's astrophysical performance had not been systematically characterized. We present the first comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction on IXPE point sources, measuring sensitivity gains versus energy. We analyze Her X-1, a bright, polarized accreting pulsar as a benchmark, and soft-state XTE J1701-461, a bright neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary with no detected polarization, to assess residual systematics. From both pipelines' Level-2 event files, we compare normalized Stokes parameters, polarization degree (PD) and angle (PA), and detection significance. For Her X-1, hybrid reconstruction increases significance at all energies, significantly above ~2.83 keV. R = {\sigma}_hyb/{\sigma}_std differs from unity by 9.3{\sigma} in the 2.83-4.00 keV bin and reaches 1.18\pm0.03 at 5.66-8.00 keV (6.2{\sigma}). For XTE J1701-461, PD is consistent with zero and R with unity. Fourier analysis reveals excess power in hybrid angle distributions at low energies for modes m = 3, 6, 12 and 15, significant at >7{\sigma} relative to the standard method; at 5-8 keV, all modes are consistent with noise in both methods. These CNN-amplified hexagonal-grid artifacts do not affect Stokes parameters because they are orthogonal to polarization modes.The method delivers a statistically significant sensitivity gain for Her X-1, consistent with Cibrario et al. 2025 and equivalent to ~20% more effective area without extra observing time. These results support systematic use of hybrid reconstruction on IXPE astrophysical data.

papers.title: Space Electric and Magnetic Sensor (SEAMS) Phase I: A Pathfinder Mission for Low-Frequency Radio Astronomy
papers.summary: In this paper, the Space Electric and Magnetic Sensor (SEAMS), a space based mission dedicated to very low frequency (below 16 MHz) observations of the radio sky is proposed. The SEAMS mission is planned in two phases. The first phase is specifically designed for radio frequency interference (RFI) mapping from the low earth orbit (LEO). The low frequency region of the electromagnetic spectrum is filled with a variety of artificial as well as natural RFI. Previous observations have confirmed the effect of this terrestrial interference on astronomical observations. Thus, a map of terrestrial RFI as observed from space would give valuable information to groups working in the low-frequency regime. For the first phase, the payload will be mounted on to the fourth stage of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)'s third generation Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), which will stay in LEO for several weeks. The payload consists of a pair of orthogonal active monopoles, a simple baseband sampling receiver optimized for recording power spectra from each antenna. The design also aims to detect strong signals of astronomical origin despite RFI. In the second phase, we intend to send a more sophisticated space payload to orbit the moon and subsequently land on its surface.

papers.title: QED VI: Neutral hydrogen gas in supernova-driven galactic outflows
papers.summary: Winds that eject mass from galactic discs regulate the growth of galaxies, and observations show that, at least within a few kpc of the disc, most of the mass flux is carried by neutral rather than ionized material. However, it has proven difficult for simulations of supernova-driven winds to reproduce this observation, leading to speculations that the bulk of the mass must be driven by radiation pressure or cosmic rays rather than supernovae. Here we report simulations of supernova-driven winds using the GPU-accelerated code QUOKKA that reach a resolution of $\Delta x = 1$ pc, significantly higher resolution and simulation volume than previous work. At this resolution the winds are dominated by neutral mass, with cloud sizes, masses and column densities broadly similar to those of the HI clouds in the Milky Way's nuclear wind. The neutral material is not ballistic, but is instead driven by momentum transfer associated with drag and condensation of hot gas onto the neutral phase. By contrast, when we coarsen the resolution to values comparable to those used in earlier work, the neutral outflow weakens at $\Delta x = 2$ pc and disappears at $\Delta x = 4$ pc. We argue that this difference arises partly because lower-resolution simulations do not resolve, with a few cells, the 3-6 pc thick cooling layers in which hot gas condenses onto neutral clouds.

papers.title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing
papers.summary: In canonical twisted-torus models of hydromagnetic equilibrium in neutron stars, the toroidal field is confined to regions where the poloidal field lines are closed. As spindown torques applied at the stellar surface need not be communicated efficiently to such magnetically-unlocked regions, toroidal zones or magnetic voids may rotate faster than the electromagnetically braked part of the star. Continuous gravitational radiation from the associated non-corotating quadrupole may therefore be emitted at higher frequencies than poloidal ones to a degree that depends on the diffusive microphysics controlling angular momentum transport. Dissipative processes can suppress long-lived lags, and we estimate the relevant timescales and their sensitivity to microphysics. Nevertheless, we show that a quadrupole component whose pattern speed differs from the observed spin is shifted, or smeared, over a finite frequency band. Single-template or narrowband upper limits therefore constrain only the quadrupole contribution lying inside the searched frequency window, not necessarily the full frequency-integrated quadrupole. Using simple models, we quantify this spectral redistribution over finite observation windows and discuss its implications for continuous-wave searches.

papers.title: A Congestion-Aware RDMA Front-End for LST Advanced Camera Readout
papers.summary: The Advanced Camera (AdvCam) upgrade of the Large-Sized Telescopes (LSTs) calls for a fully digital readout in which each front-end board streams data to the event-building servers over commercial 10 Gb/s Ethernet, using an FPGA implementation of Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over Converged Ethernet v2 (RoCEv2). In a previous work, a customized RoCEv2 core integrated with the SLAC SURF UDP/MAC stack was shown to sustain near-line-rate data transfers from a Xilinx KCU105 to a server equipped with a Mellanox ConnectX-5 NIC. However, the AdvCam topology is an incast funnel: many 10 GbE links converge onto a single uplink, and bare Priority Flow Control (PFC) congestion management protocol is known to be unfair and to suffer from head-of-line blocking. This work extends the previous design with the Data Center Quantized Congestion Notification (DCQCN) algorithm. A protocol-level ns-3 simulation is used to validate the DCQCN dynamics and to explore the parameter space; an FPGA rate-limiter integrated into the SURF MAC reacts to incoming Congestion Notification Packets (CNPs) according to the DCQCN state machine; a cocotb testbench with an emulated Python switch verifies the firmware end-to-end against a Soft-RoCE receiver; and a three-sender incast hardware test on a DCQCN-enabled commercial switch reproduces the canonical fair-share, reactive-redistribution, and saw-tooth behaviour expected from a commercial RDMA NIC. The internal rate-limiter register is shown to track the measured RoCEv2 throughput cycle by cycle.

papers.title: The biases caused by interpolated table models and their impact on X-ray spectroscopy
papers.summary: Models for X-ray spectroscopy involving complex relativistic or plasma physics are commonly pre-computed on a grid, In this paper, we aim to quantify the potential biases and distortions introduced by the computational error and propagated into parameter inference by interpolating linearly these complex, non-linear models. We analyse the performance of Bayesian sampling algorithms on mock inference problems. Then, we model real observations of an accreting black hole X-ray binary in both the soft and hard states. We find that linear interpolation can a) greatly bias the posterior distribution of model parameters and b) distort the likelihood space to such a degree that posterior distributions become artificially multimodal. This multi-modality causes a noticeable loss in computational efficiency in both sampling and fitting techniques. As a result, exploring a given parameter space until convergence requires an extremely large computational cost. These findings call for improving the computational techniques used when fitting modern X-ray data, for example through better sampling algorithms and/or more sophisticated interpolation schemes

papers.title: Investigating supernova-remnant X-ray maps with dendrogram-based techniques
papers.summary: X-ray images of supernova remnants provide important information regarding the spatial distribution of the physical and chemical parameters of the shocked plasma. Our objective is to provide a comprehensive and quantitative assessment of the similarities observed across narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a given supernova remnant. We also aim to perform comparative analyses between distinct remnants. We adopted two dendrogram-based techniques, namely a multivariate analysis and a deep-learning, graph-based approach (by exploring different metrics) for the study of Chandra X-ray maps of Cassiopeia A, G292.0+1.8, Tycho's SNR, Kepler's SNR, and W49B. We also tested the reliability of our results on synthetic X-ray maps produced from a 3D hydrodynamic simulation of Cassiopeia A. We identify clusters of narrow-band images (and equivalent-width maps) corresponding to emission lines of chemical elements that are expected to be synthesized in the same layers of the exploding star and/or that originate from plasma at similar temperatures. By comparing different objects, we clearly observe strong similarities among Type Ia remnants (namely Tycho's SNR and Kepler's SNR) and core-collapse remnants (Cassiopeia A and G292.0+1.8), with W49B being more similar to the latter objects. The methodology developed in this work provides a robust tool to measure the analogies and differences between narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a supernova remnant, offering clues on the distribution of the different chemical species and on the plasma temperature. Although tested on a limited sample of objects, the adoption of this tool for the classification of supernova remnants (Type Ia vs. core-collapse) yields promising results.

papers.title: Photometric Redshift Estimation with Hybrid Quantum Neural Network
papers.summary: A Hybrid Quantum Neural Network (HQNN) is applied to recover the photometric redshift of a galaxy dataset built using data from two astronomical surveys, the Kilo-Degree Survey (KIDS) and the VISTA Kilo-Degree Infrared Galaxy (VIKING), which provide data with coverage from the optical to the near-infrared electromagnetic spectrum. The results are then compared with those obtained by a classical neural network. We see that HQNN consistently recovers the reference photometric redshift with a high statistical fidelity. Furthermore, both the $R^2$ and the MSE found by the HQNN are consistently better than those found by the classical counterpart (albeit consistent in the error range), proving the worth of further investigating these novel technologies for this particular astrophysical application.

papers.title: Cracking into RACS - I. Measuring the cosmic dipole in the RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 radio surveys with simulation-based inference
papers.summary: We measure the dipole in the count of radio galaxies over the sky as seen by the Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP) in the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS). Our analysis focuses on the third observational epoch in the 'low' passband (943.5 MHz; RACS-low3) and the first epoch in the 'mid' passband (1367.5 MHz; RACS-mid1). We find strong evidence for a systematic relation between flux density and the temperature at the time of observation, whereby reported flux densities are suppressed to a greater degree when the ASKAP antennas are warmer. We include this temperature response in our forward model as part of our Simulation-based Inference (SBI) pipeline, generating data realisations that are then used by a neural network to learn the likelihood function. Despite this model, RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 both exhibit a dipole inconsistent with the kinematic dipole of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), adding further evidence for the 'cosmic dipole tension'. For RACS-low3, the dipole agrees in direction but has an amplitude four times in excess, while the dipole for RACS-mid1 is offset from the CMB and has an amplitude roughly five times in excess. Our findings underscore the importance of interrogating the data for systematic effects and showcase the power of SBI in handling them.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Three-Dimensional Stellar Mass Profiles of Massive Galaxy Clusters
papers.summary: We investigate the three-dimensional (3D) stellar mass profiles of galaxy clusters using simulations and observations. We develop the Projection-to-Enclosed Estimator by Layers (PEEL) model, which geometrically reconstructs the 3D stellar mass profile from the projected stellar mass profile under the assumption of spherical symmetry. Starting from the outermost annulus, the PEEL model subtracts the contributions of the outer shells from the projected mass in each inner annulus. Using 205 halos from the TNG-Cluster simulation, we show that the reconstructed profile (hereafter the PEEL profile) recovers the true 3D stellar mass profile without systematic bias. We also examine potential systematic effects, including the use of subhalos versus stellar particles, the choice of cluster center, and the 3D shape of the halo. We then apply the PEEL model to a stacked sample of nine massive clusters from the MAssive Cluster survey with Hectospec (MACH). The observed PEEL profile is much flatter than the simulated 3D profile, indicating that the simulated clusters have a more centrally concentrated stellar mass distribution, mainly because of an excess of extremely massive galaxies in their cores. Combining the PEEL profile with the total mass profile from the caustic technique, we derive the stellar mass fraction profile of the observed clusters. The stellar mass fraction remains nearly constant at $0.009 \pm 0.002$ within $R_{200}$, consistent with previous observations and with the simulated clusters. The PEEL model provides a practical tool for measuring the 3D stellar mass profiles of large cluster samples from future wide-field spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title: Mesoscale Modelling of Titan's Shangri-La region: the impact of surface properties on winds
papers.summary: The knowledge of Titan's near-surface atmosphere is sparse. The Huygens descent probe measured winds, and the multiple dune field observations and possible dust storms suggest active near-surface dynamics. The Dragonfly rotorcraft lander will fly close to the surface in the Shangri-La region, near the Huygens landing site, where complex dune orientations were observed. This study presents the first mesoscale modelling of the near-surface dynamics in this region. However, due to a lack of high-resolution topography data, synthetic maps of surface properties were built. The surface was divided into different topographical units, such as plains, mountains, etc. The slopes and height of those units were then parametrised. Maps of thermal inertia, albedo and the aerodynamic roughness height were also built. The mesoscale model is coupled to a comprehensive radiative transfer code and forced by a global climate model. No moist processes are considered in this study. Topography has a major impact on near-surface wind amplitude and direction through slope flows and valley circulations. The majority of the winds are below 0.25 m/s. These winds induce a sensible heat flux comparable to the surface solar flux. Spatially varying thermal inertia has the biggest impact on the wind and surface temperature, with high values leading to smaller diurnal amplitude. The seasonal variability is taken into account, with stronger winds in northern summer. Predicted mesoscale near-surface winds are capable of lifting dust over dune fields, with different orientations during the year, and can therefore potentially play a role in sediment transport on Titan.

papers.title: NOEMA Observations of the Center of M33: A Parsec-scale Molecular Filament and an Ordered Gas-Star-Formation Sequence
papers.summary: We present NOEMA CO(1-0) observations of the inner $\sim$500 pc of M33 at a resolution of $0.91''\times0.37''$ ($3.7\times1.5$ pc), resolving the compact molecular gas structures and revealing their relation to recent massive star formation. The most prominent structure is a southeastern molecular filament (SE filament) that extends 76 pc along its principal axis, is 23 pc wide, and contains three CO-bright knots. Across eight independent transverse cuts, the adjacent H$\alpha$ ridge is displaced preferentially to one side of the principal CO ridge by a median $10.0^{+0.9}_{-1.4}$ pc. Young OB candidates are more closely associated with H$\alpha$ than with compact CO. The filament shows little velocity change along its length but a resolved gradient across its minor axis. Its elongated morphology, transverse kinematics, and ordered CO-H$\alpha$ distribution are consistent with locally asymmetric molecular-gas compression and subsequent massive star formation. Across the wider field, 23 well-measured compact clumps have a median radius of 2.67 pc and a median velocity dispersion of 2.15 km s$^{-1}$. Their linewidth and apparent virial-parameter distributions show no clear difference between the SE filament and the rest of the field. Although the local spiral potential and pattern speed remain unconstrained, the observations provide a resolved view of a compression-compatible molecular-to-ionized-gas sequence in the center of M33.

papers.title: Inferring the Total Mass of Galaxy Halos Using Photometry
papers.summary: Galaxy size, as defined as the radius at which the stellar surface density reaches $1~\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-2}$ ($R_1$), has been shown to correlate more tightly with stellar mass than the effective radius. Cosmological simulations further predict a tight relation between $R_1$ and dark matter halo mass ($M_{200}$), but this prediction has not yet been tested observationally. We present the first observational test of the predicted $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation and assess whether galaxy size, defined through $R_1$, can serve as a robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. We analyze galaxies from the SPARC database, combining high-quality rotation curves to infer dark matter halo masses with stellar surface density profiles derived from photometric data to measure $R_1$. We then compare the observed relation with the predictions from state-of-the-art cosmological simulations. We find good agreement between observations and simulations: galaxies follow the same tight $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation predicted by numerical models across the explored mass range, with low intrinsic scatter. We provide the first observational validation of the $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation, demonstrating that $R_1$ is a simple, physically motivated, and robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. Because $R_1$ is determined entirely from photometric observations, it provides a tool for inferring halo masses from imaging data alone, with applications to studies of galaxy formation and evolution.

papers.title: Model-independent calibration of gamma-ray bursts with Bayesian neural networks
papers.summary: Context. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend cosmological distance measurements beyond the range densely sampled by Type Ia supernovae, but their standardization requires reliable calibration and uncertainty estimates. Aims. We calibrate the Amati correlation without assuming a background cosmological model, assess its stability, and examine the cosmological reach of current and future GRB Hubble diagrams. Methods. We train a Bayesian neural network on Pantheon+ supernovae, assess and recalibrate its predictive uncertainties, and calibrate the correlation for GRBs at $z \leq 1.5$ using the D'Agostini and Reichart likelihoods. We combine the GRB Hubble diagram with supernovae, Hubble-parameter measurements, and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. Local-regression, covariance, leave-three-out, redshift-evolution, and Efron-Petrosian diagnostics test the standardization assumptions. We also analyse idealized future catalogues of 1500 standardized GRBs. Results. The diagram reaches $z \simeq 9.4$. Covariance and leave-three-out diagnostics produce small changes in the cosmological constraints. A parametric evolution coefficient is consistent with zero, whereas the truncation-corrected diagnostic indicates marginal isotropic-energy evolution that can occur along the Amati relation. Dark-energy extensions improve the phenomenological fit relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM: AIC favours the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder parametrization, while BIC favours constant-$w$ dark energy. Forecasts show strong conditional model-discrimination power under the adopted uncertainty model. Conclusions. GRBs provide a complementary high-redshift extension of the supernova distance ladder. Present results do not establish an evolving dark-energy equation of state. Larger homogeneous samples are promising, but realistic selection functions and calibration systematics remain essential.

papers.title: Physical assumptions versus nature: the shape of the heliosphere
papers.summary: Context. The Interstellar Probe study describes a mission concept with a launch window beginning in 2036, aiming to reach several hundred astronomical units beyond the heliopause within a time frame of at least 50 years. One of the fundamental questions related to this mission is where the boundaries of the heliosphere are and how thick they are. To answer it we need to know the shape of the heliosphere. Over the past 60 years numerous models of the heliosphere have been developed. For a long time these models depicted a heliosphere resembling a comet. Since around 2015 models have been presented that differ significantly from the shape of a comet. Aims. The aim of this paper is to emphasize that the obtained image of the heliosphere depends on the model assumptions contained in these articles. Methods. We review numerous publications examining the shape of the heliosphere. All of these articles use a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) model of the heliosphere together with various assumptions that simplify the physics of the interaction of the solar wind flowing from the Sun with the surrounding interstellar medium. Results. The result of all these studies is a shape of the heliosphere described as either croissant-like or cometary-like, depending on the assumptions made. Conclusions. We are still uncertain which model represents the real heliosphere. Nature requires a theoretical model that is more accurate. In our opinion the interaction of the solar wind with the interstellar medium must be described by the Boltzmann system of equations using artificial intelligence. In the context of the planned space mission this conclusion is crucial.

papers.title: An Intermediate Mass Stripped Star in a 4.2-hour Orbit around a Compact Object
papers.summary: From their discovery as radio pulsars to landmark multi-messenger observations of their mergers, double neutron stars have transformed our understanding of the extreme Universe and the formation of heavy elements (Drout et al. 2017; Abbott et al. 2017). Yet, uncertainties in their formation result in predicted merger rates spanning orders of magnitude (Tauris et al. 2017; Mandel & Broekgaarden 2022). The most critical stage occurs when a star is stripped of its hydrogen-rich envelope, causing the binary orbit to shrink drastically. Despite its fundamental role, the resulting tight binaries comprising a stripped star and neutron star have remained elusive. Here we report a $\sim$$3.4\,M_{\odot}$ stripped star (Ludwig et al. 2026; Drout et al. 2023; G\"otberg et al. 2023) orbiting an unseen companion every 4.2 hours. Our orbital and spectroscopic analysis excludes a normal star, which would not fit within the orbit, as well as a second stripped star which would have been detectable in our spectra. Adding constraints from high cadence photometry gives a 99.4% probability that the companion is too massive to be a white dwarf, making a neutron star the most likely companion. We model the system's future and predict that the stripped star will transfer mass again before exploding as a hydrogen-free supernova, leaving a bound pair of neutron stars that will merge after 220 Myr. This system reveals a previously unconstrained phase of binary evolution, uncovering a new class of systems that probes the uncertain physics of massive stars, linking to observable gravitational-wave sources.

papers.title: A Warped Dust Ring in the CQ Tau Disk
papers.summary: The diversity of planetary orbital architectures calls for observational constraints on radial variations in disk-plane orientation, or warps, yet such variations in dust disks remain poorly characterized. CQ Tau is a promising target because its misaligned inner disk and candidate gas warp suggest a radially extended warp. We present the ALMA 1.3 mm dust continuum image reconstructed from the real part of the visibilities, extracting the centro-symmetric disk structure. At an effective spatial resolution of $0.052'' \times 0.042''$ ($7.8 \times 6.3$ au), the image reveals a bright main ring at radii of $\sim20$--$70$ au and an unresolved compact emission component tracing the inner disk around the central star. Ellipse fits centered on the stellar position to contours tracing the inner and outer edges of the ring reveal radial variations in position angles and inclinations. At the inner edge ($\sim21$--$26$ au), the position angle and inclination span $214^\circ$--$233^\circ$ and $23^\circ$--$39^\circ$, respectively, while they span $231^\circ$--$235^\circ$ and $33^\circ$--$36^\circ$ at the outer edge ($\sim58$--$67$ au). Whereas a coplanar ring toy model fails to reproduce such variations, a warped ring model with the local tilt decreasing from $\sim4^\circ$ at $r = 20$ au to $\sim1^\circ$ at 60 au reproduces them. The high-pass-filtered real-part image reveals a pair of opposed curved negative residuals. Similar features appear only in the warped ring model, further supporting the dust warp. These results establish CQ Tau as an example of a warped dust disk and an important laboratory for investigating the connection between three-dimensional disk geometry and planet formation.

papers.title: Explainable Prediction of High-Speed Solar Wind Streams driven by Coronal Holes via Topological Data Analysis
papers.summary: High-speed solar wind streams (HSSs) originating from coronal holes (CHs) are an important driver of recurrent geomagnetic activity. Since HSSs are associated to coronal structures visible in extreme-ultraviolet observations, this provides a natural basis for forecasting several days in advance. In this work, we investigate whether the topology of coronal structures observed in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) images contains predictive information on the subsequent occurrence of CH-driven HSSs at Earth. To this end, we consider Topological Data Analysis (TDA), and in particular persistent homology, to classify EUV solar images according to the occurrence of HSSs at Earth four days later. The target is a binary classification of HSS occurrence at a four-day lead time, defined using an HSS interval catalog and solar wind speed thresholds. Several combinations of topological representations and classifiers are evaluated under a common cross-validation framework. The results indicate that the topology of EUV coronal structures alone contains predictive information on subsequent CH-driven HSS occurrence, despite the absence of explicit CH geometric descriptors in the model input. To investigate the origin of this predictive information, we develop a model-level explainability framework based on cross-validation-aggregated feature weights and spatial evidence maps. A fully traced example connects persistence diagrams and persistence-image features to the classifier output and to their spatial localization in the original EUV observation. The proposed framework provides a transparent and computationally lightweight approach for investigating the relationship between coronal topology and subsequent high-speed solar wind streams.

papers.title: The mass discrepancy problem in massive stars: an inferential perspective
papers.summary: Bayesian inference has become a standard tool for inferring stellar parameters from stellar evolution models. However, comparatively little attention has been paid to how alternative Bayesian likelihood formulations influence inferred stellar parameters, and the resulting evolutionary mass discrepancy for massive main sequence stars. Here, we investigate the effects of mixing and alternative Bayesian likelihood formulations on the inferred stellar parameters and the resulting evolutionary mass discrepancy. We analysed a sample of seven double-lined eclipsing B type binaries with $\beta$ Cep components using one pre-computed MESA grid of stellar evolution models and observables such as mass, effective temperature, surface gravity and luminosity. Stellar parameters were inferred within a Bayesian inference method employing nested sampling and piecewise cubic interpolation across the model grid. We compared several inference strategies, including single-star and coeval binary models, with and without dynamical masses included in the likelihood function. Bayesian evidence and Pareto-optimal model selection were used to evaluate the preferred solutions. Our work reinforces that core-boundary mixing is required for all stars. Further, the inferential analysis demonstrates that different likelihood formulations may lead to systematically different inferred mass discrepancies. For the adopted input physics and the small sample of stars, we find that about half of the apparent reduction in the inferred mass discrepancy may arise from the construction of the Bayesian likelihood, while enhanced near-core mixing accounts for the remaining improvement. The preferred coeval solutions further indicate that the systems span central hydrogen mass fraction of $0.632$ -- $0.205$, with ages of $4.25$ -- $12.27$ $\rm Myr$ determined with precisions of $2$ -- $13\%$ under the adopted model input physics.

papers.title: SPAM: Survey Overview and JWST/NIRCam Multi-Band Photometry Catalog
papers.summary: We present the Star-formation from Photometry through the Addition of Medium-bands (SPAM) survey, a 62.9 hr JWST/NIRCam imaging program to add ten new filters, nine medium-band filters, and one broad-band filter to the CEERS legacy dataset. We describe the observation strategy, present the data, and detail the data-reduction process. We include a complete reduction of imaging in the legacy CEERS footprint, inclusive of all publicly available photometric parallel and GO observations within the legacy CEERS footprint. We present a multi-band photometric and photometric redshift catalog which includes all medium- and broad-band filters available on NIRCam. We find that adding medium bands from the SPAM and MINERVA programs improves photometric redshifts. We discuss how these data advance the SPAM survey's key science goals: better-constrained photometric redshifts, identification of high-redshift overdensity members, improved recovery of emission-line strengths, and more accurate star formation histories.

papers.title: Classification of Fermi Blazars of Uncertain Type Using Positive-Unlabelled Machine Learning
papers.summary: We apply positive-unlabelled (PU) machine learning to the 1623 blazars of uncertain type (BCUs) in the Fermi Large Area Telescope Fourth Source Catalogue, Data Release 4 (4FGL-DR4). Five PU classifiers are trained on seven gamma-ray features, once with the 820 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) and once with the 1490 BL Lac objects as the labelled class (FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode). Each source is scored out of fold over 100 repeated five-fold splits, and its confidence is the fraction of splits in which at least three of the five classifiers flag it. At a confidence of at least 0.1, 437 BCUs are FSRQ-like, 597 are BL Lac-like, 12 are flagged in both modes and 577 in neither. On known sources the ensemble reaches a recall of 0.80 in FSRQ mode and 0.82 in BL Lac mode at a false-positive rate of 0.08, but a logistic regression trained on the labelled sources alone does at least as well, so PU learning gives no accuracy gain here. Removing the sky coordinates from the features does not lower the performance on known sources but adds 107 BCUs to the candidate lists and drops 30, which is consistent with the coordinates acting as a selection shortcut, so we exclude them. We check the candidates against published optical spectra, SDSS-V spectra, and BCUs that later received a class in the catalogue. Among sources assigned a single class, BL Lac-like calls are correct for 84 to 100% of the sources and FSRQ-like calls for 58 to 83%, depending on the sample. These samples come from spectroscopic follow-up and do not represent all BCUs. The candidates are fainter and lie closer to the Galactic plane than the labelled sources, and the excess of unclassified BCUs in the plane is not explained. We release the confidences of all 1623 BCUs.

papers.title: The long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus: a comparison between GRMHD simulations and relativistic thin disk theory
papers.summary: In this paper we analyse the long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus using novel GRMHD simulations which, for the first time, have been run out to extremely large evolutionary times $t_{\rm max} = 10^7 GM_\bullet/c^3$. This allows for detailed comparisons between the gross evolution of this GRMHD simulation and existing "spreading disk" analytical theories. We show that the long-term features of this evolution are well described by General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory (GRTDT), which reproduces various aspects of the GRMHD evolution to within a factor $\sim 2$, despite the disk in our simulation not being remotely thin, showing dynamically dominant (MAD) magnetic fields, and launching a powerful wind. Thin disk theory functions as an accurate and cheap effective theory for the evolution in radius and time of the bulk of the disk material, and for the time dependence of the horizon accretion rate. We argue that this effectiveness originates from the global conservation laws of mass and angular momentum, together with a turbulent stress which we find to be local and independent of density, lending support to the ad-hoc local-stress-tensor phenomenology employed in analytical models. We also find that the turbulent accretion rate variability in the inner disk is log-normally distributed, consistent with a key assumption in the modeling of observed variability.

papers.title: Constraining Supermassive Black Hole Seeding and Accretion via Occupation Fractions and Mass-Weighted Distributions
papers.summary: The formation of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is a key open problem in galaxy evolution, with light- and heavy-seeding models predicting distinct black hole occupation fractions (BHOFs). Using multiwavelength observations from the LSST Deep Drilling Fields, we measure the AGN fraction and estimate the BHOF across $0<z<1$. Applying a hierarchical Bayesian model, we find that the inferred BHOF remains $100\%$ for host galaxy masses below $10^9 M_\odot$ at lower redshifts. These findings are consistent with light-seed scenarios. Additionally, we computed the black hole masses for several galaxies in the W-CDF-S to test the mass-weighted black hole occupation distributions from semi-analytic models (SAM). Using a reduced-$\chi^2$ analysis, we find that the data are consistent with the main-sequence accretion model regardless of the assumed seeding mechanism. These results provide new observational constraints on SMBH seeding and highlight the value of combining deep extragalactic surveys with probabilistic modeling.

papers.title: Connectivity rewiring and filament formation by active region emergence observed with Solar Orbiter
papers.summary: Using an 11-day dataset from Solar Orbiter, combining EUV imaging, H$\alpha$ observations, vector magnetograms and nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, we track the evolution from the emergence of a new active region to the reconfiguration of coronal connectivity. We find that the restructuring proceeds through a sequence of localized reconnection events that propagate along the filament channel, producing successive brightenings and bidirectional flows. This process leads to the gradual erosion of the original filament and the simultaneous formation of a new, highly sheared filament connecting the two regions. Magnetic modeling reveals a transition from a sheared arcade supporting the initial filament to a twisted flux rope underlying the newly formed structure. Our results demonstrate that flux emergence can reorganize filament channels through a spatially and temporally ordered sequence of reconnection events, rather than a single impulsive episode. This sequential reconnection front provides a natural mechanism for filament formation in evolving active regions and highlights the importance of continuously changing magnetic connectivity in the corona.

papers.title: pbhalo: computing primordial black hole and minihalo populations from a single primordial perturbation spectrum
papers.summary: An enhancement of the primordial curvature power spectrum on small scales can give rise to two populations of compact objects: primordial black holes (PBHs), which form during radiation domination, and dark matter minihalos, including ultracompact minihalos (UCMHs), which form from the same modes during matter domination. The package components are validated against colossus (a code for halo mass functions and cosmological quantities), pbhstat (a code for the PBH mass function from a given spectrum) and published results; joint constraints are illustrated for lognormal peaks. The code is distributed under the MIT license.

papers.title: Mapping the Milky Way with SDSS-V: Galactic Genesis Selection Function and Mock Catalog
papers.summary: Robust chemodynamic mapping of the Milky Way requires accounting for the selection function of the survey used, the probability that a given star is included in the final catalog as a function of its observable properties. We derive the empirical selection function of the SDSS-V Galactic Genesis survey, the largest Milky Way Mapper program targeting red giant stars for Galactic structure studies. Treating the Galactic Genesis sample as a subsample of its 2MASS parent catalog, we model the selection function as a function of sky position, apparent H magnitude, and G-H color using a Bayesian binomial estimator, computing both a mean and maximum a posteriori (MAP) version. The resulting selection function reflects the survey's targeting strategy and observing history, including the transition from the pencil-beam SDSS-IV footprint to the fuller sky coverage of SDSS-V and the prioritization of the Magellanic Clouds. Using this selection function with the FIRE-2 Milky Way-mass simulations, we construct mock Galactic Genesis catalogs built on existing mock Gaia DR3 catalogs, injecting realistic photometric noise and applying the selection function via a per-star Bernoulli accept-reject procedure. We demonstrate the mock catalogs' utility with an example application to azimuthal metallicity variations in the disk. Furthermore, we release a Python package allowing users to recompute the selection function for their own samples and science cases. The package, selection function and mock catalogs will be updated and made available as the survey continues, extending the tools needed to reach the full scientific potential of SDSS-V Galactic Genesis.

papers.title: Post-DART impact ejecta re-accumulation on Dimorphos and implications for Hera gravity measurements
papers.summary: Context. The DART impact might have substantially modified the surface and near-surface structure of Dimorphos, affecting the morphology and gravity field that is to be measured by ESA's Hera mission. Aims. We investigate the post-impact redistribution of ejecta and its dependence on the assumed internal structure of Dimorphos. Methods. We performed high-resolution SPH simulations of the DART impact into two low-cohesion rubble-pile models, with and without a large central boulder. We followed the processes of ejecta re-accumulation and gravity evolution for six hours. Results. The impact ejects about 13% of Dimorphos's mass, most of which is re-accreted, producing near-global resurfacing. The ejecta blanket exceeds 8 m around the impact depression but is only a few tens of centimetres thick near the antipode, with similar large-scale deposition in both interior models. Local gravity changes reach about 10% of the pre-impact value. The central boulder affects the surface gravity only within the impact depression, where the removal of overlying material enhances its gravitational contribution. Conclusions. Hera will observe a surface and gravity field substantially modified by DART, which must be considered when interpreting measurements in terms of the internal structure of Dimorphos.
