papers.title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
papers.summary: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $\alpha$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.

papers.title: Multiscale dynamics in yield stress fluids during homogeneous and shear-banded yielding
papers.summary: Whether homogeneous and shear-banded yielding involve distinct microscopic mechanisms remains unresolved. We combine oscillatory rheology with gradient-resolved particle tracking to compare a ductile Carbopol microgel that yields homogeneously with a more brittle dense emulsion that develops stationary shear bands. In both systems, we separate long-range correlated ballistic flow from local Fickian diffusion and find that the two act on the same tracers, rather than on distinct persistent populations. This finding challenges the distinct-population interpretation of earlier experiments, which could access only dynamics averaged over particles and along the velocity-gradient direction. We distinguish these contributions in Carbopol by varying the tracer radius $a$ and the observation-window size $L$ independently. The ballistic velocity is independent of $a$ but increases with $L$, indicating correlations beyond the field of view; the diffusion coefficient $D$ scales as $1/a$ and is independent of $L$. At fixed driving frequency and tracer size, emulsion measurements collapse onto a single $D(\gamma_L)$ curve, whether taken across the banded profile or at fixed height under varying applied amplitude. Local strain amplitude, rather than stress, therefore governs the mean diffusive mobility within our resolution. The increase of $D$ with $\gamma_L$ is steeper than in Carbopol, consistent with the emulsion's greater brittility. Diffusive displacements are nearly Gaussian in Carbopol, with no measurable cooperativity, while in the emulsion they are strongly non-Gaussian and cooperative. There, the four-point susceptibility is largest at the strain characterising the interband region. Homogeneous and shear-banded yielding therefore share the same dynamical ingredients, while differing in the statistics and spatial organisation of the residual diffusive motion.

papers.title: Spin-phase transition in an array of quantum rings controlled by cavity photons
papers.summary: We model a spin-phase transition in a two-dimensional square array, or a lateral superlattice, of quantum rings in an external perpendicular homogeneous magnetic field. The electron system is placed in a circular cylindrical far-infrared photon cavity with a single circularly symmetric photon mode. Our numerical results reveal that the spin ordering of the two-dimensional electron gas in each quantum ring can be influenced or controlled by the electron-photon coupling strength and the energy of the photons. The Coulomb interaction between the electrons is described by a spin-density functional approach, but the para- and the diamagnetic electron-photon interactions are modeled via a configuration interaction formalism in a truncated many-body Fock-space, which is updated in each iteration step of the density functional approach. In the absence of external electromagnetic pulses this spin-phase transition is replicated in the orbital magnetization of the rings. The spin-phase transition can be suppressed by a strong electron-photon interaction. In addition, fluctuations in the spin configuration are found in dynamical calculations, where the system is excited by a time-dependent scheme specially fit for emphasizing the diamagnetic electron-photon interaction.

papers.title: Robust spin splitting and fermiology in the layered altermagnet CoNb4Se8
papers.summary: Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three-dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination-resolved micro-ARPES, fine photon-energy mapping, spin-ARPES and density functional theory, we map the three-dimensional fermiology of the layered g-wave altermagnet CoNb$_4$Se$_8$, obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H-NbSe$_2$. We resolve the spin-split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin-ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time-reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry-protected nodal $\Gamma$--K direction. We further report a weak low-temperature anomaly near $T_0\approx50$ to 60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature-dependent micro-ARPES and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum-resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

papers.title: A strictly positive lower bound on the thermodynamic cost of running a Boolean circuit
papers.summary: All digital computers implement input-output functions using logic gates connected into circuits. Different circuits computing the same function may nevertheless incur different resource costs, and circuit complexity theory studies these costs through measures such as the number of gates and the length of the longest path from input to output. Energetic cost is another important resource, however, that is typically not included among these measures. To address this, we use mismatch cost (MMC): a nonnegative contribution to the entropy production of a process that can be characterized largely independently of the detailed physical implementation of that process, providing a natural way to analyze the thermodynamic cost of Boolean circuits at an abstract, computational level. We derive an expression for the MMC of circuits composed of Boolean gates, relate it to standard complexity measures such as circuit size and depth, and use it to define mismatch cost complexity as a measure of thermodynamic resource cost. For Boolean circuits computing a non-constant Boolean function, this expression also implies a strictly positive MMC for every input distribution, and therefore a strictly positive lower bound on total entropy production. We characterize when MMC scales linearly with circuit size and when it does not, and compare the MMC of different circuit families that compute the same Boolean function. Together, these results lay the foundation for treating mismatch cost as a resource within circuit complexity theory.

papers.title: Time-reversal symmetry breaking and inherent Josephson diodes in a multi-component order parameter superconductor
papers.summary: Spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking is a defining feature of unconventional superconductivity and a prerequisite of the technologically relevant superconducting diode effect. However, its realization remains rare and exclusive to proximity-engineered weak links. Here we examine an alternative pathway to spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking by examining junctions that appear in single-crystal microstructures of the unconventional superconductor Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, lacking external superconducting proximity. We interpret the Josephson coupling as superconducting domains of a multi-component order parameter based on a plethora of anomalous effects - including a field-free Josephson diode effect, fractional Shapiro steps, magnetic interference patterns deviating from the conventional flux quantum periodicity, and bias current-programmable bistable states. These microscopic devices corroborate earlier bulk probes of time-reversal symmetry breaking, giving a renewed impulse to the long-debated pairing symmetry of Sr$_2$RuO$_4$. Our results highlight superconducting domain walls as a platform for functional Josephson devices and the study of fundamental symmetry breaking.

papers.title: Anomalous mass renormalization in two-dimensional electron systems on ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$
papers.summary: Two-dimensional electron systems (2DESs) at wide-bandgap semiconductor surfaces and interfaces are fertile ground for emergent quantum phenomena. Here, we use micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to resolve the momentum-space electronic structure of a surface 2DES in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$, an ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor with a band gap of 4.7 eV. In situ electron doping of cleaved, high-purity $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ single crystals produces an essentially circular Fermi surface. With the self-consistent Poisson-Schr\"odinger model, the 2D electrons are estimated to be confined within approximately 1.2 nm beneath the surface, with an internal electric field of approximately 18 MV cm$^{-1}$. Our analysis based on ARPES measurements reveals nearly a twofold increase in the electron mass at high sheet carrier densities. This trend deviates from the conventional behavior reported for wide-bandgap semiconductors and indicates mass renormalization beyond the conventional screening-based picture. Our results provide quantitative momentum-space benchmarks for the Fermi-surface geometry and density-dependent quasiparticle dispersion of the $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ 2DES, opening a route to studying density-tunable interfacial quantum states in the UWBG regime.

papers.title: Space-time Floquet operator: Nonreciprocity and fractional topology of space-time crystals
papers.summary: We introduce a space-time Floquet operator for crystals whose spatial and temporal translations are intertwined. Unlike the conventional Floquet operator, which describes evolution over a full time period, the space-time Floquet operator evolves the system over a fraction of the period paired with a spatial shift that generates the primitive space-time unit cell. Its eigenmode spectrum defines a space-time band structure that unfolds conventional Floquet bands to reveal the consequences of the intertwined crystal symmetry in reciprocal frequency-wavevector space. We relate the topology of these space-time bands to quantized transport phenomena, such as Bloch oscillations and adiabatic charge transport, and uncover an intrinsically fractional charge pump enabled by the primitive space-time cycle. Numerical simulations quantitatively support these predictions with small deviations controlled by the speed of the modulation. We also demonstrate how nonreciprocal parametric resonances are naturally anticipated and accurately predicted by our framework. Our approach applies broadly to both classical and quantum systems with space-time symmetry, including non-Hermitian crystals.

papers.title: Active motility and wetting cooperatively regulate liquid-liquid phase separation
papers.summary: Liquid--liquid phase separation in aqueous two-phase systems is widespread in physical and biological settings, yet how motile agents regulate its morphology and kinetics remains poorly understood. Combining experiments on \textit{Pseudomonas aeruginosa} in a dextran--polyethylene glycol mixture with hydrodynamic simulations, we show that interfacial wetting couples bacterial motility to phase-separation dynamics. At high dextran fraction, bacteria-driven rotational flows shear inter-droplet gaps and hinder liquid-bridge formation, thereby suppressing coalescence and coarsening. As the dextran fraction decreases, wetting-driven bridging becomes increasingly important, producing an intermediate chain-like state and, ultimately, branched bacterial clusters in which activity instead accelerates capture and aggregation. A biofilm-associated protein provides an independent wetting component that similarly promotes bacterial clustering. These results reveal a composition-controlled crossover between activity-induced suppression of coalescence and wetting-dominated bridging.

papers.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.summary: Analogue gravity describes sound as a field propagating on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, which is usually treated as given; in reality, however, quantum fluctuations also feed back on the medium that defines this spacetime. This raises the question of whether a condensate modified by this backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field, which has not been established so far. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, which keeps the classical background and the quantum fluctuation distinct while retaining their mutual coupling, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation still propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate, but is no longer massless: it obeys a Klein-Gordon equation with a spacetime-dependent mass that is generated by the backreaction sources in the continuity and Euler equations and cannot be absorbed into the metric. Backreaction in a Bose-Einstein condensate is thus a change of the analogue spacetime, supplemented by a mass term that has no geometric counterpart. Solving the coupled condensate-Bogoliubov dynamics for a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas quenched from a noninteracting state, we find that, while the depletion remains below $2\%$, backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered equal-point phase correlation by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to about $20\%$ near the walls, and that the bulk enhancement survives a finite-resolution imaging model.

papers.title: Altermagnetic Signatures and Topological Textures in Ultrathin Multiferroic BiFeO$_3$
papers.summary: Magnetoelectric multiferroics promise low-power switching, nonvolatile memory, and signal transduction, yet practical deployment requires ultrathin films where polar and magnetic order often degrade. Uncompensated bound charge drives depolarization in ferroelectrics, while off-stoichiometry, reduced anisotropy, and charge transfer can produce magnetic dead layers. Here, we realize a multiferroic phase of BiFeO$_3$ with no dead layer, revealing signatures of emergent altermagnetism in the ultrathin limit. First-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomic-resolution imaging, and magnetic imaging show that short-circuit electrostatic boundary conditions and epitaxial strain drive a continuous, thickness-induced phase transition accompanied by multiferroic topological textures. At four unit cells, these boundary conditions stabilize a collinear monoclinic phase with d-wave altermagnetic order, supported by magnetic circular dichroism and spin-resolved photoemission measurements. These results establish a pathway to stabilize unconventional multiferroicity at device-relevant thicknesses, reframing scaling limits for oxide electronics.

papers.title: Electric-field controlled nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect in two-dimensional time-reversal symmetric systems
papers.summary: It's established that the nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect (NANE), originating from Berry curvature near the Fermi energy, is symmetry-permitted only when the crystal symmetry in the transport plane of two-dimensional (2D) materials does not exceed a single mirror line. Here, we show that an applied direct electric field can lift this symmetry constraint, enabling an electric-field-induced NANE emerge in time-reversal symmetric 2D systems with higher crystallographic symmetries. This electric-field-induced NANE originates from two contributions: the Berry connection polarization, which roots in the electric-field-corrected Berry curvature, and the anomalous-velocity-modified nonequilibrium Fermi distribution function. Additionally, we propose an alternating temperature gradient as a driving force instead of the conventional steady one, ensuring experimental detection of NANE via second-harmonic measurement techniques. The behaviour of electric-field-induced NANE in the monolayer graphene has been theoretically and systematically investigated.

papers.title: Coulomb Interaction and Density-Independent Exciton-Scattering Processes in Atomically Thin Semiconductors
papers.summary: In quantum-kinetic approaches to the dynamics of Coulomb-bound many-body correlations such as excitons, trions, biexcitons or higher-order correlations, a detailed knowledge of the many-body Coulomb Hamiltonian serving as a starting point is important. In this manuscript, the second-quantized description of the Coulomb interaction between Bloch electrons in a Heisenberg-equation-of-motion approach in atomically thin semiconductors is derived and reviewed. Emphasis is put on a discussion of Umklapp processes and the dielectric screening including all local-field effects. A link between \textit{ab initio} methods of screening and few-band models in effective-mass approximations for the quantum kinetics is established and important Coulomb scattering processes contributing to the exciton energy landscape and density-independent exciton scattering are discussed.

papers.title: Eutectic and peritectic equilibria in coherent binary alloys
papers.summary: This work extends the Cahn--Larch\'e thermodynamic framework to binary alloys in which two coherent solid phases coexist with an incoherent liquid and investigates how coherency strain energy modifies classical eutectic and peritectic equilibria. We derive equilibrium conditions for three-phase coexistence that include an elastic energy term dependent on the molar fractions of the solid phases and apply them to model binary eutectic and peritectic systems. We find that coherency stress transforms the eutectic point into a finite three-phase equilibrium field spanning a continuous range of compositions and temperatures. In systems whose equilibrium compositions are peritectically ordered, coherency stress progressively destabilizes the two-solid equilibrium without generating a stable three-phase field and can suppress the peritectic reaction entirely. This asymmetry is governed by the geometric relationship between the compositions of the phases: when the liquid composition lies between those of the two solids (eutectic configuration), the liquid serves as a thermodynamic buffer against the coherency penalty on the solid--solid pair; when it lies outside (peritectic configuration), no such mechanism is available. These results demonstrate that coherency stress can fundamentally alter three-phase equilibria involving a liquid and suggest that such effects may be significant in systems with large coherent misfits.

papers.title: Stress Relaxation Driven by Elementary Plastic Events in Non-Ageing Liquid Foams
papers.summary: Liquid foams are archetypal athermal amorphous solids whose elasticity arises from the jamming of densely packed bubbles. We investigate the stress relaxation of non-ageing liquid foams following flow cessation, using fast X-ray tomo-rheoscopy. Thanks to in situ, time-resolved measurements, we uncover robust linear affine relationships between shear stress, plastic activity, and coordination number throughout the relaxation toward a residual stress state below the yield value. In contrast to previous studies on amorphous solids, we observe an exponential relaxation governed by the duration of individual plastic events, rather than by cascades of correlated ones associated with much longer, shear-rate-dependent timescales or power-law relaxations. Our results provide new insight into the microscopic mechanisms governing the time evolution of stress in jammed amorphous solids.

papers.title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
papers.summary: The axion insulator exhibits a topological magnetoelectric effect characterized by an axion angle $\theta=\pi$, while the time-reversal-doubled axion insulator (T-DAXI) can be viewed as two copies of an axion insulator related by time-reversal symmetry. In this work, we show that a nonsymmorphic topological crystalline insulator with glide (or screw) symmetry can host the nonsymmorphic T-DAXI phase, diagnosed by the nontrivial hourglass (screw) invariant $\delta_h=1$ ($\delta_s=1$). In this phase, the partial axion angles ($\theta^\pm=\pi $) are quantized by the glide and/or screw symmetry, and the gapped surfaces realize half-quantized quantum spin Hall states. Furthermore, we show that nonsymmorphic T-DAXIs also exhibit the spin-magnetoelectric effect. Namely, an external magnetic field can induce a topological nonlocal spin polarization in real space. When the magnetic field is time-periodic, this leads to an alternating spin current detectable in experiment. Using ab initio calculations, we demonstrate that mixed bismuth monohalides Bi4Br3I and Bi4BrI3 realize the nonsymmorphic T-DAXIs. Our findings not only reveal the symmetry-enforced T-DAXIs in nonsymmorphic topological crystalline insulators, but also demonstrate the spin-magnetoelectric effect as a detectable topological spin response in nonsymmorphic T-DAXIs.

papers.title: Orbitronics: orbit-spin interconversions for long range orbital propagation enabled by spin current
papers.summary: Orbitronics assumes long-range orbital currents, like spin currents in spintronics. However, recent theories and experiments challenge this view, showing rather local characters for orbital polarization and importance of orbit-spin conversions. In our work, angular momentum is created by ferromagnetic resonance or thermal gradients in Ni/(Pt)Ti/Au heterostructures and detected by conversion to charge current. The observed charge currents are independent of Ti thickness up to 60 nm, which is incompatible with orbital transport and Orbital Hall Effect in Ti. Instead, they depend on both Ti interfaces, evidencing spin-mediated transport in between after and before local orbit-spin interconversions.

papers.title: Coexistence of Ferromagnetic and Overscreened Kondo Effects in a Single Molecule
papers.summary: The quest for quantum ground states beyond the Fermi-liquid paradigm remains a central challenge in many-body physics. The ferromagnetic Kondo effect is an intriguing variant of the Kondo effect in which an asymptotically free spin gives rise to singular Fermi-liquid behavior. Despite its theoretical importance, this regime has eluded experimental observation owing to subtle spectroscopic signatures, small energy scales, and symmetry constraints in nanostructures. Here, we demonstrate the coexistence of ferromagnetic and overscreened Kondo effects within a molecular spin system---a triangulene dimer comprising spin-1 and spin-1/2 units adsorbed on a metal surface. Low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals signatures of singular Fermi-liquid behavior, supported by many-body calculations. The molecular design provides control over spin configuration and coupling asymmetry, allowing distinct regimes within the same platform. Our results establish a strategy for realizing non-Fermi-liquid physics at the atomic scale and demonstrate that ferromagnetic Kondo behavior can be deliberately engineered in molecular systems.

papers.title: Surface-induced vortex core restructuring in a spin-triplet superfluid
papers.summary: Observing the structure of quantized vortices can provide evidence for the pairing nature of a superfluid or superconductor and pinpoint its order parameter. Spin-triplet superfluid $^3$He supports a variety of vortices, calculated and identified so far in bulk fluid. We show numerically that the vortex core in $^3$He is strongly altered near a surface, resulting in a structure inhomogeneous along the vortex line. The effect is asymmetric with respect to the relative orientation of the core order parameter anisotropy axis and the surface normal. Coupling of spin and orbital degrees of freedom in the gradient energy of a triplet order parameter allows the surface to lift the degeneracy of two bulk vortex states connected by spontaneously broken inversion symmetry of the core. In a wide range of external conditions, the vortex structure at the surface is found to be completely different from that in bulk. As an implication, surface-limited vortex core observations in a triplet-candidate system may not reflect the bulk structure. We propose an experimental verification of the effect by measuring a transition in the vortex structure in thin slabs of superfluid $^3$He-B.

papers.title: Transport and Phase competition in three-dimensional Hubbard-Holstein model at half-filling
papers.summary: We investigate the magnetotransport properties of the one-band Hubbard-Holstein model at half-filling in three dimensions (3D) using exact diagonalization based semi-classical Monte Carlo simulations with phonons treated in the adiabatic limit. The low-temperature electronic correlation $U$ vs electron-phonon coupling $V$ phase diagram reveals two insulating phases--antiferromagnetic (AF-I) and charge-ordered (CO-I)--separated by a first-order transition, with no metallic phase observed at their intersection, indicating robustness of these phases in 3D. For $U \sim bandwidth$, the $V$ vs temperature $T$ phase diagram exhibits multiple phases including AF-I, CO-I, Mott-Hubbard insulator, bipolaronic insulator, and two bipolaronic metallic states. Several first-order transitions occur near $V \sim 3.75$. Above the ordering temperature, the density of states shows universal behavior dominated by electronic contribution, while susceptibility and DOS analyses reveal pseudogap features. Magnetic and transport properties along the phase boundary highlight strong proximity effects between competing phases, suggesting routes for tuning correlated materials and emergent electronic states.

papers.title: Non-extensive entropy of Vinen quantum turbulence
papers.summary: In Ref. [1] the statistical structure of the turbulent cascade in the context of non-additive entropy was considered. Here we suggest that the vortex line ensemble in the Vinen quantum turbulence in superfluids is described by the non-extensive Tsallis-Cirto statistics with $\delta=3$. This in particular leads to the temperature, which describes the thermodynamics of the Vinen ensemble, $T\sim mv^2$, where $v$ is the velocity of the flow and $m$ is the mass of the atom of the superfluid liquid.

papers.title: Intrinsic i-wave altermagnetism in 2D graphene superlattices
papers.summary: Altermagnets feature unconventional magnetism due to their momentum-dependent spin splitting purely driven by magnetic order, for which a variety of transition-metal-based d-wave altermagnets have been proposed. However, carbon-based altermagnets in graphene structures remain elusive, even though magnetism in graphene nanostructures has been widely demonstrated. Here, we establish a symmetry-guided design principle to engineer i-wave altermagnets in graphene antidot superlattices and demonstrate the emergence of altermagnetic states in specific monolayer and bilayer graphene superlattices. By combining first principles methods and atomistic tight binding models, we show the appearance of an interaction-induced i-wave altermagnetic splitting, stemming from the intrinsic magnetic instability of 2D graphene antidot superlattices. Our work establishes a strategy to engineer i-wave altermagnetism in a graphene platform, putting forward a carbon-based platform for altermagnetic spintronics.

papers.title: First-Order Transitions in Weak Ising Spin-Orbit-Coupled Superconductors
papers.summary: Ising spin-orbit coupling (ISOC) can strongly protect superconductivity against exchange-field-induced depairing, typically leading to critical fields far exceeding the Pauli limit and continuous (second-order) phase transitions. Here, using a free-energy approach, we demonstrate that first-order transitions can emerge in superconductors with weak ISOC under large exchange fields. In this regime, conventional theoretical approaches based on the gap equation fail to determine the thermodynamic critical field and instead yield only the supercooling field. Moreover, we identify two pronounced in-gap coherence peaks in the quasiparticle spectra, which represent the weak-ISOC manifestation of the previously reported mirage-gap states. Our results establish the importance of free-energy analysis in describing the first-order phase transitions in Ising superconductors and reveal distinct spectroscopic signatures of the weak-ISOC regime.

papers.title: Charge dynamics at nitrogen impurities and nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond
papers.summary: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is the prototype quantum defect that enables a variety of diamond-based quantum technologies. However, charge-state instability and spectral diffusion, often induced by substitutional nitrogen impurities (N$_{\rm C}$), remain key challenges for device performance. Here, we employ first-principles density functional theory calculations to quantitatively investigate nonradiative carrier capture processes mediated by multiphonon emission at both the NV center and the N$_{\rm C}$ impurity. For relevant cases, we also compute the rates of radiative and thermal emission processes. For N$_{\rm C}^0$ $\to$ N$_{\rm C}^-$, we obtain an electron capture coefficient of $2.2 \times 10^{-8}$ cm$^3$s$^{-1}$ at 300 K. Both the magnitude and temperature dependence are in excellent agreement with experimentally measured capture cross sections. Electron capture at N$_{\rm C}^+$ is even faster, with a capture coefficient of $1.0 \times 10^{-4}$ cm$^3$s$^{-1}$ at 300 K. For the NV center, we find that carrier capture rates involving only the ground states of NV$^0$ and NV$^-$ are negligibly slow. However, capture into the excited states (NV$^{0*}$ and NV$^{-*}$) is significantly faster. In particular, the capture coefficient for the hole capture process NV$^-$ $\to$ NV$^{0*}$ is as large as $1.8 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^3$s$^{-1}$ and largely temperature-independent. Hole capture at NV$^-$ will thus occur via nonradiative capture into an excited state of NV$^{0}$ followed by fast radiative decay to the NV$^0$ ground state. Similarly, electron capture at NV$^0$ will occur via the NV$^0$ $\to$ NV$^{-*}$ $\to$ NV$^-$ pathway, but with a lower nonradiative capture coefficient ($2.1 \times 10^{-9}$ cm$^3$s$^{-1}$ at 300 K). Our calculated capture coefficients and rates provide essential information for analyzing charge-state dynamics.

papers.title: Phase transitions through excited-state level crossings and topological indicators: the case of the XXZ chain with staggered Ising interaction
papers.summary: We combine two ways of determining the phase diagram of the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain with a staggered Ising interaction and uniform transverse exchange, based on exact diagonalization. The model realizes a competition between N\'eel order and bond-dimerized phases generated by the alternating Ising interaction. The simplest approach to determine the phase boundaries is to use topological indicators based on generalized position operators (GPOs). We show that in general, the bosonized and numerical results for the topological indicators agree. The second is the method of crossings of excited energy levels (MCEL), which is justified by conformal field theory. Despite the partial loss of translational symmetry induced by the alternating Ising interaction, we show that, with the aid of the GPO to identify the relevant level crossings, the MCEL provides an accurate determination of the phase boundary between the N\'eel and dimerized phases. While the jumps of a topological indicator based on a GPO provide a qualitatively correct phase diagram, its accuracy is affected when the gap is very small (or the correlation length very large) at one side of the transition, as we show using field-theoretical arguments. The combination of both methods provides a more efficient way of calculating phase diagrams for correlated one-dimensional models than other widely used conventional approaches.

papers.title: Chirality-Resolved Spectroscopy of Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon States in Multiband FeTe$_{1-x}$Se$_{x}$ Superconductors
papers.summary: We employ terahertz Faraday magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe the relaxation dynamics of quantized helical Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) states in epitaxial FeTe$_{1-x}$Se$_x$ thin films, nodeless multiband superconductors with short coherence lengths in the moderately clean limit. By exploiting polarization-selective optical transitions, we directly resolve the helicity and band origin of vortex-core quasiparticles. We observe long-lived CdGM resonances with opposite circular polarizations for electron- and hole-like bands. This enables independent, band-resolved determination of quasiparticle lifetimes, vortex masses, coherence lengths, and upper critical fields, and reveals their systematic evolution with isovalent substitution. The results establish terahertz magneto-optics as a direct probe of helical vortex-core excitations and provide dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states in iron-based superconductors.

papers.title: Why Fe doping kills photoluminescence in CsPbCl$_3$ but not in CsPbBr$_3$: Role of midgap Fe 3$d$ states and electron-phonon coupling
papers.summary: Understanding the impact of transition-metal doping on the optoelectronic properties of halide perovskite nanocrystals is essential for their rational design in photonic applications. We establish the microscopic origin of photoluminescence (PL) quenching in Fe-doped CsPbCl$_3$ using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. The emergence of Fe 3$d$ midgap states creates efficient electron-trapping centres that drive nonradiative recombination, accounting for the reduced PL intensity. Extending this analysis to Fe-doped CsPbX$_3$ (X = Cl, Br), we show experimentally that although PL intensity is suppressed in both systems relative to their pristine counterparts, their high-doping behaviour diverges: CsPbCl$_3$ becomes completely non-emissive, whereas CsPbBr$_3$ retains a finite, saturated PL intensity. Despite this contrast, electronic structure calculations reveal nearly identical midgap states in both materials, indicating that electronic effects alone cannot explain the distinct PL responses. Phonon calculations likewise fail to capture this difference. In contrast, electron-phonon coupling calculations based on the deformation potential approach reveal significantly stronger coupling in Fe-doped CsPbCl$_3$, enabling efficient dissipation of electronic excitation energy into lattice vibrations and leading to complete PL quenching. These results identify electron-phonon coupling as the key factor governing halide-dependent PL quenching and provide a unified microscopic framework for dopant-induced nonradiative processes in halide perovskites.

papers.title: The fluid-lattice gas isomorphism with application to liquid-vapor equilibrium in physisorbed monolayers
papers.summary: Liquid-gas equilibrium is described using a pair of Ising-like thermodynamic variables. The first is a combination of density and energy fields that is even under phase coexistence, derived from the Gibbs-Duhem and Clausius-Clapeyron relations. The second is the normalized density deviation $M=\rho/\rho_d-1$, which distinguishes the coexisting phases and serves as an odd ordering variable. Combining these variables with the empirical linearities of the binodal diameter and the Zeno line leads to a projective mapping between continuum-fluid and lattice-gas states. The implications of such mapping are tested against coexistence-density and saturation pressure data for the two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid, as well as physisorbed molecular monolayers of simple molecular fluids like argon and methane. Finally, a heuristic microscopic interaction-variable formulation that motivates continuous fluids versus lattice model description is also discussed.

papers.title: Geometric formulation of state-dependent Langevin dynamics using scalar free energy
papers.summary: Stochastic dynamics with state-dependent diffusion arise broadly in confined, anisotropic, and hydrodynamically coupled systems. The conventional Langevin equation contains a spurious drift associated with multiplicative noise. Since the restricted free energy is generally non-scalar, the covariance is not explicit. Here, we reformulate state-dependent Langevin dynamics using a scalar free energy and a diffusion metric defined by the inverse diffusion tensor. The conventional spurious drift is then expressed as a Christoffel contribution. Although our formulation is mathematically equivalent to the conventional one through the relation between the restricted and scalar free energies, it makes coordinate covariance explicit and enables the phenomenological construction of thermodynamic potentials directly from system symmetries. We demonstrate its consistency in representative examples of state-dependent diffusion arising from coordinate transformations, geometric confinement, and projection from curved to flat spaces.

papers.title: Open Wilson chain numerical renormalization group approach to steady-state non-equilibrium quantum transport
papers.summary: The numerical renormalization group (NRG) approach was developed to identify and quantify different equilibrium regimes of quantum impurity systems (QISs) with unprecedented accuracy by a tailored finite size representation. Out of equilibrium, the steady-state density operator is not of the Boltzmannian form but one that is determined by the imposed boundary conditions. We extend the NRG to the nonequilibrium setting by augmenting each Wilson site with a reservoir, whose coupling functions are calculated via a continuous fraction expansion in order to recover the continuum limit exactly. The nonequilibrium parameters such as a finite bias as well as a finite temperature gradient enters through the Bloch-Redfield tensor (BRT), whose zero eigenvector gives the steady-state density operator. We used the resulting open chain full density matrix (OC-FDM) approach with an effective single lead description to investigate the charge and spin transport through a quantum dot (QD) under finite bias and temperature gradient. The influence of lead asymmetry and an external magnetic field on the transport properties are also studied. For completeness, we have also investigated local properties of the QD, such as charge fluctuations and find excellent agreement with real-time quantum Monte Carlo (RT-QMC) data. The OC-FDM approach was able to explore Kondo energy scales as low as $T_K/D \approx 10^{-8}$ in the non-equilibrium regime, as well as show convergence with the established equilibrium benchmarks, such as a quantitative agreement with full density matrix numerical renormalization group (FDM-NRG) and Fermi-liquid scaling at small bias and temperature. Owing to the effective single lead description, a single OC-FDM data point takes orders of magnitude less time on a standard laptop, compared to other state-of-the-art numerical methods.

papers.title: Evaluating the Structural Basis for Polar Altermagnet Candidate Ca$_{3}$(Ru,Ti)$_{2}$O$_{7}$
papers.summary: The interplay between polar and altermagnetic orders remains largely unexplored in the broader landscape of correlated electron systems. Density functional theory (DFT) within the PBEsol + $U$ treatment propose Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ as a polar altermagnet, reliant on the transformation of the experimentally reported $Bb2_{1}m$ phase to a lower symmetry $Pn2_{1}a$ structure. Here, we perform a targeted search for the $Pn2_{1}a$ phase using synchrotron X-ray diffraction on single crystals of Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ and Ca$_{3}$(Ru$_{0.99}$Ti$_{0.01}$)$_{2}$O$_{7}$. No diffraction signature of the $Pn2_{1}a$ structure is detected down to 20 K within experimental limits. Through diffraction simulations, we translate this result into a quantitative upper bound on the symmetry breaking distortion amplitude, which we find to be significantly smaller than the DFT predicted distortion. Our DFT calculations further motivate dilute Ti substitution ($\lesssim 2\%$) as an alternative route to stabilize the low symmetry phase, for which we again find no clear evidence for this putative $Pn2_{1}a$ structure that hosts altermagnetism. Our findings indicate that PBEsol + $U$ over-stabilizes a $Pn2_{1}a$ distortion, and the measured bounds provide benchmark for future calculations. Ti substitution exceeding $\sim$3% reveals a chemically tunable polar altermagnetic phase within the $Bb2_{1}m$ structure and we theoretically demonstrate that the spin-splitting can be tuned by Ti substitution. By combining DFT, diffraction simulations and synchrotron X-ray measurements, our study demonstrates a general methodology to quantify subtle structural distortions that underlie emergent electronic and magnetic phases.

papers.title: Implications of an analysis of the shear transformation of a zone of an oblate spheroid for dislocation theory, grain boundary sliding and superplasticity
papers.summary: Grain boundary sliding models of superplastic flow take the elementary event to be the shear of an oblate-spheroidal unit embedded in a solid matrix, whose rate follows transition state theory. The mechanics of this unit, and the assumptions linking it to dislocations and macroscopic flow, have not been stated explicitly. Here the unit is analysed as an Eshelby inclusion, a continuum, mathematical treatment without using physical concepts. The analysis gives closed-form shear and volumetric energy coefficients ($0.4456$ and $0.8889$ for aspect ratio $1/2$ and Poisson ratio $1/3$) and shows that the shear stress of the unit is a force dipole, decaying as $r^{-3}$ and changing sign with direction, unlike a dislocation. The inputs, assumptions and proposals needed to connect this unit of shear to dislocation theory and superplastic flow are then stated and classed as experimentally validated, physically realistic or fitting constants. Under three such proposals, a row of about four units acquires the Peierls-Nabarro profile of a full dislocation, and two to three units that of a Shockley partial; the Peierls and Frank-Read stresses and the stacking-fault energy then follow from experimental inputs. With the unit energy as the free energy of activation and strains fitted to superplastic data, the flow law reproduces all 52 measured strain rates of a Cu alloy within an order of magnitude. Molecular-dynamics calculations for Cu outline the extension to dislocation emission, mesoscopic grain boundary sliding and the inverse Hall-Petch effect. This gives phenomenological models of superplastic flow a mechanical basis.

papers.title: Interlayer Phase Locking and Sliding Select Topological Melting Channels in Superconducting Bilayers
papers.summary: Topological transitions in coupled superconducting layers are intertwined: an elementary vortex in one layer carries both common and relative phase winding. We study a Josephson-coupled bilayer in an in-plane magnetic field using renormalization-group analysis and Monte Carlo simulations of the compact layer phases. The field drives Pokrovsky--Talapov (PT) entry of interlayer solitons, and free-energy calculations in fixed soliton sectors show PT square-root scaling over the sampled densities at finite temperature. Interlayer phase locking and sliding then select distinct Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT)-like melting channels. The locked commensurate phase melts through same-vorticity layer pairs when the geometric-mean common helicity modulus $\Upsilon_{+,g}$ reaches $T/(2\pi)$, with layer correlation exponent $\eta_l=1/4$. A stable sliding incommensurate phase melts through elementary layer vortices on a line of BKT fixed points, where $\Upsilon_{+,g}+\Upsilon_{-,g}=2T/\pi$ and $\eta_l$ is set by the ratio of the relative and common moduli. When the relative helicity modulus is identified with the relative-phase stiffness, our simulations agree with this prediction, and the common superfluid stiffness at incommensurate melting is nearly twice its value at commensurate melting. Near soliton entry, however, the dilute sliding state is unstable to opposite-vorticity layer pairs. Our results connect PT soliton entry with field-tunable BKT-like melting and identify the pair-stability condition that links them.

papers.title: Absence of hidden analytic conserved quantities in harmonically confined rods
papers.summary: Systems of hard rods of equal length in a one-dimensional harmonic trap have been observed to exhibit peculiar non-ergodic behavior that might suggest the existence of a novel hidden conserved quantity beyond the two well known ones, i.e., the total energy and the center-of-mass energy. In this work, we investigate this possibility by systematically constraining the forms of the conserved quantities, and we rigorously rule out the existence of any extra hidden conserved quantity that is analytic in the positions and momenta of the rods involved. We do so by showing two key results: conservation during free motion demands the $U(1)$ invariance of these quantities under rotations of the position and momenta of each rod, and conservation during collisions demand an $S_N$ invariance under the permutation of the momenta of the rods as long as one of the rods have non-zero length. We then show that these conditions imply that any conserved quantity is functionally dependent on the two known conserved quantities. In addition, we show that in the special case where all rods have zero length (i.e., when they are point particles), conservation under collisions only requires invariance under a smaller $S_N$ group of permutations of the labels of the rods, which leads to a much larger set of analytic conserved quantities that we explicitly write down. In all, this rigorously clarifies the structure of conserved quantities in the hard rod problem, and motivates the application of such systematic methods to other classical systems.

papers.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
papers.summary: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($\pi/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). The proposed architecture is fundamentally robust against multiphoton leakage sidebands, offering a thermally immune, high-speed alternative to conventional semiconductor static spin transistors.

papers.title: Raman Signatures of Lithium Ion Dynamics in LLZO Garnet Electrolytes: Atomistic Insights from MD-Raman Calculations
papers.summary: Lithium lanthanum zirconate (LLZO) garnets are among the most promising solid electrolytes for next-generation batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity, chemical stability, and compatibility with lithium metal. Raman spectroscopy is commonly employed to distinguish the highly conductive cubic phase from the poorly conductive tetragonal phase of LLZO, yet the atomistic origin of these spectral differences and their direct connection to Li-ion transport remain unresolved. Here, we close this gap by comparing computed and experimental Raman spectra for the tetragonal, cubic, and Ta-doped variants of LLZO, with the computed spectra obtained from the MD-Raman approach that combines machine-learning molecular dynamics with first-principles polarizability calculations. We show that the contrasting ionic transport behavior across these LLZO variants is encoded in the vibrational dynamics of the lithium sublattice and gives rise to distinct features in their Raman spectra. A symmetry-resolved analysis further reveals that experimentally observed Raman peaks do not correspond to individual normal modes, but instead arise from overlapping contributions of multiple symmetry channels, challenging conventional peak-assignment approaches. By explicitly connecting experimentally accessible Raman signatures to the underlying atomic-scale dynamics, our results show how Raman spectroscopy can move beyond empirical phase identification toward a microscopic probe of Li-ion dynamics in lithium garnet electrolytes.

papers.title: The crossmetric tensor and the geometrical meaning of the imaginary numbers
papers.summary: The product of two Cartesian quaternions can be written as a quadratic form based on a 4x4 matrix made of the imaginary numbers i,j,k introduced by Hamilton. We generalized this matrix to non-Cartesian bases, and showed that the matrix is made of the metric and the cross tensors. We called it crossmetric tensor. Its symbols are ia,ib,ic; they are the elementary crystallographic quaternions. We determined the crossmetric tensors for the six crystal families. We also showed that any unit crystallographic quaternion can be geometrically represented by an infinity of pairs of oriented planes intersecting along the vectorial component of the quaternion such that the angle between them is the semiangle of the rotation. The composition of quaternions follows the intuitive source-target rule. The elementary quaternions ia,ib,ic are geometrically represented by pair of perpendicular and oriented planes intersecting along the axis a,b,c, respectively. Three other complementary quaternions were also introduced. They are the pairs of planes ma, mb, mc. The elementary quaternions follow Hamilton rules on the squares of imaginary numbers. The complementary quaternions follow Hamilton rules on the bi and tri-products. For Cartesian basis, the quaternions i,j,k appear as a specific case of crystallographic quaternions. They are formed by the pairs of perpendicular faces of the cube mx, my, mz.

papers.title: Real-Time FPGA-Based Multi-Parameter Feedback Stabilization of a Silicon Double Quantum Dot
papers.summary: Long term operation of semiconductor spin qubits requires active stabilization of quantum dot potentials against low-frequency charge noise. To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $\mu$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency. This effectively suppresses low-frequency 1/f noise, maintaining device stability over longer time periods, and potentially enables real-time control in large-scale quantum dot arrays.

papers.title: A closed-form theory of charge-regulated electrostatic interactions between anisotropically charged spheres
papers.summary: Proteins and many other colloids carry ionizable surface groups that are both spatially inhomogeneous (patchy) and pH-responsive (charge-regulating). In the description of the electrostatic interactions between such particles, these two aspects are often treated separately, especially from a theoretical perspective. We present a unified, closed-form theory that unites charge regulation and patchiness within the linearized Poisson--Boltzmann approximation. For spherical particles with anisotropic distributions of titratable sites, we derive both the leading-order mean-field interaction energy as well as the Kirkwood--Shumaker fluctuation interaction. The theory exposes a qualitatively new effect between two electroneutral anisotropic particles: proximity-induced charge regulation generates a net monopole, and splits orientational branches that are {mirror-symmetric} in any linear fixed-charge model. The accompanying correction to the interaction energy has no fixed sign---it weakens like-charge repulsion but can deepen an existing attraction or create one where fixed charge predicts none. We benchmark three components of the theory against published results, as no existing simulation probes their combination, which would capture the central prediction of the theory. Lastly, we apply the theory to two proteins---lysozyme and $\alpha$-chymotrypsinogen A---and show that it not only reproduces the general trends of the measured second virial coefficients but also predicts how charge regulation expands the range of pH and screening strength where the protein--protein interaction is attractive.

papers.title: Gap-controlled thermalization in a chain of alternating nonlinear springs: an SSH model version of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou problem
papers.summary: In classical anharmonic lattices, the resonance structure driving nonlinear mode mixing is reshaped by band gaps. However, it remains unclear whether a spectral gap hinders or promotes long-time thermalization. Here we study a Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT) chain of equal masses joined by alternating dimensionless spring constants $1\pm\Delta\kappa$, so that the chain is dimerized with strength $\Delta\kappa$, the classical vibrational analogue of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, and quantify how the acoustic-optical gap controls relaxation under $\alpha$-type (cubic) nonlinearity. Tracking modal energies and spectral entropy via long-time symplectic simulations, we find that dimerization delays long-time relaxation. At $\Delta\kappa=1/2$, set by the onset of the first umklapp process that allows two zone-boundary acoustic phonons to fuse into a zone-center optical phonon, the three-wave acoustic-acoustic-optical channel closes. The effective acoustic-to-optical scattering rate reveals an interplay between the dynamic resonance vertex and the kinematic resonance manifold, which evolve differently with the dimerization parameter. Above the threshold $\Delta\kappa=1/2$, energy redistribution can nevertheless continue through higher-order resonances and quasiresonances. Yet specific boundary conditions and initial conditions can inhibit equipartition. These results identify the phononic gap as a tunable, momentum-selective filter for nonlinear energy transport, suggesting a general route to controlling energy transfer and equipartition in dimerized or topologically gapped nonlinear lattices and in flexible mechanical systems.

papers.title: Dimensional Control of Excitonic Interactions in Exfoliated 2D Molecular Crystals
papers.summary: Excited states in molecular crystals depend on intermolecular coupling, charge-transfer interactions, dielectric screening and molecular packing. How reduced dimensionality modifies these interactions when molecular packing structure is preserved remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that tetracene and three other molecular crystals can be mechanically exfoliated into mono-, few- or multilayer flakes, exploiting the top-down approach established for inorganic layered materials. Electron diffraction confirms that exfoliated tetracene retains long-range crystalline order and nearly bulk-like in-plane lattice parameters. This structural fidelity enables systematic thickness-dependent spectroscopy with limited changes in molecular packing. With decreasing thickness, the Davydov splitting diminishes, whereas the Stokes shift increases to nearly three times its bulk-like value, indicating enhanced excited-state relaxation. The photoluminescence 0-0/0-1 intensity ratio also rises, suggesting greater exciton delocalization. Compared with exfoliated tetracene, assembly-grown crystals exhibit lattice contraction and larger Davydov splitting. Analysis within the Frenkel-charge-transfer mixing framework qualitatively accounts for the Davydov-state energy shifts and splitting in terms of molecular packing, intermolecular coupling and dielectric screening. Our results show that intermolecular interactions, excited-state relaxation and exciton coherence can be systematically tuned by varying layer number, demonstrating the feasibility and utility of extending dimensional control of inorganic 2D materials to molecular crystals.

papers.title: Thermal Stability of Encapsulated Molecular Structures with Extended OH-Hydrogen-Bond Chains
papers.summary: Using a coarse-grained model, we performed numerical simulations of the dynamics of linear molecular chains adsorbed on a flat substrate (on the surface of an h-BN crystal). It is shown that molecules containing benzene rings and hydroxyl groups in their structure can form stable hydrogen-bond chains OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$OH. Such chains can be formed by phenol C$_6$H$_5$OH, 4-phenylphenol C$_6$H$_5$--C$_6$H$_4$OH, paracetamol CH$_3$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH, and 4-hydroxybenzanilide C$_6$H$_5$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH molecules. The dissociation of these chains occurs at temperatures above $T_1$=160, 210, 300, and 390K, respectively. Coating such molecular systems with a hexagonal boron nitride sheet (van der Waals encapsulation) significantly enhances their thermal stability. Such encapsulated molecular structures retain hydrogen-bond chains up to temperatures of $T_2$=510, 860, 600, and 1260K, respectively. The performed simulations allow us to conclude that chains of these molecules encapsulated by h-BN sheets can be used to create anhydrous proton-exchange membranes capable of operating at high temperatures. The most promising are chains of 4-hydroxybenzanilide molecules, since their hydrogen-bond chains possess the highest thermal stability.

papers.title: Towards a Metal-Organic Framework with Pore-Confined Electrons
papers.summary: Electrides are an unconventional class of materials in which electrons are localized in crystallographic void spaces rather than solely around atomic nuclei, giving rise to appealing properties such as low work functions, strong electron-donating character, and even superconductivity. Here, we use ab initio methods to investigate metal-organic framework (MOF) electrides, a new class of materials that combines the interstitial electrons of electrides with the permanent porosity and chemical tunability of MOFs. These materials host pore-confined electrons: occupied electronic states localized in the pore space and with bands slightly below or crossing through the Fermi level. Using density functional theory calculations, we establish several design rules for stabilizing pore-confined electrons in MOFs via an anion-electron exchange process and identify candidate MOF electrides. As a proof-of-concept, we also demonstrate that the pore-confined electrons can directly facilitate chemical reactions, substantially lowering the activation barrier for H2 dissociation without requiring adsorption at a surface site. We envision that pore-confined electrons in nanoporous materials may enable a fundamentally new type of catalysis in which chemical reactions take place in the pore space, driven by electron-centered active sites.

papers.title: Disentangling spin polarization from driven circular ionic motion in EuTiO$_3$
papers.summary: Coherently driven circular ionic motion has been reported to produce large helicity-dependent optical responses attributed to transient magnetization. However, the microscopic nature and magnitude of this phenomenon, sometimes referred to as dynamical multiferroicity, remain strongly debated. Here, we directly study the connection between ionic circulation induced by a high-field circular terahertz (THz) drive and its effect on the spin system of EuTiO$_3$ using X-rays. This material exhibits an optical response consistent with the putative magnetic signal observed in related non-magnetic materials. Furthermore, the presence of Eu$^{2+}$ ions enables the use of X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) to test for the creation of transient spin polarization. Simultaneously, ultrafast X-ray diffraction (XRD) measures the circular ionic motion from which we determine the mechanical angular momentum. We find a classical ionic contribution of $3\times10^{-8}~\mu_B$ from XRD and upper limits of $0.03~\mu_B$ and $0.11~\mu_B$ from the sensitivity of XMCD at the europium $M_5$ and $L_2$ edges, probing the $4f$ and $5d$ shells of Eu$^{2+}$, respectively. These observations show that large-amplitude circular ionic motion in this system is not accompanied by a detectable spin polarization despite the clear signature in the optical data, with the XMCD upper bounds and classical contribution differing by many orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Toward catalyst-mediated growth of diamond and cubic boron nitride wires
papers.summary: Sustained catalyst-mediated growth of diamond and cubic boron nitride (cBN) wires has yet to be established reproducibly, although related methods produce carbon and BN nanotubes and many elemental and compound nanowires. I hypothesize that a retained contact between a catalyst and an existing tetrahedral crystal can sustain wire extension under conditions that do not nucleate that crystal on an otherwise comparable unseeded catalyst. The prediction is repeated, vapor-derived target-phase extension during an interval in which matched unseeded contacts do not nucleate that phase. I develop tests using diamond seeds, SiC starter wires and cBN seeds, separating the conditions used to establish the contact from those used for continuation. Worked estimates distinguish bulk precipitation driving forces from sidewall costs and show why increased carbon activity alone cannot select diamond over graphite. Comparisons with established synthesis identify the roles of pressure, hydrogen and activated nitrogen that must be retained or replaced. Isotope tracing, local structural measurements and time-dependent growth distinguish continued incorporation from seed consumption, conversion and etching. Nanometer, micrometer and larger wires could provide electrically insulating thermal connections, mechanical probes and reinforcing filaments.

papers.title: Designing Strongly Correlated Quantum Phases of Matter with Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States
papers.summary: Materials design is an inverse problem: finding the couplings of a microscopic Hamiltonian whose ground state exhibits a desired property. For strongly correlated quantum systems, this remains largely out of reach, as each candidate Hamiltonian requires its own costly simulation. Here we show that Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States, single wave functions that encode the ground states of an entire family of Hamiltonians, make this search efficient. Because the Hamiltonian couplings enter as neural-network inputs, any ground-state property can be optimized by gradient descent directly in coupling space. We use this approach to search for nonmagnetic phases in two-dimensional spin models in coupling spaces of increasing dimensionality. Specifically, we focus on quantum spin liquids, exotic phases of matter in which quantum fluctuations prevent magnetic order at zero temperature. In the largest search space considered, spanned by eight superexchange couplings and containing many paradigmatic frustrated spin systems, the optimization converges to the $J_1$-$J_2$-$\delta$ Heisenberg model when starting from a magnetic phase. We show that the ground state at the optimum set of couplings has neither magnetic nor valence-bond order in the thermodynamic limit, leading to a new quantum spin-liquid candidate. The approach is completely general and can be extended to other models and physical properties to optimize, demonstrating that Neural-Network Quantum States are tools not only for simulating quantum matter but also for designing it.

papers.title: Splicing an exact local self-energy into $GW$: tests on small Hubbard clusters
papers.summary: $GW$+DMFT-type schemes replace the local part of a $GW$ self-energy by a separately computed local self-energy. A causal double counting removes a non-causal term from the hybridization (Lee and Haule, 2017), but the resulting total self-energy has been flagged as not guaranteed to be causal (Zhu and Chan, 2021). From the Herglotz representation, the spliced self-energy is causal if and only if its spectral measure is positive semi-definite. For translation-invariant single-band systems this becomes a momentum-resolved bound: the local weight may fall short of the local $GW$ weight by at most the momentum minimum of the $GW$ weight. On finite clusters, a mismatch between $GW$ and exact poles generically produces indefinite residues. On the Matsubara axis, a negative damping eigenvalue at one frequency certifies non-causality; passing does not establish causality. We examine these diagnostics in an idealized setting, not self-consistent $GW$+DMFT: one-shot $GW$ on the exact Green's function of small Hubbard clusters with the exact local self-energy inserted. At all 528 parameter sets, our computed $GW$ and exact self-energies pass both tests, as expected. The splice fails the pointwise test at 54 points, none at half filling, all at the lowest Matsubara frequency, and already at $U/t=0.5$; there the local $GW$ damping is 1.3-9 times the exact one. A block Pick test on eight frequencies, run with a second imaginary-time code, flags 481 of the 528 sets; for the other 47 it is inconclusive. Moment checks miss all of these, because the spliced high-frequency moment is exact. The Dyson Green's function is then non-causal too, yet passes the pointwise test everywhere tested. This version replaces a withdrawn one whose reported causality violations of $GW$ itself came from a sign error in the polarization; with the sign corrected, the computed $GW$ shows the expected positivity.

papers.title: Nontrivial topological properties from the cooperation of static perturbations and Floquet fields in type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
papers.summary: In this work, we present a comprehensive theoretical study for the topological and anomalous transport properties of type-II SDSMs under three scenarios, i.e., static symmetry-breaking perturbations, periodic Floquet driving by two-frequency orthogonally polarized light (TFOPL), and their cooperative effects in the hybrid scenario. We first show that a static mass $m_z$ opens a bulk gap and drives the system into a Chern insulator with Chern number $C^{\rm per}=\pm 2\,{\rm sgn}(m_z)$. In comparison, TFOPL alone only shifts the positions of Dirac points and cannot open a full gap. Nevertheless, it produces a Berry curvature odd in the $x$-direction, yielding a finite Berry curvature dipole (BCD) along $x$ proportional to the sine of the initial phase, while the $y$-component vanishes. The hybrid scenario, by contrast, exhibits a remarkably rich phenomenology. Specifically, its gap-closure criterion becomes cubic and thus admits up to three real roots when the effective parameter along the $x$-direction is negative, thereby producing multiple light-tunable gap-closing points and a series of topological phase transitions. In particular, the BCD exhibits a double-peak structure with strong enhancement near gap-closing manifolds and synchronized sign reversal of the full vector under external tuning. We further analyze the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC), and anomalous thermal Hall conductivity (ATHC). The AHC and ATHC exhibit quantized plateaus that serve as signatures of Chern-insulator phases, while the ANC, being a Fermi-surface probe, provides complementary local information and can identify light-induced gaps even when global topological invariants remain unchanged. Taken together, these results offer useful insights into the topological properties of 2D type-II SDSMs and related systems.

papers.title: Skin phase transition of a skyrmion in a ferromagnetic superfluid
papers.summary: Compared with a scalar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), a spinor BEC supports richer phenomena because of its internal spin degrees of freedom, including topological solitons such as domain walls or skyrmions. Here, we theoretically reveal three distinct axisymmetric soliton structures formed as a circular domain wall in a spin-1 BEC, connected within fixed winding numbers. We refer to these structures as the broken-axisymmetry (BA)-skin, antiferromagnetic (AF)-skin and normal-core phases. Their occurrence is controlled by the two dimensionless parameters in the absence of linear Zeeman coefficient $p=0$: $q/\mu$, the ratio of the quadratic Zeeman coefficient to the chemical potential, and $c_s/c_n$, the ratio of spin interaction to the density interaction. The BA-skin and AF-skin phases exhibit local easy-plane magnetic order and local easy-plane spin-nematic order, respectively, while the normal-core phase is similar to a doubly quantized vortex analogous to that of a scalar BEC with a density depletion at the center. We obtain semi-analytical estimates of selected transition boundaries separating these phases by analyzing the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equation and also numerically confirm them by solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. We estimate the skyrmion radius using a hydrostatic approximation and compare the result with numerical solutions. We envision our results on skyrmions in a spin-1 BEC can trigger further investigation on novel soliton structures in a magnetic superfluid.

papers.title: Coherent Phonon Generation from Prethermal Carrier Populations in a Semiconductor
papers.summary: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. Fitting this model to the data yields an excited transition state lifetime of a few femtoseconds. These results identify transition selectivity, rather than a thermalized total carrier density, as a key factor controlling coherent-phonon generation in semiconductors excited near a band gap.

papers.title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
papers.summary: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. However, a new {\em current-gradient-induced} torque emerges in nanoscale geometries. For a series of Ni-based bilayers, the computed Ni thickness dependence of the current-gradient-induced torque is in quantitative agreement with measurements previously attributed to orbital torques. We discuss how this opens a new avenue for the electrical control of magnetic orders, possibly also including the N\'eel vector of metallic altermagnets.

papers.title: Symmetry-selected extreme shear compliance in a stable carbon monolayer
papers.summary: Extreme stiffness contrasts between loading modes usually require architected metamaterials with compliant hinges, whereas covalent crystals rarely exhibit such behavior intrinsically. Here, density functional theory calculations of the complete in-plane elastic tensors of four tetragonal carbon monolayers reveal a more than 50-fold spread in shear stiffness, despite less than a twofold variation in axial stiffness and the same symmetry-allowed tensor form. Twin T-graphene shows the strongest contrast: its shear constant, $C_{66}=3.03$~N m$^{-1}$, is 47 times smaller than in graphene and yields a shear Kelvin eigenvalue 29 times below the two normal-strain eigenvalues, while the Born stability criteria hold. This shear constant revises an earlier inference of elastic isotropy based on normal strains alone. Constrained relaxations and symmetry-resolved mode analysis identify the mechanism as a $B_{2g}$ counter-torsion of the carbon sublayers about the mid-plane bonds, which removes 96.3% of the clamped-ion shear stiffness with bond-length changes below 0.15%. An internal-coordinate model quantifies this cancellation, identifying internal relaxation, rather than weak bonding, as the origin of the soft channel. The resulting anisotropy predicts transverse sound velocities of 1.95 km s$^{-1}$ along [100] and 10.62 km s$^{-1}$ along [110], a testable acoustic signature. Phonon calculations, ab initio molecular dynamics at 300 K, and large-deformation simulations indicate that the soft channel is dynamically stable, preserves the local bonding, and persists beyond the harmonic regime. Our results show how bonding topology enables extreme mode-selective elasticity through internal relaxation in a mechanically stable covalent crystal.

papers.title: Reticulating Local Dynamics in Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.summary: In covalent organic frameworks (COFs), the geometry of the building units predetermines the structure of the framework, yet comparable design principles relating the COF linkers to the local motions that govern guest adsorption and diffusion as well as mechanical response have remained beyond reach. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (PDF) analysis with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations accelerated by machine learning interatomic potentials to resolve and compare the local dynamics of two three-dimensional imine-linked COFs, chosen to differ in the geometry and rigidity of one of their two building units. Both are constructed from the same 4-connected square planar linker, $4,4',4'',4'''$-(pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetrayl)tetraaniline (PyTTA), reticulated with the 12-connected nanographene hexakis{[3,5-bis($p$-formylphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]}hexabenzocoronene to give COF-412, {[(HBC-LA$_{12}$)(PyTTA)$_3$]}$_{\mathit{imine}}$, and with the 6-connected triptycene 2,3,6,7,14,15-hexakis(4-formylphenyl)triptycene to give COF-564, {[(Trip-CHO)$_2$(PyTTA)$_3$]}$_{\mathit{imine}}$. The PDF-MD approach resolves the amplitude, the time scale, and the spatial extent of the motion of all COF linkers, separating the limited libration of the fused aromatic cores from the larger reorientational tilts of the pendant aryl rings they carry and from the translation of whole linkers within the net. The simulations further reveal that exchanging the nanographene- for the triptycene-based linker tunes the equilibrium tilt and the positional probability density of PyTTA, raising the tilt amplitude of its linker partner, and, notably, strengthens the coupling between the translations of neighbouring linkers. This approach provides a blueprint for understanding local dynamical properties in COFs, and shows them to be selectable through the choice of building unit and amenable to design.

papers.title: Random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains revisited
papers.summary: We revisit the spin-reduction transition in the random spin-$3/2$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain using the tensor-network strong-disorder renormalization group (tSDRG). The predicted transition separates two random-singlet (RS) phases: one formed by effective spin-$1/2$ moments at weaker disorder and the other by full spin-$3/2$ moments at stronger disorder. Within the Damle--Huse classification, this transition corresponds to an emergent permutation-symmetric $P_4$ multicritical point on a $P_2$ critical line associated with the RS phases. We first derive the critical exponents governing the disorder-averaged bulk and end-to-end correlation functions in the $P_n$ universality classes within the Damle--Huse framework. Using these theoretical predictions, together with a diagnostic constructed from the mean and variance of the energy-gap distribution, we identify the $P_4$ transition point and the reentrant behavior of the RS phase.
