papers.title: ADReasoner: Acoustic-Linguistic Cue-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Explainable Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Speech
papers.summary: Speech-based Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection holds significant promise due to its scalable and non-invasive nature. However, current Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs), similar to conventional AD detection systems, still treat AD detection primarily as a simple categorical classification task. This paradigm provides limited interpretability of predictions, while leaving the inherent expressiveness and reasoning capabilities of SpeechLLMs largely underutilized. In this work, we take the first step toward reframing AD detection as a deep reasoning task via Reinforcement Learning (RL). We propose ADReasoner, an RL-enhanced SpeechLLM designed to generate accurate diagnostic predictions with interpretable rationales grounded in fine-grained acoustic-linguistic cues. To achieve this, we first systematically construct ADCoT-7K, an AD speech reasoning dataset combining real data and our quality-filtered synthetic data, where each instance features Chain-of-Thought (CoT) annotations and detailed captions. Second, observing the weak perception of AD-related acoustic-linguistic cues in current SpeechLLMs, we leverage Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to develop a cue-perception-enhanced foundation model, ADReasoner-Base, thereby improving AD speech understanding. Third, alongside two standard rule-based rewards, we introduce a reasoning reward and a reasoning-label consistency reward into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for RL. Furthermore, a shrinkage mechanism is employed to suppress misleading reasoning signals, while a gating mechanism progressively introduces both rewards to stabilize policy training. Experiments on three AD datasets (Pitt, PROCESS-1, PROCESS-2) demonstrate that ADReasoner outperforms previous state-of-the-art models in both detection performance and explanation quality, advancing AD detection toward interpretable reasoning from speech.

papers.title: Fading Suppression in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Using Frequency-Domain Replica Reconstruction and Noise-Whitened Principal Component Combining
papers.summary: Frequency-selective Rayleigh fading in distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (phi-OTDR) calls for effective diversity, but existing rotated-vector-sum (RVS) combining of nonoverlapping subbands incurs a spatial-resolution penalty. In this letter, we propose frequency-domain replica reconstruction and noise-whitened principal component combining (PCC) that combines a full-band replica and overlapping subbands using fixed weights estimated across probing periods after whitening correlated replica noise. This approach retains wider subbands and reduces reliance on noisy first-period alignment, balancing diversity with nominal spatial resolution. Experiments over approximately 7.1 km of fiber with 16-microsecond linear frequency-modulated (LFM) pulses recover 500-Hz vibrations with reduced background phase excursions and a 2.46-2.76-dB improvement in the vibration-to-background ratio (VBR) over the first-period RVS.

papers.title: Semantic-Aware Deformable Feature Alignment for Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound
papers.summary: Accurate segmentation of thyroid nodules in ultrasound images is essential for clinical diagnosis yet remains challenging due to boundary ambiguity, speckle noise, and complex geometric variability. Existing methods often fail to reconcile global semantic understanding with precise local boundary delineation, leading to errors in irregular cases. To address this, we propose SDFA-Net, a framework built on semantic-aware deformable feature alignment that explicitly decouples the learning of robust global semantics and detailed local geometry. Our approach integrates three main components: a clustered linear context aggregation module for efficient long-range dependency modeling, an affinity-driven token modulation mechanism using dynamic prototypes to suppress background interference, and a cascaded spatially-aligned feature fusion strategy that achieves sub-pixel geometric alignment across multiple resolution stages. By filtering and aligning multi-scale features, SDFA-Net ensures robust fusion that is both semantically meaningful and geometrically accurate. We validate our method through extensive experiments on three public thyroid ultrasound datasets, TN3K, TUCC, and DDTI, where it demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework offers a generalizable solution for precise medical image segmentation in boundary-ambiguous scenarios.

papers.title: RIS-Assisted Downlink Pinching-Antenna Systems With NLOS Environments
papers.summary: This paper investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted downlink pinching-antenna system (PASS) in the presence of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) users caused by unavoidable obstacles. An RIS is deployed to extend the coverage of the physically constrained PASS by establishing virtual line-of-sight (LOS) links. To improve system performance, we propose a zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming-based alternating optimization (AO) framework that minimizes the transmit power by jointly optimizing the RIS reflection coefficients and pinching-antenna (PA) activation positions. Specifically, the RIS reflection coefficients are optimized using the Riemannian conjugate gradient (RCG) method, while a novel projected gradient-based method is developed to efficiently optimize the PA activation positions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AO framework outperforms baseline schemes in terms of both transmit power and computational efficiency under different system configurations including the rate requirements and RIS sizes.

papers.title: Synergizing Wireless Foundation Models and LLMs: A Multi-Task Framework for MA Systems
papers.summary: While movable antennas (MAs) provide enhanced spatial flexibility through dynamic repositioning, they confront critical challenges in acquiring complete channel state information (CSI) and efficiently optimizing antenna positions. Encouragingly, wireless foundation models (WFMs) capture generalizable channel priors for high-quality CSI extrapolation, while large language models (LLMs) enable parameter-efficient, token-level optimization for wireless tasks. In this paper, we synergistically integrate a WFM and an LLM into a multi-task framework for MA systems. First, to address the mismatch between existing WFM pre-training and MA channel characteristics, we develop an MA-oriented ``ExtLWM'' based on the large wireless model (LWM) architecture. Second, we design a unified ExtLWM-Connector-LLM architecture that flexibly adapts to different MA configurations without structural redesign. Third, we reformulate discrete MA positioning as a sequential decision-making problem, where candidate positions are represented by numerical tokens and optimized using group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to exploit the serial generation capability of the LLM. Finally, a multi-stage training strategy is developed to maintain multi-task performance under limited training samples while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Simulation results show that ExtLWM can produce high-quality channel embeddings while outperforming various benchmarks in CSI extrapolation. Meanwhile, the proposed LLM-based approach achieves a favorable trade-off between performance and computational complexity.

papers.title: Recursive Neighbor Pruning: Decentralized Community Detection with Certified Behavior from Saturated Opinion Dynamics
papers.summary: Detecting communities, i.e., groups of densely connected nodes, usually requires a central entity that knows the whole network. We study Recursive Neighbor Pruning (RNP), a fully decentralized alternative inspired by social learning. Each agent holds a private opinion but only shows its neighbors a coarse public action, namely its opinion amplified and clipped to a fixed range. Agents repeatedly move their opinion toward the actions of their neighbors and, once opinions settle, drop the links with neighbors whose action has the opposite sign. Repeating this procedure on the remaining network splits it into communities, without any agent knowing the network or the number of communities. We use tools from nonlinear control to characterize this behavior. We show that splitting requires the amplification to exceed a threshold set by how strongly the network is bottlenecked. We also show that a group in which every member has enough of its links inside the group can no longer be split once its members agree, and that a single run separates such groups exactly when started from suitable opinions. Finally, we bound the number of runs and messages. On two standard families of synthetic networks, RNP is as accurate as the best centralized method as long as each node has fewer than about forty percent of its links outside its community, and it fails close to the value predicted by our analysis. It is more accurate than two decentralized competitors below this level, but exchanges many more messages.

papers.title: Optimal Steady-State Regulation of Nonlinear Systems: A Feedback Optimization Approach
papers.summary: This paper studies the optimal steady-state regulation problem for a class of nonlinear systems. The regulated output is required to track a trajectory that minimizes a steady-state cost depending on both the output and the exo-system. To characterize the desired steady-state behavior, we introduce a generalized regulator equation and develop a two-layer framework. The optimization layer generates the optimal reference online through a steady-state generator combined with gradient-feedback optimization dynamics, while the control layer employs backstepping to stabilize the plant and achieve the desired optimal steady-state regulation. Under suitable immersion and minimum-phase assumptions, global asymptotic stability is established.

papers.title: AV-QTSS: Class-Query Target Sound Spatialization in Multi-Source 360$^\circ$ Videos
papers.summary: Spatial audio is central to immersive 360$^\circ$ media, yet existing audio-visual spatialization renders the scene as a whole, leaving no control over an individual source. We introduce Audio-Visual Query-conditioned Target Sound Spatialization (AV-QTSS): given a monaural multi-source mixture, a 360$^\circ$ video and a class query from the 13-class DCASE sound-event ontology, it generates the first-order Ambisonics (FOA) signal of the queried source alone. The omnidirectional mixture contains no explicit spatial cues, so direction has to be inferred from the video, where several objects may sound at once. We propose a query-conditioned dense binding localizer that predicts a spherical probability map over the whole scene, coupled to the renderer so both are optimized jointly. Experiments with one to four concurrent sources show improved localization and spatial accuracy relative to established methods and ablated variants, and the localizer transfers to real 360$^\circ$ recordings after adaptation.

papers.title: In-Context Adapter Generation for Compositional Generalization in Large Audio Language Models
papers.summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance on standard speech and audio understanding tasks, yet their ability to systematically generalize to novel task compositions remains underexplored. Taking a meta-learning view, we extend Text-to-LoRA (T2L) to LALMs, generating instruction-conditioned LoRA adapters with a Transformer hypernetwork rather than learning a single fixed adapter shared across instructions. To exploit fine-grained task information, we introduce in-context adapter generation (ICAG), a token-level hypernetwork architecture; we call the resulting method T2L-ICAG. We evaluate this approach on two representative LALMs using SIFT-50M for supervised fine-tuning and construct a controlled compositional evaluation suite covering five task classes. Across two LALM backbones, T2L-ICAG consistently improves over static LoRA and also the global embedding-based T2L baseline. Coverage and capacity analyses further show that these gains are larger on structurally out-of-domain tasks and cannot be explained by parameter count alone. These results suggest that generating task-specific adapters from instructions is a promising direction for improving compositional generalization of LALMs.

papers.title: End-to-End Neural Modeling of EM Response and Design Performance for Free-Form RFIC Passives
papers.summary: Passive matching networks are critical components in radio-frequency integrated circuits (RFICs), but their design is bottlenecked by expensive finite-difference-based electromagnetic (EM) simulation. We propose an end-to-end neural framework for free-form RFIC passives that predicts both EM response and downstream design performance under varying frequency and circuit contexts, combining a frequency-conditioned neural simulator with a circuit-conditioned neural solver. To improve design performance prediction, the simulator outputs a neural EM response consisting of both the explicit EM response and a complementary response, together with a dependence regularizer that encourages the two responses to capture orthogonal information. To evaluate the proposed framework, we construct a large-scale dataset of free-form passive layouts, synthesized from both expert-designed contours and random paths. Our 21M-parameter model achieves high accuracy across a broad frequency range, circuit contexts and passive matching settings, with $R^2>0.98$ for almost all targets, while providing orders-of-magnitude faster evaluation than traditional EM simulation. Code available at https://github.com/ETH-IDEAS/RFIC-NeuralSim.

papers.title: GNSS Anomaly Detection in Urban Canyons: A Comprehensive Survey of Multimodal Visibility Inference
papers.summary: Reliable GNSS positioning in dense urban environments depends on assessing satellite visibility and identifying measurements degraded by non-line-of-sight (NLOS) reception and multipath. This survey organizes reception-state inference into three complementary evidence families: receiver-side signals, 3D maps and environmental models, and auxiliary sensors. Receiver-side approaches span antenna/electromagnetic, tracking/baseband, and observable-domain evidence, interpreted through rule-based, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods. Map-based approaches are examined by reviewing environmental representations and methods such as geometric screening, shadow matching, 3D ray tracing, and neural implicit visibility prediction. IMU, camera, and LiDAR measurements provide complementary kinematic, visual, and geometric evidence for online screening. Across these families, we compare accuracy, interpretability, hardware and calibration requirements, map dependence, computational cost, and suitability for real-time deployment. We identify open challenges in dataset quality and labeling, domain generalization, map freshness, and resource-efficient implementation. The resulting synthesis connects signal processing, environmental modeling, and sensor fusion to guide the design of robust urban GNSS measurement-screening systems.

papers.title: Space-Time Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces for Doppler-Resilient LEO Broadcasting
papers.summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade programmable layers in front of a feed. In the SIM designs reported so far, including those proposed for low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, the layer coefficients are space-only controls or are varied randomly in time to support opportunistic scheduling, so that every radiated beam carries the frequency of the feed. This paper introduces space-time SIMs (ST-SIMs), whose layers are modulated in time and use the temporal dimension of the stack deterministically: each spatial mode of the aperture is paired with its own prescribed frequency translation. The application is LEO broadcasting, where a common waveform reaches terminals with different Doppler shifts, and any common Doppler correction leaves residuals of up to half the Doppler span. We derive the harmonic-domain model of the stack, solve the minimum-energy space-frequency synthesis in closed form, and prove that full column rank of the steering matrix is necessary and sufficient for decoupling K terminal-specific translations, a result that extends to groups of terminals. We further propose a phase-only synthesis algorithm with guaranteed stationarity, together with quantization and control-rate laws. Simulations at 20 GHz over 50 random drops show that a four-layer ST-SIM with a single radio-frequency chain removes the Doppler floor of a static SIM for footprint radii above about 45 km and, under the ideal phase-only model and at equal radiated peak energy, approaches ideal digital per-terminal precompensation within 0.5 dB for resolvable terminals, whereas, in the evaluated geometries, a single time-modulated layer cannot synthesize the required modes.

papers.title: Reinsertion-Aware Parameter Estimation of the WECC Composite Load Model via Closed-Loop Equivalent-Network Co-Estimation
papers.summary: Measurement-based parameter estimation of the WECC composite load model (CMLD) commonly relies on voltage replay, where measured voltage is imposed on an isolated CMLD and its parameters are optimized to reproduce measured active and reactive power. However, this open-loop formulation neglects the two-way dynamic interaction between the load and grid, potentially causing large errors when the estimated model is reinserted into dynamic grid simulations. To address this limitation, we propose a closed-loop parameter estimation framework that alternately estimates the CMLD parameters and a five-parameter equivalent network representing the external grid. This framework restores load-grid interaction during estimation and enables voltage, active power, and reactive power to jointly constrain the parameter estimation. Compared with four baseline methods, the proposed approach achieves the highest reinsertion accuracy in both the CMLD benchmark and transmission and distribution (T&D) co-simulation environments. In the T&D case, it reduces active-power, reactive-power, and voltage errors by 73%, 64%, and 62%, respectively. The identified model also maintains improved reinsertion accuracy under disturbances not used for estimation, demonstrating transferability beyond the identification event.

papers.title: Symbolic Direct Construction of Augmented Systems for Levenberg-Marquardt Power Flow
papers.summary: Levenberg-Marquardt power flow (LMPF) addresses ill-conditioned equations and provides least-squares stationary points for infeasible operating requests. Conventional implementations form damped normal equations, where J^T J introduces fill, squares the spectral condition number of the undamped part, and adds sparse-product cost. We propose an augmented LMPF formulation with a symbolic-permutation-based Jacobian operator that fills the augmented blocks directly. We prove that the matrix is symmetric quasi-definite for positive damping, enabling fixed-order, pivot-free QDLDL factorization. This property also motivates the solver choice: KLU value-only refactorization can reuse an unsuitable pivot order, forcing fresh full factorizations on difficult LMPF trajectories. We further introduce one-probe adaptive trust-region initialization for the radius and damping. Direct assembly is 7.5-11.9x faster than the fastest coordinate-list path and 18.0-58.8x faster than cached normal-equation sparse-product formation; QDLDL reduces numerical refactorization and triangular-solve time by up to 3.40x on identical matrices. Adaptive initialization solves flat-started RTE cases in 19-25 factorizations, 7.5-11.6x faster than reproduced three-step LM. On case2383wp, our 84-iteration run performs 84 factorizations and 168 resolves in 237 ms, versus published times of 200.780-441.72 s with fewer outer iterations, corresponding to speedups of 847-1860x. These results require complete factorization and resolve accounting and reveal initialization and legacy-parameter effects. DC-initialized NR exhibits fast quadratic convergence throughout every tested solvable loading range, motivating clearer, reproducible definitions of ill-conditioned power-flow benchmarks.

papers.title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
papers.summary: Background/Objectives: Rapid differentiation of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subtypes is vital for acute management. Although current deep learning models achieve high single-dataset accuracy, they suffer from "shortcut learning" and domain shift in external validation. This study proposes a hierarchical computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system mimicking emergency triage. Methods: We introduce a 3-channel Radiology-Focused Preprocessing pipeline that feeds radiological Hounsfield Unit (HU) windows into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones via asymmetric formats (.mat and .png). The architecture utilizes a novel joint cross-attention fusion network optimized by an Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss. Results: Our system achieved a 95.48% F1-score on the internal stroke dataset. However, multi-center external validation (AISD, BHSD, PhysioNet) using a Mask Anchor filter revealed a drop to the 58-62% range, exposing the "internal validation illusion" caused by hardware noise. Critically, models exhibited high precision (77%) but low sensitivity (57%) for ischemic stroke, proving prone to hemorrhage overdiagnosis. Multi-seed variance analysis demonstrated that the DenseNet201+ViT backbone yielded the lowest deviation (0.59) and highest stability, making it the most reliable architecture for real-world clinical integration. Conclusions: To overcome diagnostic challenges, future research must focus on multimodal architectures that combine 3D volumetric extraction with clinical data.

papers.title: Frequency-Dependent Hybrid Digital and Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) Beamforming for Multiuser MIMO-OFDM Systems
papers.summary: Microwave linear analog computing (MiLAC) has recently emerged as a promising approach for reducing the hardware and digital-processing requirements of large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. In narrowband multiuser systems, hybrid digital-MiLAC beamforming can achieve digital beamforming flexibility with only as many radio-frequency (RF) chains as data streams. However, extending this advantage to wideband systems is nontrivial because practical MiLAC circuits exhibit frequency-dependent responses. In this paper, we investigate hybrid digital-MiLAC beamforming for multiuser MISO-OFDM systems with a frequency-dependent MiLAC circuit model. We characterize the frequency dependence of MiLAC by relating the susceptance of each tunable component across subcarriers to its center-frequency value. Under this frequency coupling, we show that a single MiLAC circuit generally cannot simultaneously match the desired beamforming directions across all subcarriers, highlighting the essential role of subcarrier-dependent digital precoding. We then develop a block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm to jointly optimize the digital and MiLAC beamformers for average sum-rate maximization. In particular, an efficient alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is custom-designed to handle the frequency-coupled circuit constraints in the MiLAC beamformer subproblem. Simulation results show that the proposed hybrid digital-MiLAC design outperforms conventional hybrid digital-analog beamforming, particularly when fewer RF chains are available and the channel is more frequency-selective. With $64$ transmit antennas and $4$ data streams, it attains $96.3\%$ of the digital sum-rate using only $8$ RF chains. Furthermore, under highly frequency-selective channels and using $4$ RF chains, it provides a $48\%$ sum-rate gain over the conventional hybrid design.

papers.title: A Unified Channel Model and Performance Evaluation for Underwater-to-Air Optical Links
papers.summary: This paper develops a conditional statistical framework for nominally normal underwater-to-air optical links. It combines bulk attenuation, normalized log-normal atmospheric and Weibull underwater fluctuations, and entrance-pupil collection with surface-tilt-dependent Fresnel transmission. Conditioning transmission and beam displacement on a common tilt preserves their dependence. Product distributions with explicit support and Jacobians yield integrals valid for arbitrary positive Weibull shape. Average uncoded OOK bit error rate (BER) and outage are evaluated using consistent power, noise and SNR definitions. Independent component-wise Monte Carlo verifies the full conditional model at six reference configurations; targeted importance sampling checks selected BER values down to approximately 6 x 10^-9. A circular-pupil Gaussian integral reveals parameter-dependent errors in the equivalent-beam collection approximation, including a 36.9% BER underestimate at one tested operating point. Conditional power and distance studies therefore use the circular-pupil reference and distinguish low-error short-air-segment conditions from collection-limited conditions. Source-anchored spectral and water-type contrasts, together with illumination and receiver checks, identify the dependence of these results on the prescribed operating conditions. The framework supplies reproducible error and outage calculations within a single-patch scalar model; physical operating ranges additionally depend on the surface, propagation and receiver assumptions.

papers.title: Decoding Motion-Blurred QR Codes: Motion-Parameter Error Tolerance and Model-Based Recovery
papers.summary: Quick Response (QR) code deblurring must ultimately recover the encoded payload, yet how accurately the underlying camera motion must be estimated remains an open question. To address this question, we formulate motion-blurred QR recovery within a unified mathematical framework of identifiability and systematically measure the decoding tolerance to perturbations in motion length, direction, rotation or scaling centre, and speed profile. These controlled experiments reveal three structural laws: 1) parameter tolerances shrink rapidly as blur amplitude grows and are tightest under uniform speed, whereas accelerating motion is substantially more forgiving; 2) length tolerance can differ markedly between underestimation and overestimation; 3) errors that are individually benign interact strongly and prevent decoding when combined. Guided by these findings, we propose a grey-box recovery pipeline in which two compact networks predict an initial corner trajectory, followed by tolerance-guided candidate search, alternating image-and-path fitting, and regularised linear inversion. On a new benchmark of 955 handheld motion-blurred photographs captured across four phone models and four motion categories, our method recovers the exact payload on 93.1% of the images, outperforming the strongest fine-tuned deblurring network at 83.6% and reducing the decoding error rate by 58.0%.

papers.title: TIMUSE: Text-Initialized Masked Semantic Token Modeling for Universal Speech Enhancement
papers.summary: Discrete-token-based universal speech enhancement (USE) enables strong sequence modeling but often suffers from a quality--fidelity trade-off, where perceptually plausible outputs may alter linguistic content or speaker characteristics. We present TIMUSE, a two-stage USE framework combining text-initialized masked semantic restoration with acoustic reconstruction. A pretrained diffusion language model (DLM) is adapted with LoRA to recover clean semantic tokens using masked generative modeling, while a conditional flow matching model reconstructs clean 24\,kHz speech from the recovered semantic tokens and original degraded speech. Both system-level and controlled comparisons show that TIMUSE achieves a better balance between perceptual quality and fidelity than existing discrete USE models. Ablations further show that text DLM initialization brings a targeted gain under severe degradations.

papers.title: How Much Sensing is Enough? Landslide Detection from Sparse and Noisy 3D Observations
papers.summary: Dense 3D terrain information is critical for accurate landslide detection; however, acquiring such data at large scale is often limited by sensing infrastructure, coverage, and environmental conditions. Emerging sensing modalities (e.g., mmWave, low-cost radar, sparse LiDAR) can operate under adverse conditions, but inherently produce sparse and noisy 3D observations, raising an important question: \emph{how much sensing is sufficient for reliable landslide detection?} Given the absence of large-scale sparse-terrain datasets, we have constructed a physics-informed dataset by combining digital elevation models from OpenTopography with soil moisture data from NASA's SMAP. Subsequently, we have randomly generated landslide events and introduced controlled sparsification and stochastic noise to emulate sensing constraints. We have then developed a learning-based framework to reconstruct the underlying terrain and identify landslide-prone regions using a CNN + XGBoost method. Our results show that with only 20\% of the original observations, the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 80\% and a ROC-AUC of 0.868, with a reconstruction error (L2 Chamfer Distance) of 99.67~$m^2$ on the test set. We have further studied the impact of sparsity, highlighting the trade-off between sensing density and detection performance.

papers.title: Efficient SCA Algorithms for Sparse Bayesian Learning
papers.summary: Type-II sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) for the multiple measurement vector model recovers a sparse signal power vector by minimizing the marginal negative log-likelihood via the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm, referred to as M-SBL. We revisit the covariance learning (CL) problem and develop three parallel first-order algorithms within the successive convex approximation (SCA) framework. CL-SCA minimizes per-coordinate surrogates formed by partially linearizing the log-determinant term, while CL-FP uses a damped projected fixed-point iteration derived from stationarity conditions. Both methods have closed-form updates. We prove that the fixed points of both update maps are exactly the KKT points of the CL problem, that each update direction satisfies a quantitative descent inequality, that the damped iterates achieve sufficient decrease with an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$ best-iterate stationarity rate, and we derive a backtracking rule that retains this rate without step-size tuning. If damping factors are bounded away from zero, the residual vanishes along the whole sequence and every limit point is a KKT point. Local analysis motivates CL-Hyb, which combines CL-SCA and CL-FP. Experiments on device activity detection in massive random access show that CL-Hyb-bt matches the best CL solvers' accuracy at a fraction of the runtime and is over an order of magnitude faster than EM.

papers.title: Compositional Approximately Bisimilar Abstractions of Stochastic Interconnected Systems
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of constructing (alternating) bisimilar symbolic models for discrete-time, stochastic, interconnected systems. By leveraging a refined over-approximation of the stochastic reachable sets and the q-th moment input-to-state stability (delta-ISS-Mq) property, we establish an approximate bisimulation relation between stochastic systems and their deterministic (noise-free) counterparts. This approach significantly simplifies the analysis of the approximate (alternating) bisimulation between the global interconnected stochastic system and its symbolic model. We derive formal conditions under which local bisimulation relations are preserved when composing subsystems into a global interconnected system. The engineering relevance of the proposed compositional framework is demonstrated through temperature regulation case studies involving a fixed ten-room building and a circular cascade interconnection scaled from six to fourteen rooms. The results show that, beyond a small number of subsystems, the proposed method achieves substantially faster abstraction computation times than standard monolithic approaches, with the performance gap widening as the number of interconnected subsystems grows and the monolithic approach failing to converge beyond ten rooms.

papers.title: Fluid Antennas Enabled UAV Communication Systems: Fundamentals, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.summary: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) require uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems to adapt to large-scale propagation changes and fast local channel fluctuations. Fluid antennas (FAs) provide an additional degree of freedom (DoF) by reconfiguring antenna positions within a compact aperture. This article investigates FA-enabled UAV communication systems from the perspectives of fundamentals, design challenges, and future research directions. We first introduce a dual-mobility perspective, in which UAV trajectory planning provides macro-mobility for large-scale air-to-ground geometry adaptation, and FA position reconfiguration provides micro-mobility for fine-grained local channel adaptation. We then identify key design challenges arising from the high computational complexity and information uncertainty in the joint optimization of UAV trajectory, FA positions, and beamforming under mobility, energy, hardware, and security constraints. To address these challenges, we present a hybrid offline-online optimization framework, where prior information such as environment maps, user mobility patterns, and statistical channel state information (CSI) supports long-term planning, while real-time information such as instantaneous CSI and UAV state enables fast online correction. A case study on FA-enabled UAV-assisted vehicular communications demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss future directions of FA-enabled UAV communication in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), secure communication, mobile edge computing (MEC), and aerial relaying.

papers.title: Joint Dynamic Lane Reversal and Variable Speed Limit Control: A Graphormer-Based Approach
papers.summary: Connected and automated vehicles could allow reassigning lane directions and speed limits on every road frequently, but the benefit hinges on how traffic reroutes, and one-way roads can isolate junctions. We formulate network-wide dynamic lane allocation and directional speed limit control with one-way roads, lane clearing before each reversal, and a navigable graph kept strongly connected at all times. An action-resolution algorithm grounded in graph orientation theory admits a proposal closing a direction only if the network stays strongly connected and otherwise relaxes or reverts it, keeping all junctions mutually reachable within the model, even during clearing. All road controllers share one transformer whose attention, Global Endpoint Relation-Aware Spatio-Temporal Self-Attention (GERASTSA), spans all road-time tokens, biased by the endpoint relations between roads. It is pretrained on action-conditioned traffic forecasting and fine-tuned with per-road proximal policy optimization under a mixed reward that also credits neighboring roads and the network. On a 6 x 6 grid with commuter rush hours, the learned policy makes about two thirds of roads one-way in the peak direction and cuts daily delay by 90% against the initial configuration held fixed and by 85% against a tuned two-way load balancer. Restricted to two-way roads at test time, it gains only about as much as this balancer, whereas its learned speed limits add delay. Pretraining roughly halves the updates needed to surpass the fixed configuration. Of the ablations, only removing the relational bias or the spatial embedding clearly matters, multiplying delay about fivefold.

papers.title: Moving bits instead of watts: Accelerating global AI data-centre deployment at the energy-digital-water-land nexus
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented expansion of data centres. However, this growth is increasingly stalled by grid transmission constraints that trap new data centres in years-long connection queues. Unlike electricity, computation can be moved across the globe through fibre-optic networks, but whether this spatial transfer can bypass constrained grids and accelerate global AI data-centre deployment remains unknown. Here we develop a global framework that places future data-centre capacity in energy-abundant regions and routes computational workloads through fibre-optic networks rather than transmitting electricity. We evaluate the framework through more than 11 million hourly operation simulations at subnational resolution, integrating constraints on energy systems, water, digital connectivity, land and financing risk. Results show that across multiple data-centre development and climate-policy scenarios, leveraging global data transfer allows new data centres to be sited where these conditions are favourable, lowering construction costs by 44-47% and carbon emissions by 38%. By treating the global fibre-optic network as an energy-system asset, it avoids 34-67 GW of high-voltage transmission capacity, comparable in magnitude to Italy's national peak electricity demand. Crucially, this methodology could bring more than 95% of connection-delayed data centres online in 2030, with Canada, the Nordic countries and the Arabian Peninsula emerging as preferred locations for data-centre development. Our findings establish computational mobility as an alternative to energy-system expansion, informing the coordinated global development of energy and artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

papers.title: Analysis and Antenna Position Selection for Pinching-Antenna Systems in Fading Channels
papers.summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASSs) are an emerging flexible antenna technology that enables the creation of line-of-sight (LoS) links by repositioning a radiating element along a dielectric waveguide (WG). Most existing studies of PASSs assume a purely LoS environment, despite the fact that many practical wireless environments exhibit scattering and spatially correlated shadow fading. In this paper, we present the first statistical analysis of PASS performance under Ricean fading with spatially correlated large-scale fading. Focusing on a fundamental single-user uplink PASS, we characterize the distribution and mean of the maximum achievable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). For the classical exponentially correlated shadow fading scenario, we express the channel power process in terms of Brownian motion and derive highly accurate approximations for the maximum SNR distribution and mean. For a general class of smoothly correlated shadow fading processes, we derive an accurate expression for the SNR distribution by modeling the process in terms of the fade sojourn duration. To address the challenges of antenna position selection in fading environments, we propose radio environment map (REM)-based positioning strategies, including opportunistic random-look and grid-based constructions. Analytical results are validated by simulation, and the impacts of key system parameters, such as the Ricean $K$-factor, spatial correlation, WG length, and carrier frequency are investigated. The results provide insights into PASS operation beyond idealized LoS conditions and establish a general analytical framework for performance evaluation and antenna positioning in scattered environments.

papers.title: Realizing Low-Precision Storage and Sparse Execution in a Folded FPGA Speech Enhancer
papers.summary: Hardware-aware training often optimizes FPGA resources, latency, or bit operations, but folding changes what compression saves: shared arithmetic decouples precision, weight storage, and scheduled work. We derive training objectives from the measured costs of a folded streaming speech-enhancement accelerator. Mixed-precision weights reduce on-chip storage; structured channel sparsity removes entire operations from the engine schedule. We deploy a bit-exact implementation on the Kria KV260. The best sparse model eliminates 47.3% of convolution MACs, cutting frame time by 45% (1.86 to 1.03 ms) and dynamic energy by 60% (83 to 33 $\mu$J/frame) against a storage-priced model measured in the same session, with higher speech quality. Relative to the most efficient dense build measured separately, frame time falls by 42% and energy by 48%. Reducing weight width from 8 to 6 bits lowers dynamic power by 27% but changes frame time by less than 5%. Plain channel group-lasso removes more work than cycle-cost-weighted lasso. Thus, folded-accelerator training should price storage and removable work separately, rather than rely on a single bit-operation metric.

papers.title: Sparse Target Parameter and Channel Estimation in MIMO-OOFDM-Aided Visible Light Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
papers.summary: A unified framework is developed for parameter estimation (PE) and channel estimation (CE) in monostatic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM)-aided visible light integrated sensing and communication (VL-ISAC) systems. A common optical waveform supports sensing and downlink communication while accounting for target reflections, clutter, Doppler effects, and the communication channel. For sensing PE, one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) on-grid and off-grid sparse representations are formulated. The proposed 1D off-grid Bayesian learning (1D-OffGBL) algorithm employs a joint delay-Doppler (DD) dictionary to exploit coupled DD information and achieve high estimation accuracy. In contrast, the proposed 2D off-grid Bayesian learning (2D-OffGBL) algorithm sequentially estimates the Doppler and delay parameters, thereby avoiding a high-dimensional joint dictionary and reducing computational complexity. Both algorithms iteratively refine the continuous-valued delay and Doppler parameters to mitigate off-grid basis mismatch. Furthermore, 1D and 2D sparse channel representations and corresponding CE procedures are developed, followed by range and velocity estimation for both sensing models. Closed-form Bayesian Cramer-Rao bounds (BCRBs) are derived for PE, CE, range, and velocity estimation. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithms outperform conventional sparse recovery schemes in terms of normalized mean-squared error (NMSE). In particular, 1D-OffGBL achieves the highest estimation accuracy, whereas 2D-OffGBL provides a favourable performance-complexity trade-off for practical MIMO DCO-OFDM VL-ISAC systems.

papers.title: Synchronization-Oriented Multi-Radius BMOCZ for Non-Coherent Short-Packet Communications
papers.summary: Modulation on conjugate-reciprocal zeros (MOCZ) is a promising candidate for blind short-packet communication (SPC) in future wireless systems; however, its performance is sensitive to timing and frequency synchronization errors. In this paper, we propose a novel scheme named multi-radius binary MOCZ (MR-BMOCZ). This method introduces a new root placement strategy that enhances diversity in the autocorrelation domain. The resulting structure enhances the autocorrelation properties of the transmitted waveform, leading to improved timing offset (TO) estimation. Moreover, the multi-radius construction distributes the signal energy over a larger set of radii, hence reducing the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). The resulting waveform also exhibits a distinctive spectral structure that is exploited for carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation and correction, yielding lower normalized mean square error (NMSE) compared with BMOCZ-based schemes. Simulation results over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and fading channels demonstrate that MR-BMOCZ achieves superior synchronization performance while maintaining comparable bit error rate (BER) and block error rate (BLER) performance. Consequently, the proposed scheme offers a synchronization oriented extension of BMOCZ for robust non-coherent SPC.

papers.title: Adaptive Control for General Nonlinear Stochastic Systems
papers.summary: This paper extends the least-squares and certainty-equivalence minimum-variance framework of classical linear self-tuning regulators to a broad class of nonlinearly parameterized systems with compact parameter spaces, including commonly used deep neural network models. First, historical nonlinear least-squares fitting guarantees are converted into online one-step prediction bounds under a general modulus of continuity, with explicit regret rates under parameter Lipschitz continuity and finite-moment noise. Second, approximate NLS estimation combined with certainty-equivalence control achieves closed-loop stability and asymptotically optimal tracking under mild conditions without requiring excitation or parameter identifiability. Explicit closed-loop regret and tracking error rates are established in the parameter-Lipschitz case, and closed-loop examples show that the regret rates cannot, in general, be improved for this regulator. Finally, robustness to small unmodeled dynamics is established by showing that closed-loop stability is preserved and the tracking error bounds comprise a vanishing term and a residual term determined by the model discrepancy.

papers.title: Right Model, Right Task: Capability-Constrained Carbon Labeling to Decarbonize Generative AI
papers.summary: The carbon footprint of generative-AI inference depends not only on hardware efficiency and electricity supply, but also on whether the selected model is appropriate for the task. A frontier model may expend unnecessary computation on a routine request, whereas an under-capable model may increase energy use through failure, retries, extended reasoning and escalation. However, a standardized evaluation framework that accounts for task-specific capability requirements and the carbon emissions associated with successful task remains lacking. In this Perspective, we argue for a capability-constrained carbon labeling framework that shifts environmental assessment from carbon intensity per inference towards the expected carbon emissions per successfully completed task at the required capability level. Under this framework, models would first be assessed against task-specific capability requirements, and only models capable of meeting those requirements would be compared on their expected energy use and operational carbon emissions. By linking service quality to carbon cost, this approach could enable more informed matching of the right model to the right task, offering a demand-side pathway to reducing emissions associated with generative-AI token use. Realizing this vision will require standardized capability-based service assessments, comprehensive energy accounting and transparent carbon disclosures.

papers.title: Accelerated Push-Pull with Local Updates for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization
papers.summary: We consider decentralized stochastic nonconvex optimization over directed networks. Push--Pull provides an efficient decentralized optimization framework for such networks, but in the stochastic setting, gradient variance can slow its convergence and complicate the analysis of linear speedup. Motivated by this observation, we incorporate recursive momentum into stochastic Push--Pull for variance reduction, yielding the accelerated stochastic Push--Pull (ASPP) algorithm. Under mean-squared smoothness, we prove that ASPP improves the convergence rate of stochastic Push--Pull and achieves asymptotic linear speedup with respect to the number of agents. To further reduce communication, we develop LASPP, a local-update variant of ASPP that allows each agent to perform multiple local updates between communication rounds. We show that LASPP achieves an additional asymptotic linear speedup with respect to the number of local steps. With a suitable number of local steps, LASPP reduces communication complexity while maintaining the same stochastic gradient complexity as ASPP. Numerical experiments on real datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Joint Antenna Rotation and Polarforming for Satellite Communications
papers.summary: This paper investigates joint antenna rotation and polarforming for low-Earth-orbit (LEO) communications, where a satellite equipped with rotatable dual-polarized antenna elements receives uplink signals from ground terminals (GTs) distributed across multiple clusters. In particular, antenna rotation redistributes directional gains across angularly separated clusters, while polarforming improves the separability of spatially correlated GT channels within each cluster. We formulate a weighted sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes rotatable antenna (RA) orientation trajectories, element-wise polarformers, and digital receive filters under steering-range and inter-epoch slew constraints. To solve the resulting nonconvex problem, we develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based alternating algorithm, in which the optimal polarformer for each element is derived in semi-closed form, while an exact boresight parameterization yields convex feasible sets for RA-trajectory optimization, enabling Armijo-based gradient updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed joint design outperforms benchmark schemes and reveal the complementary roles of antenna rotation in directional-gain allocation and polarforming in improving channel separability.

papers.title: Movable Antenna Enabled Anti-Jamming: From Local Optimality Guaranteed Design to a Unified Antenna Position Optimization Framework
papers.summary: Anti-jamming capability is of paramount importance in modern wireless communications, yet conventional receivers are severely constrained by their fixed array geometries, which limit the available spatial degrees of freedom and leave performance highly susceptible to strong interference. By contrast, movable antennas (MAs) provide additional spatial degrees of freedom through antenna-position optimization. This paper investigates MA-enabled anti-jamming by jointly optimizing the antenna-position vector (APV) and receive beamformer to maximize the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). For the canonical setting with a single jammer and a single line-of-sight (LoS) propagation path on the legitimate link, we develop a damped projected-gradient descent (DPGD) algorithm with low computational complexity, which scales linearly with the number of receive MAs. We establish a generic active strict-saddle landscape for the resulting steering-coherence minimization problem and prove that DPGD converges almost surely to a local minimizer rather than merely to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point. For the general setting with multiple channel paths on the legitimate link and/or multiple jammers, we derive an equivalent ridge least-squares formulation and develop a low-complexity soft-active projected-gradient (SAPG) algorithm, which also scales linearly with the number of receive MAs. We further show that the proposed antenna position optimization framework applies to both minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) and zero-forcing (ZF) reception. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithms, demonstrating substantial gains in both anti-jamming performance and computational efficiency.

papers.title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
papers.summary: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. The first (uncontrollable) network layer corresponds to the transformations offered by wireless fading, while the second (controllable) layer is implemented via SIM operations. In particular, only the first, front-end MS layer needs to exhibit nonlinear response to serve as an activation function. Leveraging the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) framework, the proposed XL MIMO system architecture is shown to be a universal approximator, and the optimal linear-SIM-based combining is derived in closed form, allowing for fast training even and partial signal observability. Numerical evaluations across diverse datasets showcase that the proposed XL-MIMO-ELM framework achieves classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models, thereby, proving the viability of low complexity, wave-domain neural computations.

papers.title: FedAvgIm: Federated Learning for Multi-Site Impedance Identification of Inverter-Based Resources
papers.summary: With the increasing integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) into power systems, assessing small-signal interaction stability has become essential. Impedance/admittance models enable frequency-domain characterization of IBR dynamics without requiring access to proprietary internal control details, but measurement-based identification is time-consuming and must be repeated across operating points. This paper proposes FedAvgIm, a privacy-aware federated-learning framework for multi-site dq-admittance identification under severe local data scarcity and raw-data-locality constraints. Each IBR site trains a local feed-forward neural network using a small set of operating-point-frequency samples, while only model parameters are shared with a cloud aggregator that performs sample-size-weighted FedAvg to update a global model and broadcast it back to all sites. To demonstrate effectiveness, EMT measurement-based admittance datasets are constructed for nine grid-following IBRs with different parameters, architectures, measurement-noise levels, and non-IID settings, where each client has only 40-390 training samples. Results show that FedAvgIm achieves performance close to centralized training and consistently outperforms local-only learning and raw-data-locality-preserving transfer-learning baselines. Additional studies show that FedAvgIm maintains stable learning behavior under measurement noise and remains beneficial under moderate non-IID conditions. The estimated dq-admittance models are further applied to generalized Nyquist stability analysis and validated against EMT time-domain simulations under multiple operating points and grid-strength conditions.

papers.title: Grid-Forming AC/DC Converters for Meshed DC Networks via Dual-Measurement Frequency Droop
papers.summary: This paper proposes and analyzes a dual-measurement frequency-droop (DMFD) controller for meshed MVDC networks. Using only two local DC measurements, bus-voltage deviation and a filtered DC-port current or power deviation, the controller enables grid-forming operation at both AC and DC ports across the mesh. Although the DMFD regulates neither the DC voltage nor the DC current directly and acts only on the terminal frequency, it is shown that AC-side synchronization closes an effective DC droop at every synchronized terminal, so that the steady operating point of the mesh exists and is unique. Constant frequency deviations at a terminal and single-terminal islanding enter the same DC equations as equivalent current offsets, with the island frequency fixed by the island power balance, allowing node voltages and branch currents to be obtained from one linear system. The steady-state model yields design-use envelopes to map the droop ratios and the net DC-injection levels into bounds on DC-voltage deviation and terminal currents. A small-signal dynamic model is developed and used to generate eigenvalue loci and damping-ratio charts that guide controller-gain selection. Averaged EMT simulations on a four-terminal ring corroborate the analysis: in regimes where PLL-based grid-following control is known to lose damping, the DMFD controller maintains stable operation and follows the predicted steady-state characteristics.

papers.title: Focusing Efficiency for Large Intelligent Surfaces
papers.summary: This paper studies wireless power transmission (WPT) with large intelligent surfaces (LISs) in a single-user scenario, with emphasis on power-transfer efficiency. The optimal current distribution on the LIS is derived under a total-power constraint for an arbitrary receiving antenna, providing a theoretical characterization of the maximum achievable focusing efficiency. The analysis shows that the efficiency is strongly affected by the receiving radiation pattern, antenna orientation, and transmission distance. Clear performance differences are observed among practical antenna types for specific orientations, whereas directional averaging makes their average focusing efficiencies much closer. The theoretical findings are further validated by full-wave FEKO simulations, showing good agreement with the predictions of the proposed formulation. These results provide insight into the impact of receiver characteristics and propagation geometry on LIS-enabled WPT and offer a theoretical basis for efficient single-user power-transfer design.

papers.title: A Robust, Explainable, and Efficient Deep Metric for Speech and General Audio Quality
papers.summary: We present a robust Speech and Audio Quality Metric (SAQM) that merges features of traditional quality metrics with a CNN trained on a large amount of data using contrastive learning methods. To overcome the problem of limited amounts of human-labeled training data, we propose two pretraining strategies relying on pseudo-labels. One uses an established objective metric PEAQ-2f (based on ITU-R BS.1387) as surrogate loss, the other is based on contrasting a wide range of coding modes by a rule-of-thumb ordering based on expected perceived quality. As a key novelty, our approach lets us generate saliency maps by propagating gradients to identify which feature has the greatest impact on the final metric outcome and enables our system to provide insights regarding the type and extent of distortions present in the tested audio signal. The resulting (SAQM) operates at low computational complexity, performs comparably to (SOTA) metrics on speech while still performing well on general audio content.

papers.title: Security Region Compression via Hybrid Vertex Pruning for Enhanced Computational Efficiency
papers.summary: The security region (SR) specifies a joint feasible region in the operational space involving various installations within the power system. It enables dynamic allocation of capacity among these energy units, thereby unlocking additional grid potential for power delivery and mitigating congestion. By constructing a convex hull from a set of vertices to form a polytope, the SR can be effectively represented with an acceptable accuracy loss. However, the SR computation inevitably generates many low-quality vertices, which contribute little to the overall hypervolume and can be discarded. By introducing SR compression, the SR data size can be reduced, which in turn facilitates the memory-efficient computation of SR and time-efficient solution of SR-related optimization problems. Accordingly, this paper proposes a vertex pruning approach that mixes local and backward search policies to achieve effective SR compression. In particular, the backward search strategy allows previously pruned vertices to be recycled when they are re-identified as critical. Subsequently, we incorporate this approach to enhance computational efficiency in the aforementioned applications. Numerical validations are conducted on two realistic medium-voltage Dutch grid cases. The results demonstrate at most 1.65% hypervolume loss with over 96.0\% SR data size reduction after applying the proposed compression approach. Empowered by this compression, the 8-dimensional (8D) SR becomes computationally tractable. Moreover, in relevant grid-aware computation challenges, the solving time can be reduced by at least 52.9% with at most an 1.36% optimality loss. All above validate both the efficacy and values of the proposed SR compression approach.

papers.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
papers.summary: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.

papers.title: Belief-Aware VLM Model for Human-like Reasoning
papers.summary: Traditional neural network models for intent inference rely heavily on observable states and struggle to generalize across diverse tasks and dynamic environments. Recent advances in Vision Language Models (VLMs) and Vision Language Action (VLA) models introduce common-sense reasoning through large-scale multimodal pretraining, enabling zero-shot performance across tasks. However, these models still lack explicit mechanisms to represent and update belief, limiting their ability to reason like humans or capture the evolving human intent over long-horizon. To address this, we propose a belief-aware VLM framework that integrates retrieval-based memory and reinforcement learning. Instead of learning an explicit belief model, we approximate belief using a vector-based memory that retrieves relevant multimodal context, which is incorporated into the VLM for reasoning. We further refine decision-making using a reinforcement learning policy over the VLM latent space. We evaluate our approach on publicly available VQA datasets such as HD-EPIC and demonstrate consistent improvements over zero-shot baselines, highlighting the importance of belief-aware reasoning.

papers.title: TRACER: An RDC-Triggered Trajectory Recovery Framework for Cyberattack-Resilient Adaptive Cruise Control
papers.summary: The increasing connectivity of adaptive cruise control (ACC) systems exposes vehicle-state information to cyberattacks, potentially causing irrational car-following behavior and unsafe longitudinal dynamics. Existing trajectory recovery methods generally lack an interpretable criterion for recovery activation and remain vulnerable to attack-induced distribution shifts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TRACER, a rational driving constraint (RDC)-triggered trajectory recovery framework for cyberattack-resilient ACC systems. TRACER employs a rationality-aware triggering (RAT) mechanism that activates recovery when the observed driving state violates the calibrated RDC bounds. It also introduces cross-branch robust imitation learning (CRIL), which combines a clean branch for learning nominal driving behavior with a noise-enhanced branch for improving robustness to corrupted observations. Cross-branch fine-tuning further aligns the robust recovery policy with the nominal driving-state distribution. Experiments across six cyberattack scenarios show that TRACER achieves reliable recovery triggering and outperforms state-of-the-art recovery baselines in terms of accuracy, stability, and safety. State-space analysis further confirms that TRACER mitigates attack-induced distribution shifts and restores coupled spacing-velocity dynamics, highlighting the effectiveness of robust policy learning for cyberattack-resilient ACC.

papers.title: Do bioacoustic foundation models hear through the noise ? SNR and generalization in underwater detection
papers.summary: Bioacoustic foundation models are claimed to generalize across taxa and recording conditions, but are trained mainly on terrestrial archives of focal, high-quality recordings and evaluated on benchmarks emphasizing architecture over data conditions. We evaluate four such models as frozen encoders on an underwater detection task, using linear probing on continuously recorded data from the Kerguelen Plateau. Four datasets of identical size were built to differ only in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of their positive segments, and probes were trained and evaluated across all combinations. Evaluation SNR accounts for more variation in average precision (AP) than model choice, and performance peaks when training and evaluation share a noise regime --- the configuration least representative of a continuous deployment. Training on mixed SNR redistributes performance toward low-SNR conditions without improving it overall, and AP remains low throughout. In light of these results, we call for evaluation standards grounded in realistic noise and deployment conditions rather than curated, high-quality recordings.

papers.title: Measuring Local Acoustic Contribution in Speech LLMs via Word-Span Counterfactual Interventions
papers.summary: Correct transcription does not establish that a word depended on its local audio. We introduce the Acoustic Evidence Contribution (AEC), a word-level counterfactual measure of acoustic grounding. It is obtained from the change in reference-token log likelihood when the word's aligned acoustic span is replaced. We combine decoding outcomes on unedited audio with thresholded AEC in an outcome-contribution matrix, where correct targets are categorized according to their local acoustic contribution as high or low. Depending on the system, 33-49% of correct single-word targets fall below the twofold contribution threshold when averaged across corpora, despite no evident rank association with WER. Retention of reference words after span removal decreases monotonically across AEC quintiles, from 76-83% in the lowest quintile to approximately 1% in the highest. AEC therefore separates transcription correctness from dependence on the aligned local acoustic span while remaining an oracle-aligned diagnostic method.

papers.title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation
papers.summary: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. To facilitate such training data, this study introduces a scalable curation pipeline that curates 3,000 hours from 41 years of raw NOAA hydrophone recordings, producing MarineSet, a large-scale and diverse dataset designed for underwater acoustic learning. A baseline model, MarineNet, trained on MarineSet achieves competitive performance on marine mammal call and ship-type classification, highlighting the value of systematic data curation for developing self-supervised learning models in underwater acoustics.

papers.title: Fast Path, Exact Path: One Library of Hardwired Operators for Streaming and Exact Canny Edge Detection on a Low-Cost FPGA
papers.summary: Hysteresis edge tracking, the final stage of Canny edge detection, follows edge chains of unbounded length and therefore resists single-pass streaming; FPGA designs either approximate it or dedicate separate labelling hardware to it. We show that a single library of hardwired 3x3 operators, each with an identical two-clock latency, delivers both a camera-rate approximation and exact hysteresis on a low-cost Artix-7 (XC7A35T). The fast path streams camera pixels through the operators and K local hysteresis stages and commits each edge decision 262.15-720.63 microseconds after the pixel arrives (K = 1-8; system simulation with a datasheet camera model), that is, 3 + K camera lines later and 46-127x sooner than a frame-based processor can even begin at 30 frames per second. It provably never reports an edge that exact hysteresis rejects, recovers 76.6-96.1% of exact edges at thresholds 20/40, and on the 200 BSDS500 test images retains at least 98.6% of the exact path's boundary F-measure (ODS 0.470-0.477 versus 0.476). The exact path holds 128x128 tiles in block RAM, is exact within each tile, and replaces two-buffer iteration with in-place forward and reverse sweeps built into the same operator. This reduces hysteresis from 38-82 passes to 3-7 on pattern and photo tiles, accelerating the hysteresis step 6.6-21.7x (40x on a worst-case tile) and a complete tile 4.5-9.9x, with identical output. Both paths are bit-exact with software golden models at every pipeline stage and close timing at 50 MHz in at most 1455 LUTs. An optimised multi-core CPU remains faster on stored images, but it cannot begin until the frame is complete.

papers.title: JIT-MPE: Just-in-Time Multi-Pitch Estimation under Output Deadlines
papers.summary: Live pitch displays, score followers and accompaniment systems must know which pitches are sounding within tens of milliseconds, but instrument-agnostic multi-pitch estimation (MPE) has mainly been designed and evaluated offline. We present JIT-MPE, a causal MPE model of 86k parameters for mixed ensembles. It gives an immediate estimate of each 20 ms frame and re-estimates the same frame as 20, 40, 80 and 160 ms of further audio arrive, so that a live display can show pitches at once and then refine them. We score each output only at a deadline by which it can be computed from the audio that has arrived, on five development sets and four held-out sets evaluated only after all design choices were frozen. At a 50 ms deadline, which reads the update made with 40 ms of lookahead, JIT-MPE is significantly more accurate than five of six published offline MPE systems in 38 of 45 comparisons (15 of 20 on the held-out sets) and less accurate in only two, although these systems read the whole recording and all but one have 6 to 170 times as many parameters; the sixth, supervised on URMP, is higher on four of the nine sets. The deadline costs little: on the held-out sets, JIT-MPE at 50 ms is within $-1.27$ to $+0.60$ points of recording-level macro F1 of its own final output with 160 ms of lookahead and within $-2.08$ to $+0.79$ points of a bidirectional model of similar size. Waiting pays off where the immediate estimate is weakest: the update at 50 ms adds 1.7-3.6 points over it on the development data and three of the four held-out sets, and raises the recall of reference frames in the first 20 ms after a note onset from 9.8% to 38.4% on the held-out AAM set. The slowest measured frame takes at most 4.15 ms on one CPU thread. Code and trained weights are available at https://github.com/Frieve-A/jit-mpe.

papers.title: How AI Load Swings Reduce Datacenter Power Conversion Efficiency
papers.summary: AI training and inference workloads make GPU power swing repeatedly between compute and communication phases. As a result, the cascaded converters in a datacenter rack keep moving between operating points with different efficiencies. This paper uses an energy based, cycle averaged method to quantify that effect along a 240 V AC to 400 V DC to 51 V DC rack power path, using measured efficiency curves of commercially available GaN based PFC and LLC converters. For a 1 Hz, 50% duty-cycle load swinging between 5 kW and 510 W, conversion efficiency falls to 95.97%, compared with 96.82% at the equivalent constant average load, a loss of 0.88%. When 51/48V to 1V point of load conversion to the chip rail is included, it is shown that the loss grows to 1.66% (89.45% vs. 90.96%). These results show that efficiency rated at average load overstates real world performance, and that the penalty grows with each load dependent conversion stage between the grid and the GPU.

papers.title: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
papers.summary: Deploying humanoid task policies requires reliable runtime monitors that anticipate unrecoverable falls in time to trigger a fallback. We formulate this task as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy. Synthesizing this monitor is challenging: existing methods assume training data naturally covers the recoverability envelope, yet acquiring such data remains a major bottleneck for contact-rich systems. Consequently, they recover only a fraction of the true envelope, leaving them prone to optimistic hallucinations for out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We resolve this via a unified framework that iterates between value learning and active exploration. Data exploration is reframed as a reach-avoid problem, where an uncertainty-guided explorer systematically uncovers unseen states while avoiding confidently unrecoverable regions. This loop is further supported by a combined Temporal Difference and Monte Carlo objective for accurate in-distribution value prediction and reliable uncertainty estimation. By explicitly treating the remaining high-uncertainty regions as unrecoverable, the monitor mitigates optimistic OOD hallucinations. Evaluated on stochastic benchmarks and a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid, our approach drastically improves monitor coverage and accuracy and successfully transfers zero-shot to real-world hardware.

papers.title: From Caveman to COBA: Coordinated Optimization-Based Attacks on Grid-Edge Smart Inverters in DER-Rich Power Systems
papers.summary: Aggregation platforms and smart-inverter control channels can allow a compromised coordination layer to alter active- and reactive-power commands across a geographically distributed DER fleet. This paper introduces the Coordinated Optimization-Based Attack (COBA), which uses network information and location-specific DER P/Q setpoints to maximize thermal loading on a selected transmission corridor. COBA is compared with low-information CAV baselines limited to a single uniform fleet command: all-off, all-on, maximum reactive absorption, or maximum reactive injection. The Hawaii Synthetic Grid-37 Buses case is evaluated with rooftop-photovoltaic-like capability aggregated at 20 selected 69-kV buses and verified using MATPOWER power flow. Under the case's single-reference-bus balancing convention, COBA overloads B86 (WAIALUA69-WAIANAE69) near 30% penetration and B51 (COCONUT69-PALM69) near 55%, while same-target uniform loadings remain lower and uniform commands primarily stress other natural weak lines. The results show that topology, target selection, and command capability determine DER-induced thermal risk beyond aggregate penetration alone.

papers.title: Performance Gaps Between Open-Loop, Certainty-Equivalent, and Optimal Control Under Action-Dependent Observations
papers.summary: In dynamical systems, feedback can improve performance by allowing decisions to depend on past observations, rather than being designed a priori. Under full observation, the current state is sufficient for decision-making; under partial observation, the controller must instead estimate the state from measurements. When actions also affect observations, control can have a dual role: actions influence both the state and the information available for future decisions. This interaction can invalidate certainty-equivalent (CE) control, a widely used strategy that applies state feedback policies as if the estimated state were the true state. We ask when this suboptimality leads to a quantitative performance gap that grows with the horizon. We study this question in a linear-quadratic system with bilinear observations by comparing the optimal policy, certainty-equivalent control, and the optimal open-loop (OL) policy. We identify an instance-dependent information-strength parameter $q$ and establish distinct performance regimes as $q$ varies. When $q$ is sufficiently small, we show that no policy can improve over OL control by more than $O(1)$ cumulative cost. For large values of $q$, we find that CE achieves an $\Omega(T)$ advantage over OL control. Our main finding is that for intermediate values of $q$, we can construct a policy that occasionally probes for information and achieves an $\Omega(T)$ advantage over OL control while CE only achieves an $O(1)$ advantage, establishing an $\Omega(T)$ gap between CE and optimal control. Our analysis relies on a regret decomposition that captures the tradeoff between the immediate cost of gathering information and its future benefit.

papers.title: Joint End-to-End Training of Weighted BP Decoder Ensembles
papers.summary: Ensemble decoding improves decoding reliability by combining component decoders with complementary failure events. Existing approaches typically obtain this diversity from code-specific structure, such as code automorphisms, multiple parity-check representations, or targeted modifications of the message-passing graph. In this work, we instead learn the diversity of an ensemble of weighted belief propagation decoders by jointly optimizing trainable Tanner-graph edge weights. A central design question is how the training objective should distribute gradient among the ensemble members to promote complementary decoding behavior. To this end, we compare four ensemble objectives under direct gradient-based optimization and identify best-member training as the most effective approach. For a (64,32) progressive edge-growth (PEG) low-density parity-check (LDPC) code, the resulting ensemble outperforms the considered trained and untrained belief-propagation-based ensemble baselines. With 10 members, it provides a gain of approximately 0.66 dB over a single belief propagation decoder at a target frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-4}$. Similar behavior is observed for a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, indicating that the learned complementarity is not specific to PEG. Although the ensemble performance improves substantially, all trained members show a higher standalone FER. The gain therefore results from learned specialization and complementary failure events rather than uniformly improved component decoders.
